title: Shared-lib extraction (Python-only) — phased tracking issue
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§3). Per `docs/specs/2026-06-15-shared-lib-architecture.md` (its `lib/ts`/contracts part is SUPERSEDED — the ecosystem is **Python-only**, `agent-tools/lib` is a plain Python library).

## What
Extract the duplicated cross-tool logic into `agent-tools/lib/<module>` and migrate each tool to import from it. **Phased, lowest-churn first** — each phase is its own PR.

## Phased order (do in this sequence)
1. **`advertise`** (install-skill — 4 copies today). First extraction, stands up the lib skeleton.
2. **`hooks`** (`agents-hooks/v1` dispatcher; tg vendored it — de-dupe).
3. **`providers`** (the biggest asset: board, failover, transports, `oc:` routing, key cascade, **capability tags incl. vision-filter for `--visual`**, **model-currency manifest**). Consumed by review, task-cli classifier, research-cli.
4. **`config`** (cascade + env precedence + `~/.config` paths).
5. **`registry` + trust-kernel** (hook-trust + visual-module-registry trust algorithm, one place).
6. **`retry`** (net-new), **`tmux-inject`** (extract from tg-ctl), **`daemon-supervisor`** (survives kills — shared by task-cli + tg-ctl), **`Gantt-render`**, `agenttools_log` (exists).

## Why
Four copies of install-skill, a vendored hooks dispatcher, the provider board reimplemented per tool — this is the recurring-churn tax. One library = a new tool spins up fast on one architecture.

## Acceptance
- `agent-tools/lib` exists as a plain Python package; phase 1 (`advertise`) lands first and at least one tool imports it.
- Each subsequent phase migrates its consumers and removes the duplicate.
- No `lib/ts`, no cross-language contracts (Python-only).

Track sub-PRs as checkboxes against this issue.

title: research-cli — new Python CLI on the shared providers panel engine
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§6). **Depends on shared-lib `providers` extraction** (phase 3 of the shared-lib tracking issue).

## What
A separate Python CLI — `research-cli` — built on the shared lib's panel engine. It reuses the `providers` module **verbatim** (board, failover, transports, key cascade, capability tags). It is NOT a review-cli mode.

## Why
Research is a distinct surface from code review; bolting it onto review as a mode would conflate two products. But it needs the exact same multi-model provider plumbing, which is why it waits on the `providers` extraction.

## Acceptance
- New repo/tool `research-cli` (Python) imports `agent-tools/lib` providers, no fork.
- Provides a research/panel command distinct from review's modes.
- Add it to the ecosystem catalog once it stands up.

(Filed in agent-tools as the umbrella; spin out a dedicated repo when work starts.)

title: Harvest skills from rollout reports + strict-ticket-discipline
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§8). One centralized pass over the wave-1/wave-2 rollout harvest reports.

## What
Promote recurring, generalizable lessons into agent-tools skills:

- **worktree-via-project-CLI** — dependency provisioning via the project's own CLI (distinct from the worktree-base-trap skill).
- **subagent-delegation contract** — the contract for dispatching/owning subagent work.
- **"diagnostic image ≠ proof"** — an acceptance bar: a diagnostic screenshot is not the same as a proof-of-behavior screenshot.
- **queued-report durability** — channel-unavailable → don't fake delivery; queue and surface the failure.
- **strict-ticket-discipline** skill + a **require-ticket-before-commit** guard (coordinate with task-cli integrations issue).

(Sources: 3d-cli AGENTS.md and the rollout reports.)

## Why
These lessons are currently scattered in per-repo AGENTS files. Promoting them to self-advertising skills is exactly the slim-AGENTS strategy (generic rules live in skills, repos keep only specifics).

## Acceptance
- Each candidate is either a new skill under agent-tools (with `<!-- skill:X -->` advertising) or explicitly rejected with a reason.
- `strict-ticket-discipline` + `require-ticket-before-commit` exist (pairs with task-cli integrations).
- The harvested skills install via rig globally.

title: Slim ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md to PERSONAL-ONLY (move tool/process docs into skills)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9, ref #3704). **Careful pass — it's the global config.**

## What
Reduce `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to **personal-only** content: identity ("address me as Alex"), preferences, dictionary, Telegram report style. ALL universal tool + process docs (how to use `review`/`tg`/`draw`, the no-short-timeout rule, etc.) must **self-advertise via SKILLS**, not be hand-written in CLAUDE.md.

Concrete first cut: the hand-written **"## Review and sanity checks"** section duplicates the `review` skill → remove it. Audit the rest the same way (many already have skills + `<!-- skill:X -->` blurbs as the self-advertising mechanism).

## Why
Hand-written tool docs in the global config drift from the tools and duplicate the skills. The earlier in-place "migrate CLAUDE.md review docs to subcommands" edit was wrong — those docs should not live in CLAUDE.md at all.

## Acceptance
- "## Review and sanity checks" removed (covered by the `review` skill blurb).
- Every other section audited: if a skill advertises it, remove the hand-written copy; if not, either create the skill or keep it (only if genuinely personal).
- Final CLAUDE.md is personal-only; tool/process knowledge is reachable via skills.
- Done as a careful, reviewed pass (it is the live global config).

title: agent-hooks don't actually FIRE in Claude Code — need an agents-hooks/v1 → CC bridge runner (+ rig installs it)
body:
**Confirmed gap (same class as the skill-loading bug rig-cli#9).** The agent-tools agent-hooks speak the `agents-hooks/v1` contract (JSON descriptor in ~/.claude/hooks/, stdin JSON, exit 10 = block). Claude Code runs hooks from `settings.json` (PreToolUse/PostToolUse, matcher + `command`) — a DIFFERENT format. There is NO dispatcher in settings.json that reads the ~/.claude/hooks/*.json descriptors and runs them. So **every agent-tools agent-hook is INERT in Claude Code** — block-no-verify, **block-raw-pr-merge** (the gh-ship guard), block-secrets-write, enforce-timeout-on-bash, stop-completion-selfcheck, **format-on-write** (PR #17) — they sit as files that nothing invokes. The 'safe because the guards intercept' pillar is currently FALSE in CC.

**Fix:** a small **bridge runner** (`agents-hooks/v1` → harness): a script wired into CC's settings.json (PreToolUse/PostToolUse, per matched tool) that discovers the matching ~/.claude/hooks/*.json descriptors for the point/tool, runs each (stdin event JSON), and maps exit-10 → CC's block + the protocol `decision`/`message` → CC's deny output. rig must install this bridge into settings.json on `rig apply` (harness-keyed, like the skill symlinks rig-cli#9 and auto-mode). Then verify (clean-room e2e, rig-cli#10) that a guard actually blocks in CC.

**Until this lands, do NOT claim any agent-hook 'works' in Claude Code.** Other harnesses (codex/oc/pi) may have their own hook mechanisms — same per-harness wiring question.

comments.body: Done: the agents-hooks/v1 → Claude Code bridge is merged (PR #20, d4ff40f), wired into ~/.claude/settings.json via `rig apply` (3 dispatcher hooks), and live-proven on the machine (blockable cmd → permissionDecision: deny, benign → allow). Auto-mode guards now fire. Follow-up advisory-message surfacing tracked in #39.

title: Third-party skill/tool ecosystem: enable · harmonize · delineate (research)
body:
## Problem (CTO, tg#3754)
Parse a month of hyper sessions and **most installed third-party skills/tools were never invoked.** Same root cause as the skill-loading (#11) and hook-firing (#18) gaps: *installed ≠ discovered ≠ applied.* We've accreted overlapping tool systems with no routing doctrine → agents default to grep/Read and ignore the specialized tools, or burn tokens choosing between redundant ones.

## Full inventory to triage (third-party / external — NOT our own ecosystem)
**MCP servers:**
- **Haft** (h-reason) — structured reasoning / decision artifacts / FPF. Heavy ceremony. Overlaps superpowers brainstorming + h-reason skill dir.
- **superpowers** — skill-discovery framework + workflow skills (brainstorming, debugging, TDD…). Self-asserts at SessionStart.
- **sverklo** — multi-repo code intelligence (semantic search, concepts/clusters, memories, impact/deps, review-diff). Overlaps serena + grep + semantic-code-search skill.
- **serena** — LSP-backed semantic code (symbol find/edit, refs, onboarding, project memories). Overlaps sverklo + grep.
- **context7** — live library/framework docs. Overlaps WebFetch + agent-browser.
- **computer-use** — desktop control.
- **claude-in-chrome** — browser automation. Overlaps computer-use browser tier + agent-browser.

**CLI-backed external skills:** **agent-browser** (web→markdown; replaces WebFetch for long pages). Overlaps context7 + WebFetch + claude-in-chrome.

**Hand-authored skill dirs:** h-reason, debate-swarm, moshi-best-practices.

*(Boundary, not the subject: our own — tg, review, draw, 3d, rig, task-cli, rtk, linear + 50 agent-tools rule-skills. Delineate the third-party tools AGAINST these.)*

## Three axes
1. **Enable** — is each actually installed + discoverable in EVERY supported harness? (Likely many configured-but-inert or cc-only — same failure class as #11/#18.)
2. **Harmonize** — compose, don't collide: Haft-vs-superpowers reasoning; serena-vs-sverklo memories (+ agent-tools MEMORY.md = three stores); two think-before-build frameworks; agent-browser-vs-context7-vs-WebFetch.
3. **Delineate** — a written routing doctrine / decision table: code search → serena (symbol) | sverklo (cross-repo concept) | grep (literal); docs → context7 (libs) | agent-browser (web); reasoning → Haft (irreversible) | superpowers brainstorming (divergence).

## Evidence step (the killer)
Parse ~1 month of hyper transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/**/**.jsonl`), count tool/skill invocations by name, surface never-fired + rarely-fired. Output = routing-doctrine doc + concrete enable/prune/route actions (likely a rig provisioning concern + a routing skill).

Related: #11 (skill-loading, merged), #18 (hook-firing bridge).

comments.body:
## Evidence (the killer step) — DONE, real data

Parsed **204 hyper sessions** (last 30d, 13 project dirs: main checkout + worktrees + ralphex tmp). Streaming tool_use extraction. Confirms the hypothesis hard:

| third-party tool | sessions | % of 204 | calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| agent-browser (CLI) | 5 | 2.5% | 50 |
| haft (mcp) | 2 | 1.0% | 18 |
| context7 (mcp) | 2 | 1.0% | 4 |
| computer-use (mcp) | 2 | 1.0% | 12 |
| sverklo (mcp) | 1 | 0.5% | 4 |
| **serena (mcp)** | **0** | **0%** | **0** |
| **claude-in-chrome (mcp)** | **0** | **0%** | **0** |

**Only 9 of 204 sessions (4.4%) invoked ANY third-party tool.** serena and claude-in-chrome: literal zero despite being configured MCP servers.

Baseline for contrast: Bash **16727**, Read 3192, Edit 1827, Agent 639, Grep 114. Agents do ~everything via Bash+Read+Edit and almost never reach for the semantic/code-intelligence tools.

**Skill-tool invocations (the exception that works):** 55 calls, 20 distinct — superpowers:brainstorming ×7, systematic-debugging ×5, using-superpowers ×4, dispatching-parallel-agents ×3, ext ×9, commit ×8, h-reason ×1. So the *self-advertising* skill mechanism IS adopted; the *deferred-tool* MCP mechanism is not.

### Likely root cause (enablement, not preference)
serena / sverklo / haft / context7 / computer-use are all **deferred tools** — they don't appear in the base tool list; the agent must run a ToolSearch to load a schema before it can call them. That friction ≈ explains the ~0% adoption: the agent reaches for the zero-friction Bash+Read+grep path instead. superpowers, which auto-asserts at SessionStart, is the one third-party system with real adoption. → **'enable' axis is the lever**: a deferred tool nobody searches for is functionally uninstalled.

Audit script: `/tmp/tool_usage_audit.py` (read-only, streaming). Denominator note: 170 of those files are the main checkout; ~99 are short/no-tool sessions, so adoption among *tool-using* sessions is a bit higher but still single digits for everything except agent-browser.

title: OSS license-policy gate (fill the dependency-review license gap)
body:
From the GHAS-parity check (tg#3777/#3779). Dropping GHAS `dependency-review-action` keeps vuln coverage (scripted `dep-audit.sh` audits the whole tree, equal-or-better) but LOSES the one thing it did that the audit doesn't: **license-policy enforcement** (allow/deny license lists, e.g. block AGPL/GPL).

Fill with an OSS license checker, provisioned by rig as a CI gate + (optionally) a pre-commit guard:
- JS/TS: `license-checker` / `license-checker-rseidelsohn` or `@onebeyond/license-checker-config`.
- Rust: `cargo-deny` (licenses).
- Python: `pip-licenses`.
- Multi-eco: `syft` SBOM → license policy, or `osv-scanner` (vulns only, no license — so not this).

Gate: fail on a denied license in the dependency tree. Knobs: allow-list vs deny-list, default deny copyleft (AGPL/GPL) matching the old dependency-review template. Lives in agent-tools `ci/license-policy/` + rig provisions it. Related: #19 (tool triage), the dropped GHAS dependency-review.

title: Self-hosted security findings dashboard (copy GitHub code-scanning UI, improve it)
body:
From the GHAS-parity check (tg#3780). What GHAS uniquely gives that we don't replicate = the **hosted code-scanning / security dashboard** (findings list, dedup, triage state, trend over time, PR-inline annotations). CTO: copy GitHub's code-scanning UI and improve it.

Idea: aggregate the OSS scanners' output (CodeQL-CLI SARIF, Semgrep SARIF, gitleaks JSON, dep-audit JSON) into one self-hosted dashboard — findings table, per-rule grouping, severity, suppression/triage state, history. Tailscale-served like the existing review-cli dashboard.

Likely home: **extend review-cli's dashboard** (already has SSE + Tailscale `--host`) rather than a new tool — it's already our findings-surfacing UI. SARIF is the common input format (CodeQL + Semgrep emit it natively; wrap gitleaks/dep-audit into SARIF). Improvements over GitHub: cross-repo view, our own triage rules, link to the suppressing `// codeql[...]` line. Related: review-cli dashboard, #19.

title: Add a Trivy (filesystem/dep vuln) CI gate to agent-tools + rig-provision it
body:
Surfaced wrapping the hyper rollout (tg#3787). hyper's bespoke `security-scan.yml` runs three scanners — Semgrep (covered by agent-tools `ci/sast/`), bun audit (covered by `ci/dependency-review/dep-audit.sh`, #23), and **Trivy** (vuln/misconfig/fs scanner) which has **NO agent-tools equivalent**.

Per the 'common gates live in agent-tools, not per-repo' principle, removing hyper's bespoke workflow would silently drop Trivy coverage. Fix: add a `ci/trivy/` gate (Trivy fs scan — OSS, no license) to agent-tools + rig-provision it, so the rollout that drops per-repo security-scan keeps full coverage. Alternatively decide Trivy is redundant with dep-audit+semgrep and document why. Related: #23 (de-GHAS gates), the hyper-rollout delegation in ROADMAP.

title: bridge: surface advisory (exit-0) v1 hook messages as CC additionalContext
body:
Follow-up from the #20 review (codex P2).

Today an advisory v1 hook (`on_error: open`) that exits 0 with a JSON `message` has that message **discarded** by the bridge dispatcher — `_run_hook` returns `("allow", "")` and `dispatch()` emits nothing. This matches the documented design (README: advisory hooks "stay out of the way"), so it is not a regression, but the guidance an advisory hook wants to give the agent (e.g. `enforce-timeout-on-bash`, `block-raw-process-env` in default mode) never surfaces.

**Enhancement:** parse the exit-0 v1 `message`, collect messages across all non-blocking hooks, and — when nothing blocked — emit a CC PreToolUse `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (and a `systemMessage` for `Stop`) carrying the advisory text, WITHOUT a `permissionDecision` (must not force-approve the tool; the tool proceeds through CC's normal permission flow).

**Why it's a separate PR, not part of #20:** it needs careful CC output-schema work (the repo uses neither `additionalContext` nor `systemMessage` today) and its own tests for the "allow + context, not allow + auto-approve" distinction. #20 lands the security-relevant fixes (timeout/non-UTF-8 hardening + NotebookEdit path normalization) now.

title: orchestrator-stays-thin over-blocks fully read-only shell pipes (3+ segments)
body:
## What's wrong

`_is_implementation_bash` in `agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py` over-blocks ONE legitimate class: a **fully read-only** shell pipe of 3+ commands.

The read-only carve-out (`READ_ONLY_BASH`) only protects an UNCHAINED single command:

```python
chained = bool(CHAIN.search(command))
if not chained and READ_ONLY_BASH.search(command):
    return False  # single inspection one-liner -> never block
if HEREDOC.search(command) or BUILD_EDIT.search(command):
    return True
return len(CHAIN.findall(command)) >= 2   # <-- trips here for read-only pipes
```

So a pipe where **every** segment is read-only inspection (e.g. `find ... | grep ... | head`, `tail X | grep Y | wc -l`) trips the `len(CHAIN.findall()) >= 2` implementation-shape rule on the WARN-then-BLOCK tier, even though nothing is being implemented.

### Repro (confirmed)

```
'find . -name foo | grep bar | head' -> is_implementation = True
'tail -100 log | grep err | wc -l'   -> is_implementation = True
'find . | grep x | head -5'          -> is_implementation = True
```

Found in a live session: the hook blocked a legitimate `find|grep|head` inspection command.

## User-facing consequence

The orchestrator can't run multi-stage read-only inspection (the bread-and-butter of planning/verifying) without hitting the delegate-to-subagent block on the repeat. That is exactly the inspection the orchestrator is SUPPOSED to do inline.

## Fix

In `_is_implementation_bash`: if EVERY chain segment matches `READ_ONLY_BASH` and NONE matches `BUILD_EDIT` or `HEREDOC`, return `False` (not implementation) regardless of chain count. A read-only pipe of any length is never blocked; a pipe that includes any build/edit/heredoc segment still blocks.

## Acceptance criteria

- A 3-segment read-only pipe (`find ... | grep ... | head`) is ALLOWED (never warns, never blocks on repeat).
- A read-only pipe with one `sed -i` / `npm install` / heredoc segment is STILL BLOCKED on repeat.
- Existing single-command and 3+-impl-chain block behavior unchanged (heredocs, sed -i/tee, build/install runners, mixed read-only+impl pipes all still block).
- Full `tests/` suite green.

title: Codify the orchestrator-only / all-work-in-swarms doctrine in AGENTS.md
body:
The CTO made a standing rule (2026-06-22): "Ты только оркестрируешь. Вся работа в роях субагентов." (You only orchestrate; all work runs in subagent swarms.)

Codify it as a crisp, prominent doctrine section in AGENTS.md, in English (the file is English-only).

The doctrine must state:
- The main/orchestrator agent ONLY orchestrates: PLAN, DISPATCH to subagents/workflows, VERIFY. It does NOT implement inline.
- ALL implementation work (fixes, features, builds, investigations, migrations) runs in subagent swarms (the Agent tool / a Workflow), never in the main thread.
- Fan out broadly and in PARALLEL, grouped by repo (one shipping agent per repo at a time) to avoid worktree/ship collisions; parallel across repos.
- Each dispatched agent carries the full discipline: ticket -> fresh worktree -> tests -> review-gate ([ok]) -> gh ship.
- The orchestrator VERIFIES every "done" (PR merged + CI green; never trust a subagent's "all green" on its own word) and only marks a roadmap item done after it is verified AND the CTO has approved it's OK.
- Enforced mechanically by the existing `orchestrator-stays-thin` agent-hook (blocks the main agent's implementation-shaped Bash/Edit/Write; subagents exempt). The hook is the mechanism; the section is the intent.

Link to the existing 'Agent-hooks' section for the hook mechanics rather than duplicating them.

title: research-cli: adopt shared agenttools_errors (what/why/how-to-fix + structured exit codes)
body:
## What

`research-cli` (`tools/research-cli/`) hand-rolls its error reporting: every failure is a bare
`print(f"research <cmd>: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)` plus an ad-hoc per-command exit code
(`2`/`69`/`70`). None of these messages follow the ecosystem's **error-system v2** shape — a
three-part **what / why / how-to-fix** block with a stable, per-class exit code — even though the
shared `agenttools_errors` module already implements exactly that and is already importable from
research-cli (its `providers.py` puts `lib/` on `sys.path`, the same shim the providers CORE uses).

Concretely today:

- `research ask` with no reachable seat prints a one-line "no seat answered — set a provider key…"
  and exits `69`. A bad/unresolvable manifest prints `research ask: <ProviderError>` and exits `70`.
- `research board` prints `research board: <ProviderError>` and exits `70`.
- `cli.py` prints `research: unknown command 'x'` (exit `2`) and `research: cannot load command…`
  (exit `70`) as bare strings.

These give the symptom but never the **why** or the **how-to-fix**, so an agent or a human can't act
on them without reading the source.

## Acceptance criteria

1. research-cli's user-facing errors are raised as `agenttools_errors` structured errors (or rendered
   through the same what/why/how formatter), so each failure prints **what** happened, **why**, and a
   concrete **how-to-fix** line.
2. The `unknown command` path (`cli.py`) uses the shared `unknown_item_error` builder so it gets the
   **did-you-mean** heuristic against the discovered command list instead of a bare string.
3. Exit codes stay a documented, stable contract. Where the lib's class maps cleanly
   (usage→`EXIT_USAGE=2`, network/unreachable, internal), adopt it; any deliberately-kept research
   code (the `EX_UNAVAILABLE`/`EX_SOFTWARE` convention) is documented in the command docstring with
   the mapping rationale.
4. RED-first regression tests assert the rendered message contains the fix hint and the right exit
   code per failure class (unknown command + did-you-mean, empty question, unreachable board,
   malformed manifest).
5. Full repo suite green (`uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml python -m pytest tests/ -q`); `ruff`
   clean on changed files. No new runtime dependency (the lib is stdlib-only).

## Notes

This is the roadmap's error-system v2 ("one shared `errors` … consumed by review/rig/tg/draw/3d/task")
applied to one bounded, in-repo slice — proving the shared layer composes with a tool that doesn't yet
use it. `agenttools_errors` is already adopted by rig; research-cli is the next clean adopter.

title: model-freshness checker: adopt shared agenttools_errors (what/why/how + structured exit codes)
body:
The `model-freshness` CLI (`lib/checker/model_freshness.py`, the daily model-currency checker, run as a cron per ROADMAP §4) hand-rolls its error reporting — exactly the pattern PR #85 fixed for research-cli (issue #84):

- a bad/unreadable/malformed manifest is reported as a bare `print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)` + an ad-hoc `return 2`;
- a failing `--validate` prints `manifest INVALID:` + a bullet list and `return 1`;

none follow the ecosystem's **error-system v2** shape — the three-part WHAT / WHY / HOW-to-fix block with a **stable per-class exit code** — even though `lib/agenttools_errors` already implements exactly that and is already importable here (the same `lib/` `sys.path` shim `providers.py` / research-cli's `_errors.py` use).

### Scope (bounded, decision-free — mirrors #85)
- New `lib/checker/_errors.py` shim: the ONE import point, re-exporting the shared error classes/builders + the exit-code constants the checker returns (stdlib-only, so `--validate`/`--help` stay fast and offline).
- `main()`: a manifest load failure raises a structured `UsageError` (`EXIT_USAGE=2`); a failing `--validate` raises a `UsageError` whose WHY lists the problems and whose FIX points at the manifest; both render through `guard`.
- Exit-code contract migrated to the shared codes: bad/malformed manifest **and** invalid `--validate` are now `EXIT_USAGE=2` (the `--validate` failure was the ad-hoc `1`; a malformed config is the usage class per the `structured-exit-codes` skill). Documented in the README + the command docstring.
- RED-first regression tests assert the rendered block contains the fix hint and the right exit code per failure class.

No new runtime dependency (the lib is stdlib-only). No behavior change beyond the error shape + the `--validate`-failure exit code (1→2, aligning it with the malformed-manifest class).

title: research-cli test test_ask_no_seat_answered_is_network_class_with_fix is red in the yaml-less CI gate (exit 2 not 7)
body:
Found while shipping #86 (model-freshness error-layer adoption). Pre-existing on origin/main, NOT introduced by that PR.

`tests/test_research_cli_errors.py::test_ask_no_seat_answered_is_network_class_with_fix` asserts `ask` returns `EXIT_NETWORK=7` when no seat is reachable. But the `ask` path loads the providers manifest (`lib/contracts/models.yaml`) which needs PyYAML; with no yaml installed the manifest load fails FIRST and the command returns `EXIT_USAGE=2`, so the test gets `assert 2 == 7`.

Reproduce (the dependency-free gate's exact shape):
```
uv run --with 'pytest>=8,<9' pytest tests/test_research_cli_errors.py::test_ask_no_seat_answered_is_network_class_with_fix -q
# -> assert 2 == 7
```

It currently passes in the LIVE `tests` CI gate only because that runner happens to have PyYAML resolvable; the test has a hidden yaml dependency it doesn't declare. Fix: either give the test the same `importorskip('yaml')` guard the sibling `test_model_freshness.py` uses, or make the no-seat path independent of a loadable manifest (so the NETWORK class is reached before the manifest is parsed). Low priority — it's a test-environment-coupling bug, not a runtime bug.

title: model-freshness checker: adopt shared agenttools_errors (structured WHAT/WHY/HOW + stable exit codes)
body:
## Problem

`lib/checker/model_freshness.py` is an in-repo CLI (the model-currency cron checker, runnable by hand as `python3 lib/checker/model_freshness.py`). Its `main()` still hand-rolls error handling the way research-cli did **before** #85:

```python
except ManifestError as exc:
    print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2
...
if problems:               # --validate failure
    print("manifest INVALID:", file=sys.stderr)
    ...
    return 1
```

Two concrete defects:

1. **Bare, unstructured error strings** — `error: {exc}` gives the symptom but no WHY / HOW-to-fix, unlike every other ecosystem CLI now that the shared `agenttools_errors` layer exists (error-system v2). #85 adopted it for research-cli; this is the same fix for the checker.
2. **Wrong exit code for an invalid manifest** — `--validate` failure returns `1`, but the public exit-code contract reserves `1` (`EXIT_INTERNAL`) for *unexpected internal bugs / tracebacks*. A malformed or invariant-violating manifest is a **config/usage** error → must be `EXIT_USAGE`/`EXIT_CONFIG` (`2`), so a calling script (the cron) can branch on "the config is bad" vs "the tool crashed". The load-failure path already returns `2` — the two manifest-failure paths are inconsistent.
3. The `PyYAML not installed` case is collapsed into `ManifestError` → exit 2, but it is genuinely a **missing-dependency** failure (`EXIT_MISSING_DEP` = 127) with an install hint — the exact class `agenttools_errors` models.

## Fix (bounded, decision-free)

Adopt `agenttools_errors` in `main()`:
- Render manifest-load / invalid-manifest failures as the 3-part structured block via `guard()`, mapping to `ConfigError` (exit 2).
- Route the missing-PyYAML case to `MissingDepError` (exit 127 + install command).
- Keep the success paths and `--json` output byte-identical.

## Acceptance criteria

- `main()` exit codes: invalid manifest -> 2 (not 1); unreadable/malformed manifest -> 2; missing PyYAML -> 127.
- Error output is the structured `error:/why:/fix:` block on stderr.
- New RED-first tests cover the `main()` exit codes + structured rendering (currently `main()` has zero test coverage).
- Full repo pytest suite green; ruff clean on changed files.
- README exit-code note added (help-docs-sync).

title: research-cli: machine-readable JSON output for `research ask` (--json)
body:
## What is missing

`research ask` emits ONLY a human-readable Markdown note to stdout. The panel pass already produces a fully-structured `ResearchResult` (every `SeatAnswer` carries seat/model_id/provider/ok/text/error), but that structure is collapsed into a Markdown string and discarded. There is currently NO way to get the per-seat answers as data.

## User-facing consequence

A research tool whose output can't be piped/parsed forces every downstream consumer (the phased multi-round and model-driven-synthesis follow-ups in the README, plus any caller scripting a panel pass) to scrape Markdown — brittle and lossy. Every other ecosystem CLI is scriptable; research-cli's core command is not.

## Scope (bounded, decision-free)

Add a `--json` flag to `research ask` that prints the run as a stable JSON object instead of the Markdown note:

```json
{
  "question": "...",
  "answered": <int>,
  "failed": <int>,
  "seats": [
    {"display": "Analyst", "lens": "analyst", "model": "claude-opus-4-8",
     "provider": "anthropic", "ok": true, "text": "...", "error": ""}
  ]
}
```

- Markdown remains the default (no behavior change without the flag).
- The same structured-exit-code contract applies: `--json` with no seat answered still exits `7` (EXIT_NETWORK), the JSON is still printed first (a script gets the data AND the exit class).
- No transport rework, no research-flow design, no new dependency (stdlib `json`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `research ask --json --offline "q"` prints valid JSON with one `seats` entry per board seat, each carrying ok/text/provider/model/lens/display.
- `--json` + no-seat-answered still exits 7 and prints a JSON object (answered=0).
- Default (no `--json`) output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- New deterministic tests (StubTransport, RED-first); full repo suite green; ruff clean.

Part of ROADMAP §6 phased follow-ups (scriptability groundwork for multi-round / model-driven synthesis). Tracking parent: #13.

title: test(cli): Docker harness — real-agent proof that task-cli is advertised AND enforced, wired into CI test-cli
body:
## What

`research-cli` (`tools/research-cli/`) hand-rolls its error reporting: every failure is a bare
`print(f"research <cmd>: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)` plus an ad-hoc per-command exit code
(`2`/`69`/`70`). None of these messages follow the ecosystem's **error-system v2** shape — a
three-part **what / why / how-to-fix** block with a stable, per-class exit code — even though the
shared `agenttools_errors` module already implements exactly that and is already importable from
research-cli (its `providers.py` puts `lib/` on `sys.path`, the same shim the providers CORE uses).

Concretely today:

- `research ask` with no reachable seat prints a one-line "no seat answered — set a provider key…"
  and exits `69`. A bad/unresolvable manifest prints `research ask: <ProviderError>` and exits `70`.
- `research board` prints `research board: <ProviderError>` and exits `70`.
- `cli.py` prints `research: unknown command 'x'` (exit `2`) and `research: cannot load command…`
  (exit `70`) as bare strings.

These give the symptom but never the **why** or the **how-to-fix**, so an agent or a human can't act
on them without reading the source.

## Acceptance criteria

1. research-cli's user-facing errors are raised as `agenttools_errors` structured errors (or rendered
   through the same what/why/how formatter), so each failure prints **what** happened, **why**, and a
   concrete **how-to-fix** line.
2. The `unknown command` path (`cli.py`) uses the shared `unknown_item_error` builder so it gets the
   **did-you-mean** heuristic against the discovered command list instead of a bare string.
3. Exit codes stay a documented, stable contract. Where the lib's class maps cleanly
   (usage→`EXIT_USAGE=2`, network/unreachable, internal), adopt it; any deliberately-kept research
   code (the `EX_UNAVAILABLE`/`EX_SOFTWARE` convention) is documented in the command docstring with
   the mapping rationale.
4. RED-first regression tests assert the rendered message contains the fix hint and the right exit
   code per failure class (unknown command + did-you-mean, empty question, unreachable board,
   malformed manifest).
5. Full repo suite green (`uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml python -m pytest tests/ -q`); `ruff`
   clean on changed files. No new runtime dependency (the lib is stdlib-only).

## Notes

This is the roadmap's error-system v2 ("one shared `errors` … consumed by review/rig/tg/draw/3d/task")
applied to one bounded, in-repo slice — proving the shared layer composes with a tool that doesn't yet
use it. `agenttools_errors` is already adopted by rig; research-cli is the next clean adopter.

title: require-ticket hook: subcommand detector over-matches read-only inspection commands
body:
## What

In `agent-hooks/require-ticket-before-commit/require_ticket_before_commit.py`, the `GIT_COMMIT` detector matches any command containing the words `git` and `commit` separated by anything. A read-only command like `git log --grep commit` (or `git log --oneline --grep=commit`) matches `GIT_COMMIT`, is not excluded by `SKIP_COMMIT`, carries no ticket/exempt marker, and in strict-default mode therefore returns a hard BLOCK (exit 10) — blocking a completely innocent inspection command.

(Observed live: a `gh issue create` whose BODY merely contained the words "git" and "commit" got blocked by the agent-hook bridge — same root cause, the detector is matching the surrounding command string, not an actual authoring commit.)

## Why / impact

A `git log`/`git show` (or any command) that mentions the word "commit" in a flag/arg/body gets wrongly blocked in strict mode. False-positive blocks erode trust in the gate and can wedge legitimate commands mid-session.

## Repro (the event shape the hook reads)

    echo '{"args":{"command":"git log --grep commit"}}' | ./require_ticket_before_commit.py; echo " exit=$?"
    # observed: decision:block, exit=10  — should be allow (not an authoring commit)

## Suggested fix

Tighten `GIT_COMMIT` so it only matches an actual `git commit` invocation (the `commit` subcommand in argv position), not any command that contains both words. The file already tokenizes argv via `shlex` elsewhere — require `commit` to be the git subcommand token, not a flag value / unrelated word.

## Source

Found while vendoring this hook into the task-cli Docker enforcement harness (task-cli PR feat/harden-agent-leg-and-enforce-assert). Not exercised by that harness (it only feeds real authoring commits), but it is a real false-positive in the canonical hook.

title: Require + enforce version bump on every tool release
body:
## Problem

`rig --version` was a hardcoded `0.1.0` for the whole life of the tool — never bumped across many releases. A hardcoded literal that never moves makes `--version` a useless stale string, not a freshness signal: a user can't tell which build they run or whether a fix landed.

## Fix (this repo — the catalog)

Two durable pieces:

1. **Rule (skill)** `skills/universal/bump-version-on-release/SKILL.md` — every versioned tool MUST bump its declared version (`pyproject.toml` `[project] version` / `package.json` `version`) on every release, and `--version` MUST read that declared version dynamically (never a hardcoded literal that drifts). Semver: patch/minor/major.

2. **Mechanical enforcement in the ship gate** `ci/ship/ship.sh` — before merging, refuse if a PR changes shippable SOURCE (not docs/test/CI) but did NOT bump the repo's version field vs the PR base. Override for a genuine no-release ship: `--no-version-bump-ok <reason>` or `SHIP_SKIP_VERSION_BUMP=1`. Repo-agnostic (auto-detects pyproject/package.json, `SHIP_VERSION_FILES` for non-standard layouts).

## Tests
`tests/test_ship.py` — source-change-without-bump BLOCKED; with-bump PASSES; docs-only NOT required to bump; override (flag + env) works; no-version-file skips.

## Follow-up (other repos — separate tickets)
- rig-cli: `rig --version` literal `0.1.0` → bump + read pyproject dynamically.
- audit tg/review/task/draw/3d for the same hardcoded-literal anti-pattern.

title: require-ticket: -F - (stdin) message is unreadable by a PreToolUse hook, false-blocks ticketed commits
body:
## What's wrong

`require-ticket-before-commit` now reads the commit message from `-F <file>` / `-F<glued>` / `--file=<path>` (landed in #100). But `git commit -F -` puts the message on **git's stdin**, which a PreToolUse agent-hook **cannot read** — the hook's own stdin is the JSON event, not git's. The current code passes the literal `-` to `_read_message_file`, which tries to open a file named `-`, fails, returns `""`, finds no ticket, and **BLOCKS** — even when the streamed message legitimately contains `Closes #N`.

## Evidence (RED)

```
$ echo '{"args":{"command":"git commit -F -"},"cwd":"/tmp/x"}' | python3 require_ticket_before_commit.py
exit: 10  decision: block
stderr: could not read commit-message file /tmp/x/-: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

So a legitimately-ticketed commit piped via `git commit -F -` is false-blocked, and the only escape is `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1` — which bypasses the whole gate.

## User-facing consequence

Subagents that author commits via `-F -` (heredoc/stdin, common in scripted commits) hit a false block and resort to `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1`, so the gate is effectively bypassed for that whole commit form.

## Fix (acceptance criteria)

The gate genuinely cannot see a `-F -` message — so for `-F -` **specifically**, FAIL-OPEN (allow) rather than false-block, and **LOG** that it allowed an unreadable-message commit (a `-F -` bypass surface), so it stays visible. Do NOT fail-open for `-F <file>` (that one is readable and already works).

- `git commit -F -` -> ALLOWED, with a logged note that the message was unreadable.
- `git commit -F<file-with-Closes #1>` / `-F <file>` -> ALLOWED (reads the file) — unchanged.
- `-F <file-with-no-ref>` -> BLOCKED — unchanged.
- `-m "Closes #1"` -> ALLOWED, `-m "no ref"` -> BLOCKED — unchanged.
- editor commit (no -m/-F) -> behavior unchanged.

Document the `-F -` limitation in the hook docstring + README.

title: require-ticket: flip -F - (stdin) from fail-open to fail-closed-with-hint
body:
## Problem

agent-tools#102 made `git commit -F -` (commit message on git's own stdin, which a PreToolUse hook genuinely cannot read) **fail-open**: it allows the commit with a logged note. But that is a real bypass surface — `git commit -F -` dodges the ticket requirement entirely.

The CTO's intent is **strict** enforcement of require-ticket. A silent fail-open contradicts that.

## Fix

Flip the `-F -` / stdin-sentinel branch to **fail-closed-with-hint**: BLOCK (exit 10, the `[require-ticket] BLOCKED` marker) with an actionable message — the gate can't read a `-F -`/stdin message to find a ticket reference, so pass the message a readable way:

- `-m "...Closes #N..."` (checked)
- `-F <file>` with the ref inside (read + checked)
- the documented escape `[skip-ticket: <reason>]` or inline `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1` for a genuine no-ticket exception (the escape still works even on a `-F -` command, since it's parsed from the message/command, not the unreadable stdin).

All other behavior unchanged: `-m` checked, `-F <file>` read+checked, editor-commit path unchanged, accepted ticket-ref forms + escapes all still work.

## Acceptance

- `git commit -F -` (all spellings: `-F -`, `-F-`, `--file -`, `--file=-`), no ticket → **BLOCKED** (exit 10 + marker + a hint mentioning `-m`/`-F <file>`/skip).
- `-F <file with Closes #1>` → still ALLOWED.
- `-m "Closes #1"` → ALLOWED; `-m "no ref"` → BLOCKED.
- `[skip-ticket: reason]` on a `-F -` command → ALLOWED (escape still works for stdin).
- README/docstring updated from 'fail-open' to 'fail-closed-with-hint'.
- #102 tests flipped accordingly; full suite green; ruff clean.

title: docs(spec): rig-agents-provisioning.md is an UNCOMMITTED orphan in the primary checkout (corrected in place; needs landing)

title: require-ticket hook: clustered short flag `git commit -am "...msg..."` loses the message → false BLOCK + lost exemption
body:
## What

The canonical `agent-hooks/require-ticket-before-commit/require_ticket_before_commit.py` does not parse **clustered short flags** when extracting the commit message. `commit_message_from_argv` / the file-flag value extraction only recognize `-m`, `-mMSG`, `--message`, `--message=`, `-F`, `-F<path>`, `--file`, `--file=`. The very common `git commit -am "..."` (and `-aF`, `-amMSG`) is NOT handled: the token `-am` matches no branch (`'-am'.startswith('-m')` is False), so the message text is dropped and `message == ''`.

## Repro (against the current canonical, verified)

```
echo '{"args":{"command":"git commit -am \"fix ABC-12\""},"cwd":"/tmp"}' | REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=1 python3 require_ticket_before_commit.py
# → decision: block, exit 10  (the ABC-12 ticket id in the message is invisible)

echo '{"args":{"command":"git commit -am \"chore: cleanup\""},"cwd":"/tmp"}' | REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=1 python3 require_ticket_before_commit.py
# → decision: block, exit 10  (empty message ⇒ is_exempt('') is False ⇒ the chore exemption is lost too)
```

## Impact

`git commit -am "fix ABC-12"` and `git commit -am "chore: ..."` — both extremely common — falsely BLOCK in strict mode even though the message carries a ticket id / an exempt type. Note the asymmetry: `is_skip_commit` / the SKIP_FLAGS argv parsing DO handle clustered `-am` (consume the following token), but the message-extraction path does not — so `-am` is parsed differently in two places.

## Fix

Recognize clustered short flags in the message-extraction path (a leading `-a`/`-s`/`-S` etc. cluster ending in `m`/`F` consuming the following value, plus `-amMSG` inline), mirroring how the argv parser already peels them. Add tests for `-am`/`-aF`/`-amMSG`.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the opus review of task-cli #20 (the vendored-hook drift guard). The vendored copy is byte-identical to this canonical, so the bug reproduces on a real rig machine. NOT fixable in the task-cli vendored copy (that would create the very drift #20 guards against) — must be fixed here, then re-synced downstream via `task-cli/scripts/resync_vendored_hook.py`.

title: skills-read-gate: does NOT exempt dispatched subagents → false BLOCK demanding delegate-work-to-subagents + visual-proof-cycle on subagent commits
body:
## What

`agent-hooks/skills-read-gate/skills_read_gate.py` gates every work-shaped action (a `git commit`, or a build/test command) on the mandatory skills having been invoked — default `MANDATORY_SKILLS=delegate-work-to-subagents,visual-proof-cycle`. It is explicitly **NOT subagent-exempt** (README "Not subagent-exempt").

But two of the default-mandatory skills are **structurally N/A for a dispatched subagent**:
- `delegate-work-to-subagents` — the subagent **IS** the delegated work; demanding it delegate again is wrong (and a sub-subagent dispatch hangs, see memory). 
- `visual-proof-cycle` — a subagent committing a backend/test file with no UI surface has nothing visual to prove.

## Impact (surfaced by the swarm)

A 3d-cli subagent reported `skills-read-gate` **blocked its commits** demanding these two skills, forcing repeated `ALLOW_SKIP_SKILLS` overrides on every commit. Every dispatched subagent hits this on its FIRST repeat commit. The orchestration gates (`orchestrator-stays-thin`, `background-subagent-gate`) already exempt subagents via the forwarded `agent_id`/`agent_type` from the v1 event; this gate does not mirror that.

## Fix

Mirror `orchestrator-stays-thin`'s subagent detection (`agent_id` present in the v1 event, forwarded by `lib/cc_hook_bridge`): when the tool use fires inside a dispatched subagent, **drop the orchestration-only mandatory skills** (`delegate-work-to-subagents`, `visual-proof-cycle`) from the demanded set. The subagent IS the delegate (no re-delegation), and a non-UI subagent has no visual proof to give. Any project-specific mandatory skills configured via `MANDATORY_SKILLS` still apply to subagents — only the two orchestration/visual defaults are dropped. The orchestrator (no `agent_id`) still gets the full gate.

## Acceptance

- RED-first: a subagent event (`agent_id` present) with no fresh markers + a `git commit` → currently BLOCKs on repeat → after fix ALLOWs (the two orchestration defaults are N/A).
- The orchestrator (no `agent_id`) with no markers still WARN→BLOCKs (gate intact).
- A subagent with a PROJECT-specific mandatory skill (set via `MANDATORY_SKILLS`) still gated on that skill.
- Full hook test suite green; ruff clean.

title: block-no-verify: fail-closed message on an unbalanced-quote git commit is misleading (reads as 'hook broken'), causing friction
body:
## What

`agent-hooks/block-no-verify/block_no_verify.py` fails **closed** when it cannot tokenize a command that plausibly contains `git` + `commit`/`push` (the `_plausible_git_commit_or_push` path in `main()`). For a genuinely-unbalanced `git commit` — e.g. `git commit -m 'fix: don't bypass'` (an apostrophe inside single quotes) — it emits:

```
block-no-verify: could not inspect the command (fail-closed)
```

## Impact (surfaced by the swarm)

The agent landing #109 hit a `block-no-verify` BLOCK on a legit commit whose **message body** carried backticks / flag-looking tokens, and read the generic "could not inspect" message as **the hook being broken** — not as 'your commit has unbalanced quotes'. That's friction on every dispatched subagent that writes an apostrophe-bearing single-quoted message.

## Investigation finding (important)

The originally-suspected mechanism — *'backticks/flags in a **heredoc** confuse the tokenizer'* — **does NOT reproduce**: `_strip_heredocs` removes the here-doc BODY before tokenizing, so a `git commit -F - <<EOF … \`--no-verify\` … don't … EOF` is handled correctly and ALLOWs (verified across many cases; #37/#40 already covers this fully). Parseable commits whose message mentions `--no-verify`/`core.hooksPath=`/`HUSKY=0` also correctly ALLOW.

The ONLY residual over-block is a **genuinely-unbalanced-quote** `git commit`/`push` (apostrophe in a single-quoted `-m`), which:
1. is malformed shell the user's real shell would also reject, and
2. **cannot be safely narrowed to ALLOW** — a quote-recovery (append a balancing quote and re-inspect) flips `git commit -m 'unterminated --no-verify` to ALLOW, swallowing a real `--no-verify` into the message → reopens the bypass the gate exists to stop (verified). So the decision must stay BLOCK.

## Fix (no security change — message only)

Keep the BLOCK, but make the fail-closed message **actionable** for the unbalanced-quote case: say the command has unbalanced quotes and to fix the quoting (e.g. use `-F <file>` or a heredoc for a message with apostrophes) — instead of the generic 'could not inspect', which reads as a broken hook. The allow/block decision is unchanged; every existing bypass test (#36/#39) and over-block test (#37/#40) stays green.

## Acceptance

- RED-first: assert the fail-closed message for `git commit -m 'don't'` is the new actionable text (and still BLOCKs).
- Every real-bypass test (`--no-verify`, `-n`, `core.hooksPath`, env tricks, wrappers, fused/chained, `env -S` obfuscation) stays BLOCK.
- Every over-block test (parseable message mentioning triggers, unparseable non-git command) stays ALLOW.
- Full hook test suite green; ruff clean.

title: require-ticket parser: untreated value-bearing flags (--author/--date/…) + is_skip_commit asymmetry (post-#111 follow-up)
body:
## Context

While re-syncing task-cli's vendored copy of this hook to the #111 `-am` de-cluster fix, the opus review of the new parser flagged three gaps in the **canonical** `require_ticket_before_commit.py` argv parser. They predate #111 (the refactor narrowed but did not introduce them), but since #111 deliberately re-engineered the parser for lock-step parity with git on value-bearing flags, leaving the flag set incomplete is an open fail-open.

## Findings

### 1. Value-bearing long flags with a mandatory separate value are not skipped → potential ticket-gate bypass

`_OTHER_VALUE_LONG` covers reuse/reedit/fixup/squash/template, but **`--author`, `--date`, `--cleanup`, `--trailer`, `--pathspec-from-file`** also take a mandatory next-token value (git-parseopt consumes the next token even if it starts with `-`). Because they aren't skipped, a value that looks like `-m`/`-F`/`-` gets re-read as a real flag, diverging from git.

Bypass example:

```
git commit --author '-m' 'TICKET-1: ok'
```

- Our parser: `--author` skipped (`i+=1`), then the value token `-m` de-clusters into a message flag and eats `'TICKET-1: ok'` → `commit_message_from_argv` returns "TICKET-1: ok", ticket "found".
- Real git: `author="-m"`, `'TICKET-1: ok'` is a pathspec, no message in argv → editor opens, commit can proceed **without a ticket**.

Similarly `git commit --author '-F' -` makes both parsers read stdin as a message file, which git does not.

### 2. `_takes_following_message_value` / `is_skip_commit` doesn't account for `_nonmessage_flag_consumes_next`

`_takes_following_message_value` (used by `is_skip_commit`) skips only `-m`/`-F`/`--message`/`--file` values, not `-C`/`-c`/`-t`/`--reuse-message`/`--template`/… The two other parsers were taught to skip those tokens; this one wasn't — asymmetry that can mis-classify or spoof "skip". Likely fix: `_takes_following_message_value` should also return True for `_nonmessage_flag_consumes_next(tok)`.

### 3. Add behavioral tests for the new de-cluster branches

Pin at least: `-amF` (message "F", not a separate `-F`), `-aFpath`, `-amMSG`, `-C -m x` / `--reuse-message -m x` (message is NOT "x"), `-t -F -` (stdin not read), `-am -F -` (message "-F", stdin not read), and the finding-1 cases (`--author '-F' -`).

## Provenance

Surfaced by opus during task-cli PR #37 (re-sync of the vendored fixture to agent-tools #111). The fix belongs here in the canonical, not in task-cli's vendored copy (which must stay byte-identical to the canonical or its drift guard breaks); task-cli will re-sync again once this lands.

Refs #111.

title: orchestrator-stays-thin: narrow _is_subagent to read only args.agent_id (drop the unsanitized top-level event.agent_id relax-surface)

## What

`agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py` `_is_subagent` reads `args.get('agent_id') or event.get('agent_id')`. ## Fix

In `_is_subagent`, read only `args.get('agent_id')` (drop the `or event.get('agent_id')` fallback). Add a regression test that a top-level / tool_input-nested `agent_id` does NOT exempt. Keep the empty/whitespace guard.

## Acceptance

- `_is_subagent` reads only `args.agent_id`; a top-level `event.agent_id` no longer exempts.

title: require-ticket parser: value-consuming long flags matched by exact string, not git's unambiguous abbreviation (residual ticket-gate divergence)
body:
## Context

Surfaced by the opus review of #119 (require-ticket value-bearing-flag fix, agent-tools#114).
The fix added the missing value-bearing long flags (`--author`/`--date`/`--cleanup`/`--trailer`/
`--pathspec-from-file`) to `_OTHER_VALUE_LONG` so the require-ticket parser skips their value and
stays in lock-step with git. But `_OTHER_VALUE_LONG` (and `_nonmessage_flag_consumes_next`) match
by **exact string**, while git accepts **unambiguous abbreviations** of any long option.

## The residual divergence (NOT introduced by #119 — pre-existing for the whole set)

git resolves `--au` → `--author`, `--clean` → `--cleanup`, `--reu` → `--reuse-message`,
`--temp` → `--template`, etc., as long as the prefix is unambiguous. The exact-match set does not,
so the same class of divergence the fix closes stays open through an abbreviation:

```
git commit --au '-m' 'TICKET-1: ok'
```

- **Real git:** `--au` = `--author`, `author="-m"`, `'TICKET-1: ok'` is a PATHSPEC, no message in
  argv → editor opens, the commit is ticketless.
- **Our parser:** `--au` is not in the set, its value is not skipped, the value token `-m`
  de-clusters into a message flag and eats `'TICKET-1: ok'` → phantom ticket → gate falsely
  **ALLOWs**.

This applies equally to the already-handled `--reu`/`--reedit`/`--fix`/`--squ`/`--temp` and to the
five flags #119 added (`--au`/`--dat`/`--clean`/`--trail`/`--pathspec-f`). It is a parser-wide
limitation, not specific to #114's flag set.

## Why it was left out of #114

#114 was scoped to the missing-flags class (exact long spellings). Abbreviation handling is a
separate, broader concern that touches every value-consuming long option uniformly, so it belongs
in its own change rather than widening #114's blast radius.

## Possible fixes (decide in this issue)

1. **Prefix-match the value-consuming set** — for a `--xxx` token, if it is an unambiguous prefix of
   exactly one value-consuming long option (and not also a prefix of a non-value-consuming one),
   treat it as that option. Must replicate git's ambiguity rule (a prefix matching >1 option is an
   error, not silently the first) to avoid a NEW false-positive direction.
2. **Document the limitation** explicitly (a comment + a known-gap note) and accept that an
   abbreviation can slip the gate, on the grounds that an agent abbreviating commit flags to dodge
   the ticket gate is an adversary the hook is `on_error: open` against anyway.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision recorded (prefix-match vs document-only) with rationale.
- If prefix-match: RED-first tests for `--au '-m' …`, `--clean '-m' …`, `--reu '-m' …`, plus an
  ambiguity case (a prefix matching >1 option must NOT silently resolve), plus the legit path
  (`--au 'someone' -m 'Closes #1'` still allows).
- If document-only: the limitation is noted in `_OTHER_VALUE_LONG`'s comment and this issue is the
  tracked known-gap.

## Provenance

opus `review diff --staged` on #119 (finding 1, "security, остаточный обход"). Refs #114, #119.

title: CI gate scripts: leftover-grep shallow-fetch silent no-op, codeql suppression seam, dependency-review tamper model, conflict-marker false-positive
body:
Surfaced by the pre-commit review board during rig rollout wave-2 (provisioning the CI gates into bot repos). These are properties of the **shipped catalog CI gate scripts/workflows** — copied verbatim into every rigged consumer — so fixing them here fixes all consumers at once. Captured as deferred findings, not fixed in the rollout PRs (which only copy the gates).

## Findings

1. **[High] `leftover-grep` shallow-fetch breaks the three-dot diff base → gate can silently no-op.** `leftover-grep.yml` fetches the PR head with `git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin $HEAD_SHA`, then `ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh` computes `git diff --unified=0 "$base...$HEAD"`. With a depth-1 head, `git merge-base origin/main <head>` has no reachable common ancestor → either git errors (and the error is swallowed by `done < <(emit_lines)`, so `set -e` doesn't catch it → prints PASS, exits 0 → merge-blocking gate silently passes having scanned nothing) or it diffs against an empty tree → flood of false positives. Fix: fetch enough history for a real merge-base (unshallow head, or fetch base+head to the merge-base), and don't read `emit_lines` via process substitution — write to a temp file and check $?.

2. **[Med] `leftover-grep.sh` swallows `emit_lines` failures** (the `< <(...)` process-substitution issue above) — violates the claimed fail-closed for a block-tier gate even apart from depth.

3. **[Med-Low] CodeQL self-gate in-source suppression seam.** `is_source_suppressed` only walks up a *contiguous* comment block directly above the flagged line; CodeQL often attaches the alert to the step/`run:` line, not the `- name:` line where the `# codeql[...]` marker sits → suppression misses, self-gate blocks its own files. Also the codeql.yml header says 'flagged line or the line directly above' but the impl walks the whole comment block — doc/code drift.

4. **[Low] dependency-review tamper model inconsistent.** `leftover-grep` and `review-threads` run the trusted base script under `pull_request_target`, but `dependency-review.yml` (tier block) runs the PR-checked-out `ci/dependency-review/dep-audit.sh` under plain `pull_request` → a PR can weaken its own blocking gate. Align or justify.

5. **[Low] secret-scan scope drift.** `secret-scan.yml` scans the working tree (`gitleaks dir .`); `ci/secret-scan/secret-scan.sh` defaults to full history (`gitleaks git`, SCOPE=full) → the script can red-flag historical findings the workflow won't. Align defaults / document the two entry points.

6. **[Low] Conflict-marker false positive.** A `={7}( |$)` matcher false-positives on a source separator line of exactly 7 `=`.

7. **[Low] No tests for the gate parsers.** awk unified-diff parser (`emit_lines`), `is_source_suppressed`, the jq pagination sum in `review-threads.sh` — all untested, yet they decide whether a merge is blocked. Add fixtures (diff/SARIF/GraphQL samples) + unit checks for added-line extraction, the suppression matcher, and fail-closed behavior.

8. **[nit] Double-trigger.** `dependency-review.yml` and `secret-scan.yml` trigger on both `pull_request` and `push: ['**']` → two runs per PR-branch push. Consider pinning minimum tool versions (`bun audit`, `gitleaks`).

comments.body:
Additional CI-gate findings surfaced reviewing the HyperSummaryBot rollout PR (codeql self-gate, same shipped scripts):

9. **[High] `codeql.yml` detect-step: `pipefail` + `git ls-files | grep -q` can falsely report 'no source' → silently disable CodeQL.** `grep -q` exits on first match and closes the pipe; `git ls-files` then gets SIGPIPE → exit 141; under `pipefail` the pipeline status is 141 → the `if` goes to `else` → `has_source=false` → CodeQL skipped despite source existing. Non-deterministic; on a large repo the gate self-disables — the exact 'silent disable' the comment promises to avoid. Fix: drop `pipefail` for that pipe, or `git ls-files > files.txt; grep -qiE "$pattern" files.txt`.

10. **[Med] `is_source_suppressed`: SARIF `artifactLocation.uri` used as a CWD-relative path.** Absolute or `file://`-prefixed URIs make `[ -f "$src" ]` always false → in-source suppression never matches, every finding gates as unsuppressed. Normalize the URI (strip `file://`, map to checkout root) or pin the expected format.

title: docs(ci): document client-vs-server gate enforcement (the #543 bypass gap)
body:
## What is wrong

hyper-saas PR #543 squash-merged through **red CI, open review threads, and no screenshot**. Two root causes, both outside the catalog's current client-side enforcement:

1. **No server-side branch protection** — the catalog's `tier: block` CI gates only make a workflow go *red*; they are **advisory** unless promoted to a **required status check** + branch protection. That promotion is a manual admin step the catalog documents nowhere as mandatory.
2. **`ship.sh` / `block-raw-pr-merge` are client-only** — a GitHub-UI merge or a raw `gh pr merge` from an uninstrumented shell bypasses them entirely.

The catalog (this repo) is the **documentation/policy** half. The server-side reconciler that actually flips required-checks + `require-conversation-resolution` is **rig-cli#5** (built separately).

## Evidence

- hyper-saas #543: merged state with `statusCheckRollup` red + an unresolved review thread + zero embedded image. The `tier: block` `tests` workflow was red; the merge button was not blocked because no required-check/branch-protection existed.

## User-facing consequence

Anyone trusting "the catalog installs gates" believes red CI / open threads block a merge. They do not, unless server-side enforcement is separately provisioned. Silent false sense of safety → broken code lands on `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ci/screenshots/` slot exists with a server-side workflow + README that states it must be a REQUIRED check.
- [ ] Every `tier: block` gate README (review-threads, leftover-grep, pr-checklist, screenshots, dependency-review, tests) carries the "required-status-check + branch-protection or it does NOT block the merge button; rig-cli#5 provisions via `github:`" note.
- [ ] README.md + AGENTS.md carry a CLIENT-vs-SERVER enforcement section citing #543.
- [ ] The `github:` rig.yaml block (required_status_checks, required_conversation_resolution, enforce_admins, required reviews) is documented as a schema/example, referencing rig-cli#5 for the reconciler.

title: fix(review-gate): use `command git` to bypass shell aliases/wrappers in hash computation
body:
## Problem

The review-gate hook computes a hash of `git diff --no-ext-diff --cached` to verify a commit was reviewed. RTK (Rust Token Killer) can be configured as a shell alias/wrapper that rewrites `git diff` output into a compact summary format — completely different from real git's unified diff output.

This means that if a shell alias or function wraps `git`, the hash computed in the hook would differ from the hash written by review-cli (which calls the real git binary via subprocess directly), blocking commits even after a legitimate review.

## Root cause

The hook uses bare `git diff`, which is subject to shell alias/function resolution. review-cli uses `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` which bypasses aliases entirely.

## Fix

Use `command git` instead of bare `git` in the hook. `command` bypasses shell aliases and functions, ensuring the hook always calls the real git binary and produces the same hash as review-cli.

This closes the open follow-up from the roadmap: "review-gate / review-tool: pinned git diff vs rtk fragility"

title: install-local-hooks: already-wired lefthook repos keep the stdin-less pre-push entry (fail-open) after a8bfc54
body:
## What
PR #157 (a8bfc54) fixed `inject_lefthook` to emit `use_stdin: true` on the injected pre-push command — without it lefthook does not forward the pushed-refs stdin and `protect-main` fails OPEN on a direct push to main.

But `inject_lefthook` short-circuits on the wiring marker for the WHOLE config file:

```sh
if grep -q "$MARKER" "$cfg" 2>/dev/null; then
  log "lefthook already wired ($cfg) — no-op"; return 0
fi
```

A lefthook repo wired BEFORE a8bfc54 already carries a pre-push `global-git-hooks-dispatcher` entry WITHOUT `use_stdin: true` (pre-push was in `EVENTS` since #3). Re-running the installer / `hooks-sweep` is a no-op for it, so those repos stay fail-open on protect-main until someone hand-edits `lefthook.yml`.

(husky is fine: `inject_husky` checks the marker PER EVENT FILE, so a re-run adds the missing `.husky/pre-push`.)

## User impact
On machines/repos wired via the retrofit script or `hooks-sweep` before the fix, a direct `git push origin main` in a lefthook-managed repo is NOT blocked — the exact gap #157 shipped to close — and nothing reports it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `install-local-hooks.sh` upgrades an already-wired lefthook pre-push dispatcher entry that lacks `use_stdin: true` (or the wired-check becomes per-event/per-shape, not whole-file)
- [ ] selfcheck assertion: a lefthook.yml pre-wired with the OLD stdin-less entry gets `use_stdin: true` on re-run

Found during HYP-856 activation (2026-07-02). Ref: PR #157, rig-cli#100.

title: orchestrator-stays-thin: whitelist `gh ship` release chains for the orchestrator (gated-ship deadlock)
body:
## What
Add a narrow carve-out to the orchestrator-stays-thin pre-bash agent-hook ([orchestrator_stays_thin.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py)): a Bash line whose chain segments are all either a `gh ship` invocation (segment HEAD, optional env-var prefixes) or read-only inspection is treated as a RELEASE action, not implementation, and never trips the warn-block tier. Matching is per-segment argv HEAD, never substring-in-text, so a needle like grep 'gh ship' cannot self-exempt, and `gh ship` cannot launder an implementation segment (in-place edits, package installs, heredocs still block). Nothing else (tg etc.) is whitelisted.

## Why (motivation)
Deadlock observed live (Alex tg#5694, answer 'B'): the delegate-work hook warn-then-blocks the ORCHESTRATOR's inline `gh ship` chains (it flapped — let one through, blocked the next two), while the auto-mode classifier denies SUBAGENTS running gh ship (self-merge relay). Net effect: nobody can reliably run the one sanctioned merge command.

## User impact
The orchestrator can always run the sanctioned gated merge (`gh ship <PR>`, incl. '| tail' plumbing) without hook flapping, so finished PRs actually merge instead of wedging; all other implementation-shaped inline Bash stays gated exactly as before.

## Cost of inaction
Every ship attempt is a coin-flip on the warn-block tier TTL: PRs pile up unmerged, agents burn turns on escape hatches or (worse) route around the sanctioned merge path entirely.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] pre-bash event with command "gh ship 605 2>&1 | tail -30 | grep -i merged" exits 0 (allow) on first AND repeat call (never primes the warn-block tier); proven by running the hook script with crafted stdin JSON — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-work-hyperide/81bb8c60-8548-4884-b29a-259dec215585/scratchpad/criterion1_gh_ship_allow_fixed.txt)
- [x] implementation chains stay blocked: an in-place-edit chain ending in gh ship and a stage-commit-push chain still WARN then BLOCK (exit 10 on repeat); a grep needle containing 'gh ship' inside a non-read-only pipe is NOT exempted — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-work-hyperide/81bb8c60-8548-4884-b29a-259dec215585/scratchpad/criterion2_impl_chains_block_fixed.txt)
- [x] pytest [test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py) green with new carve-out tests following the per-segment-head pattern of [#80](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/80) — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-work-hyperide/81bb8c60-8548-4884-b29a-259dec215585/scratchpad/criterion3_pytest_green.txt)

title: Harness workflow guards: worktree-only writes + orchestrator-only enforcement (tg#5742/5743)
body:
## Motivation

Two harness-discipline rules from Alex need enforcement at the PreToolUse layer (agents ignore prose rules; hooks make them stick):

- **tg#5742 — worktree-only:** no authoring on a repo's default branch. All Edit/Write goes in a worktree on a feature branch; the default branch is for merge/pull/read-only. Complements the existing pre-push `protect-main` git-hook (that blocks the *push*; this blocks the *authoring* that precedes it).
- **tg#5743 — orchestrator-only:** the main thread only orchestrates; subagents do the implementation work. The `orchestrator-stays-thin` hook already enforces this; this issue broadens its allow-list (so orchestration chains like `gh pr list && gh pr view`, `gh ship && tg done` don't flap into a block) and makes it per-repo configurable.

## Scope

- New `worktree-only-writes` pre-write hook (denies Edit/Write while HEAD is on the default branch, detected via `origin/HEAD` / `init.defaultBranch`, never hardcoded). Opt-IN.
- Broaden `orchestrator-stays-thin`: sanctioned-orchestration allow-list (`gh pr` reads, `gh ship`, `tg`, `review`, `git worktree list`, GET-shaped `gh api`), wrapper stripping (`timeout 60 pytest`), quote-aware chain split. Default-ON (opt-OUT).
- Per-repo config knobs read from `rig.yaml` at fire time: `agent_hooks.worktree_only` (default false) / `agent_hooks.orchestrator_only` (default true). Schema/validator side lands in rig-cli.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A pre-write on the default branch is denied by `worktree-only-writes` when `worktree_only: true`; allowed on a feature branch and in any repo that leaves the knob off (e.g. `3d-cli`).
2. An orchestration-only chain (`gh ship 5 && tg done`, `gh pr list && gh pr view`) is never blocked; a real inline implementation (`git commit`, `pytest`, `sed -i … && …`) warn-then-blocks.
3. The broadened allow-list does NOT launder a mutation smuggled past its head-anchor (command/process substitution, bare-`&` background, `git branch <arg>`, find delete/exec/file-write) — verified no regression vs the pre-existing hook.
4. `3d-cli` (works directly on main) is exempt: `worktree_only` off + `orchestrator_only: false`.
5. Both hooks fail-open on a git/parse error; escape hatches exist (`RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1`, `ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK=1`+reason).
6. Full agent-tools test suite green.

## User impact

Without this, the harness rules are prose the agents drift from: work lands on main, and the main thread does implementation inline instead of delegating — the exact failure modes tg#5742/5743 call out. With it, the discipline is enforced per-repo and configurable, with a clean exemption for repos that legitimately work on main.

title: gh ship --repo <owner/repo> cross-repo support lost from ci/ship/ship.sh
body:
## Problem

`ci/ship/ship.sh` explicitly REJECTS `-R/--repo` (arg-parse case ~line 90):

> ship.sh does not support -R/--repo — run gh ship <PR-number> from inside the repo checkout instead.

The `gh ship` alias resolves to a per-repo thin delegator (`.claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh`) that only forwards args to `ci/ship/ship.sh`. So the rejection here is the single point where cross-repo shipping breaks.

## Impact

An orchestrator that is forbidden a `cd && gh ship` (policy) has NO way to ship a PR into a non-CWD repo (agent-tools, rig-cli, tg-cli). `--repo` is the only mechanism. A previous full ship script (pre thin-delegator) supported `--repo` correctly; the support was lost when the logic moved into `ci/ship/ship.sh`.

## Fix

Restore `--repo <owner/repo>` (and `-R`, `--repo=…`, `-R=…`, `-R…` forms): thread it through every gh call via `GH_REPO`, and SKIP remote-branch deletion when the target is a foreign remote (so `git push origin --delete` never hits the wrong repo).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `gh ship <n> --repo x/y` is accepted (no "does not support"/"Unknown flag") and pins `GH_REPO` onto the gh calls.
- [ ] Foreign `--repo` skips remote branch deletion with a clear message; the wrong remote's branch is untouched.
- [ ] The plain `gh ship <n>` (no `--repo`) path is unchanged.

title: gh ship --repo: make local gates (version-bump, CI-down runner, worktree/branch cleanup) target-aware
body:
## Context

Follow-up from #165 (restore `gh ship --repo`). That PR faithfully ports the pre-thin-delegator cross-repo design: gh calls (view/checks/merge) and remote-branch deletion are target-aware via `GH_REPO`; the remaining LOCAL operations stay bound to the CWD checkout, matching the original's documented limitation.

Multi-model review (codex, P1 x3) flagged the CWD-bound paths:

1. **Local worktree/branch preflight + cleanup** operate on `$BRANCH` in the CWD checkout. A foreign PR whose branch name collides with a local branch could false-block on the local ahead-check, or after merge remove the CWD repo's same-named worktree/local branch. (`ci/ship/ship.sh` local-branch sanity + `cleanup()`.)
2. **Version-bump gate**: `gh pr diff` is pinned to the target via `GH_REPO`, but `locate_version_file()` reads `$ROOT` (CWD). A foreign target with `package.json` can be checked against this repo's `pyproject.toml`, or skipped if CWD has no version file.
3. **CI-down local fallback** runs local tests in `$ROOT` (CWD), not the `--repo` target — during a target-repo CI outage it could merge a foreign PR based on unrelated local tests.

## Why deferred

Fixing these properly requires a target-repo checkout mapping (or explicit target test/version knobs) — a new design beyond the "restore lost functionality" scope of #165, which was constrained to a minimal faithful port. The collision risk is low in practice (foreign branch names rarely match local ones) and #2/#3 are non-destructive (wrong gate verdict, not data loss).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Foreign `--repo` skips (or correctly targets) the local worktree/branch preflight + cleanup so a CWD same-named branch/worktree is never touched; test proves survival.
- [ ] Version-bump gate resolves the version file from the target repo/PR (or requires an override) for foreign ships; test with differing CWD/target manifests.
- [ ] CI-down local fallback is disabled (or target-aware) for foreign `--repo`; test with `--repo` + `SHIP_TEST_CI_DOWN=1`.

title: fix(agent-hooks): visual-proof-gate effective_cwd() mishandles tilde-expanded cd targets
body:
## What
[effective_cwd()](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/c2466e7f4eb4609d36e62b74ad875b2b7f467cd4/agent-hooks/visual-proof-gate/visual_proof_gate.py#L206) in visual_proof_gate.py resolves the real target repo for a cd <dir> && git commit / git -C <dir> commit, but did not shell-expand a leading ~ in the cd/-C argument. cd ~/repo produced a bogus path (<session_cwd>/~/repo), the subsequent git -C <bogus> diff --cached failed, and the whole gate silently failed OPEN (skipped the visual-proof check) instead of resolving the real repo.

title: chore(agent-hooks): port punctuation_chars tokenizer to visual-proof-gate + skills-read-gate (glued-separator under-split)
body:
## What
require_review.py already solved TWO related problems visual_proof_gate.py and skills_read_gate.py still have, with a shlex.shlex(punctuation_chars=True) tokenizer plus a _CD_CARRY_SEP set. (1) Glued separators: plain shlex.split glues a no-space separator to the adjacent word (a cd target directly followed by a semicolon and "git" -- one token, never split), under-detecting the real target repo. (2) Full-chain conditional-execution validation: visual_proof_gate.py's effective_cwd now trusts a cd preceded by && or ; (matching _CD_CARRY_SEP), which is REQUIRED for the common "setup && cd target && git-commit" pattern to resolve correctly, but this only checks the SINGLE separator immediately around each cd, not the full path to the commit segment. A narrow, deliberately-adversarial construction remains open: a failing predecessor chained via && into a cd targeting a real-but-irrelevant repo, then a semicolon before the real commit -- a real shell never runs that cd (the predecessor fails, short-circuiting the &&), so the commit lands in session_cwd, but effective_cwd still resolves to the decoy repo, because the semicolon that decouples the eventual commit's execution from the cd's success is never checked. Properly closing this requires validating that EVERY separator from a cd through to the commit segment is unbroken &&, not just the one next to the cd. Currently documented and test-pinned in visual_proof_gate.py as an accepted trade-off (this hook's own doctrine is on_error: open, process discipline not a security boundary) rather than fixed, given fixing it naively (treating any && as untrustworthy) breaks the much more common and higher-value "setup && cd && commit" pattern -- confirmed by an actual regression caught and reverted during review of agent-tools#172.

## Why (motivation)
Surfaced during multi-round review (review diff --pool 1) of [PR fixing visual_proof_gate.py's effective_cwd() tilde-expansion bug](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/172) (tg#6137). Confirmed empirically: shlex.split('cd /b;git commit -m x') == ['cd', '/b;git', 'commit', '-m', 'x'] (one glued token, never segmented). Pre-existing in both hooks before that PR; not a regression it introduced.

> **tg#6137** — Alex, 2026-07-04 02:34 UTC:
> Да, Да
<!-- tasklib:msgref-quote:6137 -->

## User impact
A cd <other-repo>;git commit or cd <other-repo>&git commit (no space around the separator) is not recognized as changing directory, so the visual-proof-gate / skills-read-gate checks the wrong repo's staged files -- silently missing an unproven UI commit in a real other repo.

## Cost of inaction
Glued-separator commit chains keep silently bypassing (or wrongly gating) these two hooks; the gap is not exploitable often but is a real, known, unfixed correctness hole.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] visual_proof_gate.py and skills_read_gate.py tokenize with the same punctuation_chars + _CD_CARRY_SEP model as require_review.py (or import/share a common implementation)
- [ ] a test with a glued separator (cd /other;git commit, cd /other&&git commit with no spaces) correctly resolves the cd target in both hooks

title: fix(agent-hooks): skills-read-gate is_skip_commit still exempts a chain on its FIRST commit segment (out of sync with visual-proof-gate)

## What
[visual_proof_gate.py's is_skip_commit()](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/c2466e7f4eb4609d36e62b74ad875b2b7f467cd4/agent-hooks/visual-proof-gate/visual_proof_gate.py#L326) was fixed, see [agent-tools#172](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/172), to require EVERY commit segment in a chained command to carry a skip flag before exempting the whole command -- previously it returned on the FIRST commit segment found, so a rebase-continue chained with a second real commit was wrongly exempted. skills_read_gate.py's is_skip_commit (or equivalent) still has the original bug: it returns on the first commit segment, so the SAME bypass command exempts skills-read-gate's mandatory-skill check even though it doesn't exempt visual-proof-gate anymore.
