title: feat(agent-hooks): visual-proof-gate should evaluate EVERY commit segment in a multi-commit chain, not fall back to session_cwd
body:
## What
In [effective_cwd()](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/c2466e7f4eb4609d36e62b74ad875b2b7f467cd4/agent-hooks/visual-proof-gate/visual_proof_gate.py#L296), a command chaining TWO OR MORE non-skip commit invocations (e.g. one commit targeting repo B, a second targeting repo C, via -C or cd, neither being session_cwd) is ambiguous, so the current fix falls back to checking only session_cwd -- correctly closing the decoy-commit bypass this PR (agent-tools#172) found, but it still does not evaluate repo B or repo C at all. A real staged, unproven UI file in either could still land uncaught. Proper fix: evaluate the resolved target directory of EVERY non-skip commit segment in the chain and BLOCK if any of them has staged visual files without a fresh proof marker, rather than picking one directory to check.

## Why (motivation)
Surfaced during the same review pass that fixed agent-tools#172's decoy-commit-first bypass; the session_cwd fallback closes that specific bypass but is not a complete fix for a chain of multiple REAL commits across multiple non-session repos.

## User impact
A single bash invocation chaining commits into two DIFFERENT other repos (both real, neither a decoy) can still land an unproven UI change in either repo, because the gate only ever inspects one directory per invocation.

## Cost of inaction
Multi-repo, multi-commit chains remain a known, narrow gap in the visual-proof doctrine; not worse than before agent-tools#172 (the old code also only ever checked session_cwd), but not fully closed either.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] effective_cwd (or a replacement) returns/evaluates the target directory for EVERY non-skip commit segment in a chain, not just one
- [ ] main() blocks if ANY evaluated target has staged visual files without a fresh proof marker
- [ ] a test with two real commits into two different non-session_cwd repos, one with an unproven staged .tsx, proves the gate now blocks on it

title: rtk-rewrite hook rewrites 'git commit'-like text INSIDE string arguments — silent corruption
body:
## Problem

The rtk-rewrite hook silently corrupts arbitrary text data that happens to contain command-like substrings, not just text being executed as shell commands.

**Discovered 2026-07-04**: While filing a different ticket, the ticket's own body text got silently corrupted because it contained the phrase 'git commit' as prose, not as an executed command. This was caught only by accident; similar corruption could easily go unnoticed in other cases (log messages, code comments passed as CLI args).

## Impact

Any CLI invocation whose string argument happens to contain command-like substrings can be silently mangled by this hook, corrupting data with no error or warning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- rtk-rewrite only rewrites text that is actually being executed as a shell command
- Never rewrite text embedded as DATA inside quoted string arguments (e.g., a ticket body, commit message being composed, --title flag value)
- Regression test: a command whose argument literally contains 'git commit' as part of unrelated prose does not get corrupted

## Example Scenario

```bash
gh issue create --title 'ticket about git commit command' # this gets corrupted
```

The --title value is data, not a shell command being executed, so it should pass through unchanged.

title: feat(agent-hooks): block-reset-hard — guard git reset --hard / clean -f
body:
## Motivation

Incident: a subagent working an unrelated PR ran `git reset --hard` mid-session in a
checkout shared with a different session, wiping that session's uncommitted work
(client/App.tsx + .claude/scheduled_tasks.lock in the hyperide repo). Data was recovered,
but it exposed a real gap: nothing technically stops an agent from running
`git reset --hard` (or `git clean -f...`) without deliberate, logged approval.

## What's wrong

No agent-hook exists to intercept these two destructive, irreversible git operations
before they run. Advisory docs (AGENTS.md) cannot stop an autonomous agent mid-session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `pre-bash` agent-hook `block-reset-hard` blocks `git reset --hard` (any ref) and
      `git clean` with a real `-f`/`--force` flag (alone or clustered with `-d`/`-x`).
- [ ] Allows safe alternatives: `git checkout --`/`git restore`, bare/--mixed/--soft reset,
      `git clean -n`/--dry-run, and text that merely mentions the phrase.
- [ ] Escape hatch: `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD=1` + `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD_REASON=...`, or inline
      `# no-reset-guard: <reason>` sentinel.
- [ ] `on_error: closed` (fail-closed).
- [ ] Registered in `agent-hooks/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`'s pre-bash hook tables.
- [ ] Unit tests + full suite green.

## User impact

Turns an accidental destructive `git reset --hard`/`git clean -f` into a deliberate,
logged action instead of a silent, irreversible data-loss event.

title: agent-hooks README inventory count is stale (says 8, actual is 20+)
body:
## What's wrong

Found while working PR #179 (block-reset-hard agent-hook). The top-level `agent-tools/README.md` has an inventory line claiming "Agent-hooks: 8 — ..." but the `agent-hooks/` directory actually contains 20+ hooks now (block-no-verify, block-raw-pr-merge, block-raw-process-env, block-secrets-write, worktree-only-writes, orchestrator-stays-thin, background-subagent-gate, decision-request-format, enforce-timeout-on-bash, model-error-fallback, no-long-inline-process, no-shell-file-edit, require-review-before-commit, require-ticket-before-commit, skills-read-gate, stop-completion-selfcheck, subagent-no-bg-longproc, visual-proof-gate, block-reset-hard, ...).

This predates the block-reset-hard change and is out of scope for that PR.

## Impact

A reader trusting the README's count undercounts the actual guard surface by more than half — makes the hook catalog look smaller/less mature than it is, and the count will keep drifting every time a hook is added without a corresponding README bump.

## Fix

- Update the inventory line to the real count.
- Consider generating it (a small script that counts `agent-hooks/*/​*.{point}.json` descriptors) so it can't silently go stale again, same idea as `rig-cli`'s catalog scanner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README inventory line matches `ls agent-hooks/ | wc -l` (or the descriptor count) at time of fix.
- [ ] Either a comment noting "update this when adding a hook" or an automated count, so it doesn't drift again.

title: Sibling pre-bash hooks missing 'if' in leading-shell-noise stripping (same gap fixed in block-reset-hard)
body:
## What's wrong

While building PR #179 (`block-reset-hard`), hardening rounds (multi-model `review diff`) caught a real bug in the leading-shell-noise stripper: `if` was missing from the set of leading control-flow tokens stripped before checking `argv[0]`, so a guarded command wrapped in `if ...; then git reset --hard; fi` could slip past detection undetected. Fixed it locally in `block-reset-hard`'s own copy of the tokenizer.

Each pre-bash hook in `agent-hooks/` carries its OWN self-contained copy of this argv-parsing logic (by design — see `agent-hooks/README.md`, no shared runtime between hooks). That means the same gap is very likely present in the sibling hooks that use the same shlex-based tokenizer pattern:

- `block-no-verify`
- `require-ticket-before-commit`
- `block-raw-pr-merge`
- (possibly others — worth auditing every hook that strips leading shell-noise tokens before argv[0] inspection)

Not fixed as part of #179 since it's each hook's own code, not block-reset-hard's, and touching them was out of scope for a focused PR.

## Impact

A command wrapped in `if COND; then git commit --no-verify; fi` (or the pr-merge / ticket-check equivalents) could bypass the corresponding guard even though the direct, unwrapped form is correctly blocked. This is the same class of gap the hardening rounds found and fixed for block-reset-hard.

## Fix

Audit each sibling hook's `_LEADING_SHELL_NOISE`-equivalent set (or whatever it's named locally), add `if`/`then`/`else`/`elif`/`fi` as needed (matching what block-reset-hard now does), and add a regression test per hook (`if true; then git commit --no-verify; fi` → still blocked, etc.).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `block-no-verify` strips `if`/`then`/`else`/`elif`/`fi` before argv inspection, with a regression test.
- [ ] `require-ticket-before-commit` — same.
- [ ] `block-raw-pr-merge` — same.
- [ ] Any other pre-bash hook found to share this gap during the audit — same.

title: feat(agent-hooks): pin the primary worktree to its default branch (pre-bash)
body:
## What's wrong

Incident (Alex tg#6462/tg#6477, 2026-07-04): an agent doing HYP-917 work ran `git checkout
feat/hyp-autofix-unsupported-framework` directly in the SHARED main checkout
(`/Users/ultra/work/hyperide`) instead of its own isolated worktree. No file damage happened
this time (the agent caught it immediately and had authored everything in its real worktree),
but a second, concurrent agent then also checked out (and committed on) a *different* feature
branch in that same shared checkout before switching back to main — a real collision, since any
agent relying on the primary checkout sitting on `main` can have it pulled out from under it
mid-operation.

Investigation found TWO pre-existing, real gaps:

1. **Never enrolled anywhere.** `worktree-only-writes` (pre-write; PR #164, tg#5742) is opt-in
   per-repo via `agent_hooks.worktree_only: true` in a repo's `rig.yaml`. Its own README/AGENTS.md
   claim "hyperide + the agent-ecosystem repos set worktree_only: true" — but NONE of hyperide,
   agent-tools, or rig-cli's own `rig.yaml` (nor the global `~/.config/rig/config.yaml`) actually
   set it. The guard has been a documented no-op since it shipped.
2. **A blind spot even when enrolled.** `worktree-only-writes` only fires on Edit/Write tool
   calls, so a bare `git checkout <branch>` (a Bash call) is invisible to it. And once the
   checkout HAS moved to a feature branch, its own branch check treats "on a feature branch" as
   "exactly where authoring belongs" — true for a *linked* `git worktree add` tree, false for the
   PRIMARY checkout, which it never distinguishes.

## The fix

New `pre-bash` agent-hook `pin-primary-worktree` (this PR): detects the PRIMARY worktree via
git's own `--git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` distinction, and BLOCKS a `git checkout`/`git switch`
that would move it onto anything but the default branch — regardless of target branch name.
Shares the same `agent_hooks.worktree_only` opt-in knob as `worktree-only-writes` (one feature,
one flag) and the same `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT` escape hatch. Complements, does not replace,
`worktree-only-writes`.

Gap #1 (never enrolled) is a separate, per-repo config fix (hyperide's `rig.yaml`, tracked
separately in the hyperide repo).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pin_primary_worktree.py` blocks `git checkout`/`git switch` to a non-default branch when
      the checkout is the repo's PRIMARY worktree, and allows it in a LINKED worktree.
- [ ] Checking back OUT to the default branch, `git worktree add`, and all read-only git
      commands remain unaffected.
- [ ] `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1` escape hatch works, matching `worktree-only-writes`.
- [ ] Full existing pytest suite (2296+ tests) stays green.

## User impact

Without this, any concurrent-agent session sharing one repo checkout can silently clobber
another agent's expected branch state in the primary worktree — exactly what happened on
2026-07-04. Cost of inaction: repeat collisions, possibly with real file damage next time
instead of a clean-tree near-miss.

title: bug(catalog): one-descriptor-per-hook-dir scan silently drops a hook's second point
body:
## What's wrong

Found while building `pin-primary-worktree` ([PR#183](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/183)): `riglib/catalog.py`'s `_scan_agent_hooks` (rig-cli) does

```python
descriptor = next(iter(sorted(d.glob("*.json"))), None)
```

— ONE descriptor per hook DIRECTORY, alphabetically first. `riglib/plan.py` then emits exactly ONE `install_agent_hook` Action per catalog Item, carrying that single descriptor name. This model doesn't support a hook directory with more than one `*.json` descriptor.

`orchestrator-stays-thin/` ships TWO: `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-bash.json` and `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-write.json` (added together in [#164](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/164), the same PR that shipped `worktree-only-writes`). Sorted alphabetically, `pre-bash` < `pre-write`, so `pre-bash` wins the single "descriptor" slot and `pre-write` is silently never planned or installed.

**Confirmed on the live machine**: `~/.claude/hooks/` has `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-bash.json` but NO `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-write.json` — meaning the "keep the orchestrator thin" gate's `pre-write` half (blocking the main thread from inline CODE Edit/Write, not just Bash) has been non-functional since #164 shipped, on every machine that ran `rig apply` since.

## Why this matters

This is the exact class of bug the whole `pin-primary-worktree` investigation was about: a guard that looks shipped and documented but was never actually wired to fire. Same root cause here — the provisioning layer, not the hook logic itself.

## Fix

`riglib/catalog.py` `_scan_agent_hooks` should collect ALL `*.json` descriptors per hook directory (not just the first), and `riglib/plan.py` should emit one `install_agent_hook` Action per descriptor, not per directory. Needs care around:
- the per-hook enable/disable knob in `rig.yaml`'s `agent_hooks.items.<name>` — currently keyed by directory name; decide whether it now applies to all descriptors in that dir (likely correct) or needs a compound key.
- `riglib/drift.py`'s `_extras_hooks` (already iterates `hook_dir.glob("*.json")` correctly — only the catalog/plan side has the one-descriptor limit).

## Scope note

NOT fixed as part of #183 — that PR deliberately sidesteps this by giving `pin-primary-worktree` its OWN hook directory (single descriptor), so it installs correctly under the CURRENT (buggy) model. This ticket tracks fixing the underlying catalog/plan limitation so `orchestrator-stays-thin`'s pre-write half (and any future dual-point hook) actually installs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rig apply` (or the equivalent test) installs BOTH `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-write.json` and `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-bash.json`.
- [ ] A regression test in rig-cli's `tests/test_actions_drift.py` (or sibling) covers a hook directory with 2+ descriptors.
- [ ] `rig status` drift-check no longer needs the workaround of separate hook directories to get multi-point hooks installed.

## User impact / cost of inaction

The orchestrator-stays-thin pre-write gate (delegate-work-to-subagents enforcement for inline code edits) has silently done nothing since #164 shipped — the main thread can freely Edit/Write code inline with no nudge to delegate, on every machine, indefinitely, until this is fixed.

title: pin-primary-worktree: wrapper commands (env/timeout/nice/...) bypass classification, same class as the leading-assignment bug
body:
## Context

PR #183 fixed two review findings in `agent-hooks/pin-primary-worktree/pin_primary_worktree.py`:
1. missing shebang (exec-format error → fail-open, every checkout allowed)
2. leading shell assignments (`GIT_TRACE=1 git checkout x`) not stripped before checking `toks[0] == "git"`, so the whole segment was misclassified as "not git" and skipped — a full bypass of the block.

While fixing #2, `_classify_git_segment` now skips leading `VAR=val` assignments. It does **not** skip passthrough command wrappers — `env`, `timeout`/`gtimeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `time` — so a segment like:

```
env git checkout feat/x
timeout 5 git checkout feat/x
nice -n10 git checkout feat/x
```

still has `toks[0] != "git"` (or, after skipping the wrapper's own flags, the classifier still starts at index 0 rather than scanning past the wrapper), so these are classified as "not git" and silently ALLOWED — the same bypass class as the leading-assignment bug, just via a different shell idiom.

## Why this wasn't fixed in #183

The two code-review threads on #183 only flagged the leading-assignment shape (`VAR=val git ...`); wrapper commands weren't raised, so fixing them was out of scope for that PR's review cycle. Flagging here per the "don't silently drop a finding" discipline rather than scope-creeping the original fix.

## Existing reference implementation

The sibling `agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py` already solves exactly this problem: `_strip_wrappers()` (see `_ASSIGN_RE`, `_WRAPPERS`, `_WRAPPER_OPT_ARGS`) strips leading assignments AND passthrough wrappers (env/time/timeout/nice/nohup/stdbuf/ionice/setsid, basename-matched so `/usr/bin/env` counts), with per-wrapper option-arg tables so a flag like `-i` isn't misread the same way across different wrappers.

## Suggested fix

Port the same stripping logic (or extract a shared helper, if a shared module between agent-hooks scripts becomes acceptable — currently each hook is standalone by convention) into `pin_primary_worktree._classify_git_segment`, ahead of (or combined with) the current leading-assignment skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `env git checkout <feature>` in an enrolled primary worktree is BLOCKED (currently silently allowed)
- [ ] `timeout 5 git checkout <feature>` / `gtimeout 5 git checkout <feature>` is BLOCKED
- [ ] `nice -n10 git checkout <feature>`, `nohup git checkout <feature>`, `stdbuf -i0 git checkout <feature>` are BLOCKED
- [ ] A bare `env` (print environment, no command) remains read-only/allowed
- [ ] Regression tests added per case, following the existing `tests/test_pin_primary_worktree.py` conventions (real temp git repos, not mocks)

title: rig apply never runs automatically after an agent-hook PR merges to main — new/changed hooks silently don't take effect
body:
## What's wrong

Third occurrence of this exact failure mode in one day (2026-07-04):

- PR #179 (`block-reset-hard`) merged to main at ~16:14.
- PR #183 (`pin-primary-worktree`) merged to main at 16:37.
- Neither hook's `.pre-bash.json` descriptor was actually installed to the live
  `~/.claude/hooks/` directory that `cc_hook_bridge` reads — `rig status` showed both as
  `descriptor not installed` right up until this issue was filed, i.e. for the entire
  ~2+ hours between merge and discovery. During that window `git reset --hard` was NOT
  blocked in any live Claude Code session on this machine, despite the hook existing,
  being merged, and being covered by 2296+ passing tests.
- This is exactly how a subagent (ac355d41, working PR #183 itself) hit an unrelated
  `git reset --hard` mid-session that wiped its own round-1 edits — at that moment the
  guard that exists specifically to stop this had already been merged to main for over
  an hour, but was not yet live because nobody had re-run `rig apply`.

Root cause: `rig apply` is the ONLY mechanism that syncs `agent-hooks/*/*.pre-bash.json`
source templates (with the `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/` placeholder resolved to a real path) into
`~/.claude/hooks/`. Nothing triggers it automatically on a merge to main — not a
post-merge git hook, not a CI job, not a launchd/cron timer. A developer or agent has to
remember to run it by hand after every agent-hooks change, in every repo/machine that
should pick it up. We've now had 3 variants of "a guard exists in source but isn't
actually live" in a single day because of this gap.

## The fix

Some form of auto-reconciliation so a merged agent-hook is live within minutes, not
"whenever someone happens to run `rig apply`":

- A post-merge/post-checkout git hook in agent-tools' own repo (via the existing
  global git-hooks dispatcher) that runs `rig apply` (or at minimum the `agent_hooks`
  slice of it) whenever `agent-hooks/**` changes land on main in a checkout that has it
  checked out.
- And/or a periodic local timer (launchd, matching the existing tg-ctl / model-freshness
  cron pattern already in `~/.config/rig/config.yaml`) that runs `rig apply --only
  agent_hooks` on a short interval (e.g. every 15-30 min) so drift self-heals even
  without anyone noticing a PR merged.
- `rig status`/`rig apply` output should probably also be surfaced somewhere more visible
  than "run it and read stdout" — e.g. a SessionStart hook that runs `rig status --quiet`
  and warns if there's agent_hooks drift, so a stale install is visible at the start of
  every Claude Code session instead of silently doing nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A newly merged/changed agent-hooks descriptor becomes live in `~/.claude/hooks/`
      without a human remembering to run `rig apply` by hand — verified by merging a
      trivial hook change and observing it appear on disk within the chosen
      interval/trigger, with no manual `rig apply` invocation.
- [ ] `rig status` drift for `agent_hooks` is surfaced proactively (not just when someone
      thinks to run `rig status`) — e.g. visible at Claude Code SessionStart.

## User impact

Every agent-hook shipped today (block-no-verify, block-raw-pr-merge, worktree-only-writes,
block-reset-hard, pin-primary-worktree, ...) has this same silent-lag risk on every future
change. Cost of inaction: guards that pass CI and get merged provide zero actual protection
until someone happens to notice and re-apply — which is exactly the class of incident this
issue documents happening 3 times in one day.

title: block-reset-hard: fail-closed bailout blocks prose mentions of the command, contradicting README's 'mentions are safe' claim
body:
## What's wrong

`block-reset-hard`'s own README explicitly promises: "text that merely **mentions** 'reset
--hard' or 'clean -fd' — a commit message, a code comment, a doc, a grep for the string —
parsed via real argv, never substring-matched" is safe and allowed through.

In practice, right after installing this hook live (2026-07-04, this session), a `tg
"<long multi-line report>"` call whose message body *quoted/discussed* the destructive
command in prose (as part of reporting on this very hook) was denied with:

```
block-reset-hard: could not verify this command is not a destructive `git reset --hard`/
`git clean -f...` (reset --hard) — blocking (fail-closed).
```

Tracing the source (`block_reset_hard.py`), this is the deliberate `fail-closed` path taken
when the parser can't confidently tokenize the command (unbalanced-quote detection, or the
`_WrapperOverflow` nesting cap) — see comments around lines 206, 234, 264, 314, 406, 504,
566. A long multi-line heredoc-style string argument (many embedded quotes/newlines, as a
`tg "..."` report naturally has) is exactly the shape that trips the parser's own
"can't reliably tokenize" bailout, and the bailout denies rather than allows.

This isn't necessarily wrong as a *default* (fail-closed is the documented, deliberate
design) — but it directly contradicts the specific claim in the hook's own README that
mentioning the phrase in prose/docs/commit messages is safe. In practice it means: any
agent trying to *report on this hook's own behavior* (docs, incident reports, tickets,
`tg` messages) in reasonably long/quoted text will get blocked, unless it avoids the
literal command shape entirely — a real ergonomic tax on the class of usage the README
says is fine.

## Repro

Run (adjust to any harness with the hook installed):

```
tg "some long multi-line message that quotes: 'git reset --hard' as prose, with several
embedded quotes and newlines elsewhere in the same string"
```

vs. a short single-line mention, which correctly passes.

## Suggested fix (pick one, or document if intentional)

- If the fail-closed bailout is intentional for genuinely unparseable input, the error
  message should distinguish "I could not parse your command" from "you're running a
  destructive reset" — right now both read identically, which reads as a false accusation
  when the actual command is an unrelated `tg`/`echo`/`gh issue create` call.
- Consider recognizing a very common shape — a single command whose *entire* remaining
  argv is one quoted string literal passed to a non-git binary (`tg`, `echo`, `cat <<EOF`)
  — as parseable-and-safe rather than falling into the nesting/quote-balance bailout,
  since the reset/clean detection only matters for the *outer* shell command, not prose
  inside an opaque string argument to another program.
- At minimum, document this false-positive class in the README so agents know to reach
  for `--body-file`/a temp file instead of inlining a long report as a literal argv string
  when discussing this hook.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `tg`/similar call whose sole destructive-sounding content is prose *inside* a
      quoted string argument to a non-git command no longer fail-closed-blocks, OR the
      denial message clearly says "could not parse, not "detected a destructive reset",
      so it's not mistaken for an actual policy violation.
- [ ] README's "mentions are safe" claim matches actual behavior for realistic multi-line
      report text, or the claim is narrowed to say what it actually guarantees.

## User impact

Every agent reporting on an incident involving this hook (like the current one,
agent-tools#186) hits this immediately — the tool built to make incidents visible instead
makes discussing them harder. Low severity (workaround exists: shorter messages / files),
but it directly contradicts a documented safety property of a security-relevant hook.

title: Replace self-service escape hatches in pin-primary-worktree & block-reset-hard with a deny-by-default external-approval gate (tg#6554)
body:
## Problem

Two `pre-bash` safety hooks — `pin-primary-worktree` and `block-reset-hard` — each shipped a **self-service escape hatch that the very agent the hook is meant to constrain could set on itself**:

- `pin-primary-worktree`: `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT` (env AND an inline `VAR=val` prefix on the offending command).
- `block-reset-hard`: `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD` (env) AND an inline `# no-reset-guard: <reason>` sentinel.

Either way the agent authoring the very command being checked could flip the bypass — security theater, not a permission gate (Alex tg#6554).

## User impact of not fixing

A destructive-action guard whose bypass the constrained agent can self-grant provides no real protection: a confused or misdirected agent that "decides" it needs the exception just sets the flag on its own command. The guard only stops the accidental case it happens to not route around.

## What to build

Replace the self-set bypass with a real external-approval extension point that **defaults to deny**:

- New shared `rig.yaml` convention `agent_hooks.approval_cmd` (+ optional `approval_cmd_timeout_s`) — a committed, code-reviewed shell command, deliberately NOT an env var.
- Unconfigured → deny (no subprocess). Configured → run it; allow only on exit 0; nonzero/error/timeout → deny, resolved inside the approval function so it never falls through to the hook's own `on_error`.
- Context (`RIG_APPROVAL_HOOK/KIND/TARGET/CWD/COMMAND`) passed as env vars, never string-interpolated.
- Remove the old env/inline hatches entirely; keep the incident-history docs.
- Bump the manifest `timeout_ms` to give the internal approval timeout headroom; clamp the effective approval timeout under the manifest budget so a misconfig can't become a silent allow (pin is `on_error: open`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Old env + inline bypasses are dead (regression tests: still BLOCK for both hooks).
- [ ] Unconfigured → deny, no subprocess spawned.
- [ ] `approval_cmd` exit-0 → allow; nonzero → block; timeout → block.
- [ ] Approval context reaches the command via `RIG_APPROVAL_*` env (trust-boundary test).
- [ ] Full `pytest tests/` stays green; ruff clean; SYNC copies byte-identical across the two hooks.

## Notes / provenance

Origin: Alex tg#6554. A genuinely unforgeable synchronous "ask Alex on Telegram and wait" approver must live inside `tg-ctl` (out of scope here) — tracked separately in the `tg-cli` repo; `approval_cmd` is the wiring point for it once it exists.

title: New universal skill: message-scope-verification
body:
## What

Alex (tg#6682): a message about an unrelated VS Code-extension task landed in the wrong agent pane/session; rather than assign blame, he asked for a durable, harness-agnostic instruction so any agent checks whether an inbound message is actually on-topic before abandoning unfinished work for it, and asks the user to confirm if it looks misdirected.

title: README.md Inventory section counts are stale (agent-hooks, CI slots)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
A code-review pass on an unrelated skill-addition PR (agent-tools#190) noticed these two Inventory counts are stale — pre-existing drift, not introduced by that PR, so left out of its diff to keep it minimal (per smallest-change discipline), but noted here so it doesn't get lost.

## User impact
A stale inventory count in the README undersells the catalog to anyone skimming it (8 agent-hooks vs 22 real ones is a 2.75x undercount) and erodes trust in the doc once a reader notices one wrong number.

## Cost of inaction
The gap keeps widening every time a hook/CI-gate is added without a matching README bump, same as just happened with the universal-skills count (39 vs the real 45) fixed in #190.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] README.md's Inventory section 'Agent-hooks: 8' matches the actual agent-hooks/ directory count (currently 22 per git ls-tree).

title: fix(agent-hooks): block-reset-hard unparseable fallback over-triggers on prose naming the guard
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Found live in agent-tools#197. A gh pr create command using a heredoc-based body was blocked by the reset-hard guard fail-closed unparseable path. Root cause: the heredoc body had enough embedded quotes and backticks that the whole multi-line command failed the shlex tokenizer, and the fallback hint regex is a loose DOTALL pattern that only requires the words git, reset, and hard to appear anywhere in that order. The PR body text named the guard hook itself, which alone satisfied the pattern, with zero actual destructive git command anywhere in the real command. Workaround used: write the body to a file and pass it via a file flag instead of an inline heredoc.

## User impact
Any agent writing a PR description, issue comment, or commit message in this repo that discusses git safety hooks by name, which is common here since this repo documents those hooks, can get its command silently fail-closed blocked for no real destructive-git reason, forcing a non-obvious workaround.

## Cost of inaction
Agents keep hitting this confusing false positive whenever they document or reference this hook family inside an inline heredoc body, with no guidance pointing at the workaround.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A gh pr create or gh issue comment command whose body text merely discusses git safety hooks (mentions the guard by name, or writes an example destructive git invocation as prose) but contains no real dangerous git invocation does not fail closed, even when embedded quotes make the overall command unparseable by shlex

title: fix(agent-hooks): visual-proof-gate effective_cwd() cd-detection misses parenthesized subshell form
body:
## What
`effective_cwd()` in `agent-hooks/visual-proof-gate/visual_proof_gate.py` detects a leading `cd <dir>` segment via `seg[0] == "cd"`. For the very common parenthesized-subshell idiom `(cd <worktree> && git commit ...)`, `shlex.split` glues the opening paren onto the word — the first token is literally `"(cd"`, never `"cd"` — so this check never matches. `effective_cwd()` then falls back to `session_cwd` instead of the actual repo the commit runs in.

Confirmed via direct repro:
```
>>> import shlex
>>> shlex.split("(cd repoB && git commit -m x)", comments=True)
['(cd', 'repoB', '&&', 'git', 'commit', '-m', 'x)']
```

Flagged in PR #176 review (chatgpt-codex-connector, P2): "When the command uses the common subshell form `(cd <worktree> && git commit ...)`, `shlex.split` leaves the first command token as `(cd`, so this branch never records the directory change and `main()` checks `event.cwd` instead of the repo where the commit runs."

## Why (motivation)
PR #176 fixed `effective_cwd()`'s bare `cd <dir> && git commit` / `git -C <dir> commit` cases, but the fix's own `cd`-detection check doesn't account for shlex's tokenization of a leading `(`. Caught by automated PR review before merge; fixing as a same-PR fixup rather than a separate follow-up since the PR isn't merged yet.

## User impact
An agent session rooted in repo A can run `(cd repoB && git commit -m x)` with staged `.tsx`/UI changes in repo B — the gate checks repo A (clean, no UI changes) and ALLOWS, silently bypassing the mandatory screenshot-proof requirement for the actual repo (B) where the UI change is being committed. This is a real bypass of the visual-proof-cycle doctrine via an extremely common shell idiom (subshelling a `cd` so it doesn't leak into the caller's shell).

## Cost of inaction
Any `(cd ... && git commit ...)` workflow silently bypasses the visual-proof gate for the real target repo; UI commits in a subshell-`cd`'d repo land unproven with no error or warning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `effective_cwd()`'s `cd`-detection recognizes a leading shell-grouping marker (`(`) whether glued to the token (`(cd`) or its own standalone token (`( cd`), and still correctly resolves the real cd target
- [ ] unit tests cover: glued `(cd repoB && git commit ...)`, spaced `( cd repoB && git commit ... )`, and a regression check that the existing bare `cd repoB && git commit` (no parens) still resolves correctly
- [ ] full pytest suite green

## Screenshots
(none - pure backend/CLI hook logic fix, no user-visible UI surface to screenshot)

## Links
- PR: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/176
- Review comment thread: chatgpt-codex-connector, P2, on visual_proof_gate.py
- Related: #172, #173 (same shlex-gluing tokenization family, different specific gaps)

title: skills-read-gate / visual-proof-gate: is_skip_commit allowlist misses other value-consuming git-commit flags (post-#197 --trailer fix)
body:
## What

`_takes_following_value()` in both `agent-hooks/skills-read-gate/skills_read_gate.py` and
`agent-hooks/visual-proof-gate/visual_proof_gate.py` (mirrored parsers, PR #197 just added
`--trailer` to the checked set) only recognizes `--message`/`--file`/`--trailer` as long-form
flags that consume a following token as their VALUE. But `git commit` also consumes the next
token unconditionally for several other flags: `--author`, `--date`, `-C`/`--reuse-message`,
`-c`/`--reedit-message`, `--fixup`, `--squash`, `--cleanup`, `--pathspec-from-file`, `-t`/`--template`.
If that following value happens to be a literal `--skip`/`--abort`/`--continue`, the SAME class
of leak as the just-fixed `--trailer` bug occurs: the value token isn't stripped, leaks into
`_commit_flags()`'s output, and `is_skip_commit()`'s `any(tok in SKIP_FLAGS ...)` check wrongly
matches it.

Example (single segment): `git commit --author --skip -m x` → `_commit_flags` → `[--author,
--skip]` → `is_skip_commit == True` → the mandatory-skills-read / visual-proof gate is wrongly
skipped for what should be a real, gated commit.

## Why (motivation)

Surfaced by two independent reviewers (opus + codex, `review diff` on PR #197's --trailer fix)
during the multi-model review of that fix. Both flagged that the allowlist covers only
`--trailer`, and the same structural gap exists for the other value-consuming flags. Precedent:
this exact class was already found and fixed for the *different* `require_ticket_before_commit.py`
hook in agent-tools#114 (missing flags) and agent-tools#120 (abbreviation handling) -- these two
hooks (`skills_read_gate.py`/`visual_proof_gate.py`) share the SYNC-comment-linked parser but
never got the equivalent full-allowlist treatment.

## Mitigating analysis (important -- NOT a live exploitable bypass today)

Per opus's review: for every flag in the list above except `--trailer`, `--skip`/`--abort`/
`--continue` is NOT a valid value -- `git` itself rejects the commit before it's created:
- `--author --skip` -- invalid author format, git errors.
- `-c/--reedit-message --skip`, `-C/--reuse-message --skip` -- not a valid commit-ish, git errors.
- `--cleanus --skip` -- invalid `--cleanup` enum value, git errors.
- `--pathspec-from-file --skip` -- no such file (almost certainly), git errors.
- `-t/--template --skip` -- no such template file, git errors.

So today this is a **parser-consistency gap, not a committable bypass** -- unlike `--trailer`,
whose value is arbitrary free text git happily accepts, these all fail downstream in real git
before any commit is authored. Low severity; tracked here so it doesn't silently regress if any
future flag gets an arbitrary-value acceptance (or if the hook's classification is ever used for
something other than "did a git commit actually succeed").

## User impact

None currently exploitable (see mitigating analysis) -- an agent trying `git commit --author
--skip -m "real change"` gets a git error, not a silently-skipped-gate commit. If this ever
becomes exploitable (e.g. a future flag with a git-accepted arbitrary value, mirroring
`--trailer`), the mandatory-skills-read / visual-proof gates could be silently bypassed on a
real commit.

## Cost of inaction

The allowlist stays structurally incomplete; low current risk, but the same story that led to
the `--trailer` bug (an unlisted value-consuming flag) can repeat for any future git-commit flag
addition, and this repo has already independently rediscovered variants of this exact class
twice for the sibling hook (#114, #120).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the fix shape: full allowlist (mirror #114/#120's approach: `--author`, `--date`,
      `--cleanup`, `--pathspec-from-file`, `-t`/`--template`, `-C`/`--reuse-message`,
      `-c`/`--reedit-message`, `--fixup`, `--squash`) vs. documented-limitation-only, in BOTH
      `skills_read_gate.py` and `visual_proof_gate.py` (kept in step per their SYNC comment).
- [ ] If full allowlist: add tests pinning at least one path-valued long flag (e.g.
      `--pathspec-from-file --skip -m x`) and one short next-token flag (`-c --skip -m x`) in
      both hook test suites, mirroring the #114/#120 test shapes already proven for
      `require_ticket_before_commit.py`.
- [ ] If documented-limitation-only: add an explicit comment + a boundary test (clearly named,
      e.g. `test_KNOWN_GAP_*`, referencing this issue number) so a future full-allowlist fix
      doesn't look like an unexpected regression when it flips that test.

## Screenshots

(none)

## Links

- PR: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/197
- Related: agent-tools#174 (the sibling chain-bypass bug in the same file), agent-tools#114 and
  agent-tools#120 (the identical value-flag-allowlist class, already fixed for the sibling

title: feat(watchdog): tiered stall detection for background subagents
body:
## What
A reusable Python module + CLI (agenttools_stall_watchdog under lib) that polls a background Claude Code subagent's transcript file mtime and fires two tiers on inactivity: a Tier-1 warning (default 5 min stale) delivered via tmux pane injection to the orchestrating pane plus a Telegram alert, and a Tier-2 abort (default 30 min stale) that force-kills the process when a PID is known, and otherwise prints and alerts an explicit abort recommendation with the exact diagnostic pointer (transcript path, stat/tail commands, SendMessage/TaskStop hint) since an in-session Agent-tool subagent has no externally-killable PID.

## Why (motivation)
Per Alex's direct feedback (tg message #6942): a background subagent sat stalled for about 2 hours because the orchestrator was only checking manually every 20-30 minutes via ScheduleWakeup. He asked for both the harness and the process to be fixed so that after 5 minutes of no progress a warning fires automatically, and after 30 minutes the run is aborted with a pointer to full diagnostics, instead of relying on a human or orchestrator remembering to poll.

## User impact
Alex (and any orchestrator agent supervising background subagents) gets an automatic, timely alert instead of discovering a stall hours later by accident; stuck runs stop silently burning wall-clock time and compute.

## Cost of inaction
The orchestrator keeps relying on manual ScheduleWakeup polling every 20 to 30 minutes, so a hung subagent, for example one stuck on a blocking call with no timeout wrapper, can silently burn hours before anyone notices, as already happened once.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tier-1, default 300 seconds and configurable, of mtime staleness on the watched transcript fires exactly once per stall episode: prints a WARN line that a Monitor tool can consume, and best-effort tmux-injects plus Telegram-alerts a nudge naming the transcript path
- [ ] Tier-2, default 1800 seconds and configurable, fires exactly once per stall episode: prints an ABORT line, sends SIGTERM then escalates to SIGKILL when a pid argument is supplied and still alive, and always sends a Telegram alert plus prints the exact diagnostic pointer, transcript path plus stat and tail commands plus a SendMessage or TaskStop hint, even when no pid is killable
- [ ] Progress resuming, meaning the mtime advances again, after a WARN resets internal state so a later stall re-fires WARN or ABORT instead of staying silent forever
- [ ] Unit tests cover the pure classify and poll logic with an injected fake clock and fake mtime source with no real sleeps; a live smoke test with scaled down thresholds around 10 and 30 seconds against a real dummy stalled process proves both tiers fire in practice
- [ ] Scope covers any long-running process's output/log file, not only a subagent transcript: an e2e/Playwright suite, npm test, or Electron-launch log, watched by the same --watch-file flag (--transcript kept as a backward-compatible alias)
- [ ] Tier-1 WARN is delivered ONLY via tmux pane injection into the watching agent/orchestrator's own pane, in English (agent-facing signal); it must NOT reach Alex over Telegram by default. Tier-2 ABORT additionally sends a Russian, explicit-field alert to Alex over the tg CLI (what is stuck, how long idle, what the watchdog did, where to find diagnostics, what to do), abort-tier only unless --tg-on-warn is passed
- [ ] Production default thresholds are exactly 5 minutes (warn) and 30 minutes (abort), matching Alex's original request verbatim; any invocation with scaled-down thresholds for testing must pass --test so every alert states the exact test threshold used plus a note that the production default is 5m/30m

title: Verify stall-watchdog fires under a simulated stall
body:
## What

title: stall-watchdog: tmux nudge is not shell-safe if --tmux-target ever points at a raw shell
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Found live while writing an end-to-end integration test for agenttools_stall_watchdog ([issue #209](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/209)): pointing --tmux-target at a plain zsh pane (instead of an agent's REPL) causes the injected nudge to be parsed as a shell command line, not just displayed.

## User impact
If an operator ever wires --tmux-target to the wrong pane (a shell instead of the intended agent session), the watchdog's own alert becomes visible shell noise/errors instead of a readable nudge, and depending on the message field contents this is a latent command-injection-shaped surface, not just a cosmetic one.

## Cost of inaction
The assumption 'tmux-target is always a live agent REPL' stays undocumented and untested; a future misconfiguration silently degrades the one thing this tool exists to make reliable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Document (or fix) that build_nudge_line's output contains unescaped shell metacharacters (e.g. literal '[stall-watchdog]' brackets) which, when injected via tmux send-keys + Enter into a pane that is a bare shell prompt (not an agent REPL), get parsed and partially executed by that shell (observed: 'zsh: bad pattern: [test-only', 'zsh: command not found: check'), fragmenting/mangling the visible message.
- [ ] Either the watch CLI's docs explicitly warn --tmux-target must be a live agent REPL, never a raw shell prompt, or build_nudge_line's payload is made shell-parse-safe (e.g. avoiding bare brackets) so a misrouted target degrades to a garbled-but-harmless line instead of shell errors.

title: Harden hatch escalation: self-sufficient timeout below CC 600s default + multi-segment single-ask cap
body:
## What
Follow-up findings from the review of [#200](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/200) (the two P2/High-class items not fixed in the merge, which only added a 30s descriptor headroom over the 930s helper worst case). Two residuals remain in agenttools_hatch_escalation and the two hooks that use it. First, Claude Code's own command-hook timeout defaults to 600s, BELOW the helper's 930s worst case and the 960000ms descriptor budget. If the live settings or rig-cli hook_bridge_entries register cc_hook_bridge without a timeout above 960s, CC kills the bridge at 600s before the helper returns, so the descriptor on_error path never runs and CC's own expired-hook behavior decides the outcome. Verify empirically whether CC blocks or allows an expired PreToolUse hook; if it allows, both hooks are bypassable by simply setting RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* and waiting about 600s. Mitigation: make the helper self-sufficient by capping its tg-ctl timeout below CC's 600s default (e.g. 540s) so an unanswered ask resolves to an explicit deny inside the bridge regardless of settings, and land the settings or rig-cli timeout raise as part of rig apply. Second, a chained command with the hatch env set makes one up-to-900s ask PER dangerous or gate-worthy segment (the hatch path is deliberately not bounded by the 10s _MAIN_LOOP_BUDGET_S), so N segments can sum past the descriptor budget; for pin-primary-worktree (on_error=open) a bridge kill mid-chain silently allows the remaining segments. Fix by the existing approval_cmd pattern: allow at most one hatch ask per invocation and deny subsequent gate-worthy segments with the existing split-into-separate-Bash-calls message. Also fold in the Gemini doc-clarity nits (context value-type contract in request_hatch_approval docstring; realpath resolution of rig.yaml tg_ctl_path; README note that the aggregate approval_cmd budget is not reset by a long hatch wait). This is the same class as the residual timing gap already tracked in [#204](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/204) and part of the broader hatch rework in [#213](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/213).

## Why (motivation)
The merge of [#200](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/200) fixed the equal-timeout race (added 30s descriptor headroom) but the multi-model review surfaced two deeper residuals: the CC 600s default preemption and the unbounded multi-segment hatch asks. Both were left out of the merge to avoid injecting unreviewed code and restarting the review loop; they must not be lost.

## User impact
Until closed, an agent under pin-primary-worktree or block-reset-hard can still, in narrow but real conditions (CC settings timeout not raised above 960s, or a multi-segment chained command with the hatch env set), race the hook into a silent allow of a primary-worktree checkout or a git reset --hard or clean -f, defeating the exact guard the hatch escalation exists to enforce.

## Cost of inaction
The self-sufficiency gap and the multi-segment fail-open stay live; the hatch escalation guarantees hold only when an operator has separately raised the CC settings hook timeout above 960s and never uses chained gate-worthy commands with the env set, an unenforced precondition, precisely the kind of implicit assumption tg#6554 warned against.

> **tg#6554** — Alex, 2026-07-04 16:46 UTC: RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 такой паттерн надо запретить Можно добавить некий request либо в виде env var либо как-то ещё И ес…
<!-- tasklib:msgref-quote:6554 -->

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Helper's effective tg-ctl timeout is capped below Claude Code's 600s default command-hook timeout, or the settings and rig-cli timeout raise above 960s is landed and verified, so an unanswered hatch ask resolves to a deny inside the bridge regardless of external CC settings; verified against CC's actual expired-hook behavior
- [ ] A chained command with the hatch env set makes at most one hatch ask per hook invocation; every subsequent gate-worthy segment denies with the split-into-separate-Bash-calls message, with a regression test covering approved-then-unapproved and unapproved-then-approved multi-segment chains for both hooks

title: ship.sh hatch helper audit+tg not guarded under --dry-run
body:
## What
[PR #225](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/225) ([ticket #224](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/224)) added the review-quorum Guard-B gate to [ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh). During its merge a P2 was fixed: `_review_quorum_audit_log` wrote to SHIP_AUDIT_FILE even under `--dry-run`, violating the "dry-run changes nothing" contract (fixed in [commit 60bfc40](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/commit/60bfc40) with a DRY_RUN=1 guard + regression test). The remaining gap: the python hatch helper [ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py) writes its OWN `bypass:approved`/`bypass:denied` audit line AND sends a live Telegram via tg-ctl. That path is NOT dry-run-guarded. It only fires when RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM is explicitly set, so a `--dry-run` invocation that also sets the hatch-request env would still send a real TG to Alex and append a real audit line.

## Why (motivation)
The `--dry-run` contract for ship.sh is that it changes nothing and produces no side effects. The main audit-log path was guarded in [60bfc40](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/commit/60bfc40), but the hatch helper's own audit write + live Telegram send were left unguarded, so the invariant is only half-enforced.

## User impact
A dry-run that is supposed to be side-effect-free can spam Alex with a live approval request over Telegram and mutate the ship audit log, making dry-run unsafe to use for validation.

## Cost of inaction
The "dry-run is safe" invariant that the Guard-B gate itself relies on stays eroded; anyone testing ship.sh with --dry-run plus the hatch-request env silently fires real side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

title: Decide handling of shell-layer bypasses: GLOBAL_HOOKS_SKIP + review-gate $REVIEW_SKIP (follow-up to #213)
body:
Follow-up to #213 (PRs #231/#232/#233 converted the 11 **Python** agent-hooks to `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` live approval). Two **shell-layer** bypasses remain and were deliberately NOT blind-converted, because a synchronous `tg-ctl` Telegram approval is the wrong mechanism for a git-hook/dispatcher that runs on every git operation. They need a design decision.

## 1. `GLOBAL_HOOKS_SKIP` (item #12 in #213) — `git-hooks/global-dispatcher/run-global-hooks`
The ticket labeled this a "blanket kill-switch", but the actual mechanism is narrower than assumed:
- `is_skipped()` (run-global-hooks ~L209) already **ignores** env `GLOBAL_HOOKS_SKIP` for **PROTECTED** fragments (`# global-hook-protected: true`, e.g. secret-scan). So safety-critical global hooks are already immune to the agent self-granting via this env var.
- It only skips **UNPROTECTED** convenience fragments (formatters/lint), where skipping is a convenience, not a safety bypass.
- It runs in a POSIX-sh dispatcher on **every git operation in every repo**, with no per-invocation approval contract. Wiring a blocking `tg-ctl ask` (up to 900s) into that path would be an unacceptable UX/architecture change.

**Options:** (a) leave as-is (protected fragments already covered; document that unprotected skips are non-safety); (b) require `hooks.skipGlobal` git-config (already the trusted, non-repo-injectable path) and drop the env var entirely; (c) something else. Recommend (a) or (b), not a Telegram conversion.

## 2. `review-gate` `$REVIEW_SKIP` — `git-hooks/global-dispatcher/hooks/review-gate`
A **separate, surviving** mechanism from the agent-hook `require-review-before-commit` converted in #231. This is a git pre-commit fragment that does `[ -n \"\$REVIEW_SKIP\" ] && exit 0`. Same category as #1: a shell git-hook, not an agent pre-bash hook with a `tg-ctl` contract. Also referenced in `git-hooks/global-dispatcher/hooks/pre-commit` and `.../global-hooks.d/pre-commit/10-secret-scan` docs.

**Options:** same shape as #1 — decide whether shell git-hook bypasses should route through git-config/protected-fragment discipline vs. a self-service env var, consistently with #1.

Both are process-discipline/git-hook-layer, distinct from the agent-hook `cc_hook_bridge` layer where the `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` mechanism lives. Filing so the #213 "convert every hatch" scope is honestly closed with these two explicitly triaged rather than silently dropped.

title: block-raw-pr-merge: multiline commands (bare newline / comment / heredoc) evade or over-block segment detection
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
block-raw-pr-merge tokenizes via shlex which treats a bare newline as whitespace (not a command separator), so a multiline echo-then-merge collapses into one echo-headed segment and the raw merge on line 2 evades the gate. A naive newline-to-semicolon normalization (attempted in the hatch stack, then reverted) introduced a WORSE bug: it broke shlex hash-comment termination (comment-before-newline swallows the merge) and mis-parsed heredoc bodies (false-positive block). A correct fix needs real shell-structure parsing (comments, heredocs, quotes), out of scope for the hatch escape-hatch PRs. See PRs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/231 (codex review that surfaced this).

## User impact
An agent could bypass the raw-merge block with a two-line command (defense-in-depth only: branch protection and the session-level block-gh-pr-merge.sh remain), and unusual heredoc/comment commands can be mis-handled. Pre-existing behavior (shlex always treated newlines as whitespace).

## Cost of inaction
The multiline bypass persists as a latent defense-in-depth gap and any future newline-normalization attempt risks re-introducing the comment/heredoc bugs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A bare-newline-separated gh pr merge on line 2 is BLOCKED (multiline echo then merge). — forced: Verified on origin/main/current checkout: tests/test_block_raw_pr_merge.py::test_bare_newline_second_line_merge_is_detected passed in the focused pytest run; full tests/test_block_raw_pr_merge.py -> 163 passed.

title: Harden agent-hook hatch-lib import: unify all 5 hooks on spec_from_file_location + isolated interpreter
body:
Follow-up hygiene from the #231 fresh codex review (task 213). NOT a blocker for #231/#232/#233.

**Finding (codex, iteration 12 on #231 current diff):** The hatch-enabled agent-hooks import the shared approval lib by name after a conditional sys.path insert:

```python
sys.path.insert(0, str(_LIB_DIR))
import agenttools_hatch_escalation as hatch_escalation
```

This is the PYTHONPATH-hijack shape the ship gate (`ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py`) already hardens against with `spec_from_file_location` + `python3 -I`. If a malicious same-named module were preloaded (sitecustomize/usercustomize) it could return an approved hatch.

**Why NOT a #231 blocker (adjudicated by a 2nd model):**
- The convention is pre-existing and identical in already-merged hooks `block-reset-hard` and `pin-primary-worktree` (#218); #231 only extends it to 3 more hooks (block-raw-pr-merge, require-review-before-commit, decision-request-format). No new vulnerability class.
- Low reachability: hook subprocesses inherit the harness environment, not the agent command's inline env, so a guarded agent cannot set PYTHONPATH for a hook process it does not spawn. Poisoning requires writing sitecustomize/usercustomize into the interpreter site dir (high bar).
- The actual merge-authority gate (ship review_quorum_hatch) is already hardened.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. All 5 hatch-enabled agent-hooks load `agenttools_hatch_escalation` via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` from the exact file path (mirroring review_quorum_hatch.py), replacing the by-name import.
2. A regression test per hook mirroring `test_hatch_helper_import_resists_pythonpath_hijack` (a preloaded same-named module must NOT be able to approve).

**Impact if not done:** defense-in-depth inconsistency; the pre-bash guard hooks remain theoretically hijackable via a site-dir write, unlike the hardened ship gate.

Refs #213 #218 #231

title: Guard B ship review-quorum gate authorizes on a 0/0 quorum read (latent bypass)
body:
## What
The ci/ship/ship.sh review-quorum gate (Guard B, from PR #225) is supposed to refuse a self-merge unless >=3 passed review iterations across >=3 distinct models are recorded. On 2026-07-10, while shipping review-cli PR #141 (task GH-139), the `gh ship` subprocess printed `review quorum met: 0 iterations across 0 models` and STILL AUTHORIZED the merge — i.e. its in-subprocess quorum counter resolved to 0/0 and the gate passed anyway. The gate must FAIL CLOSED: 0 iterations / 0 models means quorum NOT met, never met.

Why it is a real hole: an independent `review task GH-139 --check` in the same session correctly returned exit 0 / passed=true with 3 genuine distinct models (codex, claude-opus-4-8, gemini-3.5-flash), so THAT particular merge was legitimate. But a gate that prints "0 iterations across 0 models" and authorizes means the min-floor/threshold resolved to 0 in the ship subprocess environment — so a PR with a genuinely EMPTY quorum (0 real reviews) could also pass. That defeats the entire >=3x3 self-merge bar the gate exists to enforce.

Likely cause to investigate: in the `gh ship` subprocess, the quorum check's min-iter/min-models floor is resolving to 0 (env/arg/task-code-derivation difference between the ship subprocess and a direct `review task --check`), or the stats-store path/task-code the subprocess reads differs from the one the reviews were recorded under.

Relates to the review-quorum gate from PR #225 (agent-tools) and the verdict-mode fix PR #138 (review-cli, merged). Fix must be coordinated with the in-flight codex gate-hardening (PRs #241/#236/#237) to avoid conflicts.

## Why (motivation)
Alex mandated a >=3 passed review iterations across >=3 distinct models bar before an agent may self-merge (Guard B). A gate that authorizes on a 0/0 read makes that bar bypassable and hollow.

## User impact
Agents can self-merge with a hollow/empty review quorum — the >=3-model self-merge bar is bypassable whenever the ship subprocess reads 0/0, so unreviewed code can land on main under an agent's own authority.

## Cost of inaction
The whole Guard B self-merge safety guarantee is illusory in the environments where the floor reads 0; unreviewed self-merges can slip through undetected.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The ship-gate quorum check fails closed when it reads 0 iterations OR 0 distinct models (0/0 -> refuse, never authorize).
- [ ] The min-iter/min-models floor cannot silently resolve to 0 in the ship subprocess: assert a hard minimum >=3, or refuse if the floor is unset/0.
- [ ] Regression test: a ship invocation whose quorum store shows 0 iterations for the task code is REFUSED.

title: cc_hook_bridge format-on-write hook reformats foreign-style repos, ballooning diffs
body:
## What
The global PostToolUse format-on-write hook (cc_hook_bridge, PYTHONPATH=/Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools/lib) auto-runs a formatter (ruff format / equivalent) on every [Edit/Write](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools) tool call. It applies ONE global formatter config regardless of the target repo's own style config (its own ruff / line-length / pyproject settings). In repos whose existing style differs from the hook's configured settings, a 1-word or 1-line change balloons into a huge whole-file reformat. It should either honor the target repo's formatter config, format only the changed hunks/lines, or be scoped to repos that opted in.

## Why (motivation)
Observed repeatedly on 2026-07-09/10 across multiple agents working in [alex-mextner/review-cli](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli): a 1-word model-id change turned into a 682-line reformat, and the verdict [PR #138](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/138) agent hit ~1450 lines of whitespace churn. Agents were forced to route edits via raw Bash/python to keep diffs surgical.

## User impact
Every agent editing a repo whose style differs from the global hook config either ships a bloated, unreadable diff or wastes cycles on fragile Bash edit-workarounds (bypassing the editor tool). Recurring drag observed across ~4 agents in one session. It can also silently reformat unrelated code, muddying blame and risking accidental style flips on files the change never intended to touch.

## Cost of inaction
Continued unreadable review diffs and huge PRs for trivial changes, fragile agent Bash edit-workarounds, and risk of silent style flips in unrelated code (muddied blame).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The format-on-write hook respects the target repo's own formatter configuration (pyproject.toml / ruff.toml / .editorconfig) instead of a single global style.
- [ ] Alternatively/additionally, format only the edited region, not the whole file.
- [ ] A repo with a divergent style no longer gets whole-file reformats from a one-line edit.

title: block-raw-pr-merge: backtick command-substitution merge bypass (pre-existing)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
While fixing the bare-newline evasion in block-raw-pr-merge (PR #247), Codex confirmed a separate PRE-EXISTING bypass on main: a raw PR merge wrapped in backtick command substitution — `gh pr merge 1 --admin` — is NOT detected by the block hook, so it sails past the gate with no approval. Note: $(...) command substitution IS detected via the '(' split; only the backtick form is missed. Scope: this predates PR #247's diff and is out of scope for that PR (which fixes bare-newline tokenization). Filing separately so it's tracked. Reference PR #247 (bare-newline fix) and the gh-api bypass work (hyperide HYP-960).

An agent can bypass the raw-merge guard (skipping gh ship's proof gates) by wrapping the merge in backticks — the same class of hole #242/#247/HYP-960 are closing on other vectors.

## Cost of inaction
The merge-discipline gate has a known open bypass vector that an agent can use to merge PRs without the proof/approval gates.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The block-raw-pr-merge hook detects a 'gh pr merge' inside backtick command substitution the same way it detects $(...) substitution, and also covers the 'gh api' merge routes.
- [ ] Add a regression test: a backtick-wrapped merge (`gh pr merge 1`) is blocked, while a benign backtick command is not blocked. Keep it fail-closed and avoid false-positives on unrelated backtick usage.

comments.body: Related variant (same class): a raw merge inside a command substitution wrapped in DOUBLE QUOTES — `echo "$(gh pr merge 1 --admin)"` — is also missed by block-raw-pr-merge. A real shell executes the `$(...)` even inside double quotes, but the scanner keeps the double-quoted content as a single literal token and never inspects it. Flagged during PR #247's review (claude-opus). Acceptance for this issue should cover BOTH the backtick form and the double-quoted `"$(...)"` command-substitution form — detect a `gh pr merge` / gh-api-merge / mergePullRequest invocation inside command substitution regardless of surrounding single/double quotes or backticks, with a regression test for each, kept fail-closed and without false-positives on benign command-substitution.

## Why (motivation)

title: ship.sh CI gate: dedup statusCheckRollup to latest-run-per-check (stale PR Checklist FAILURE wrongly blocks)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Guard B ship gate counts EVERY statusCheckRollup entry without deduping by check name. GitHub keeps multiple entries per check when a workflow re-runs; the PR Checklist gate reads the historical pull_request.body, so stale FAILURE runs linger after acceptance boxes are checked. ship.sh refuses even when GitHub reports mergeStateStatus=CLEAN. Sibling of the review-threads-stale family.

## User impact
A developer whose PR is actually green (GitHub shows it mergeable) cannot ship it: gh ship keeps refusing because of an old failed check run that already passed on re-run. Re-running the check does not help and only makes it worse, so their PR and the release it belongs to stay stuck with no clear way out.

## Cost of inaction
The extension release stays blocked; any PR whose PR Checklist gate re-ran becomes un-shippable via gh ship

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ship.sh CI gate groups statusCheckRollup by check name/context and evaluates only the LATEST run per check
- [ ] A check with an old FAILURE + newer SUCCESS is treated as passing; a check whose latest run is FAILURE still blocks; adversarial revert of the dedup re-breaks the stale-pass case

title: ship.sh CI gate: statusCheckRollup is capped at contexts(first:100), no pagination (fail-open on >100 checks)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup emits contexts(first:100) with no pagination. On a PR with many checks or many historical re-runs, checks after entry 100 never reach the CI gate's dedup/FAILED evaluation, so a failing check can be silently omitted and the merge permitted. Pre-existing (independent of the latest-run dedup in #260); flagged by review (Sol P1).

## User impact
A developer on a PR with more than 100 check entries (easy to hit once workflows re-run several times) could have gh ship merge it even though one of the checks is actually red, because that check fell off the first page and the gate never saw it. The merge looks safe but shipped on a red check.

## Cost of inaction
The green-CI gate has a fail-open hole on large/rerun-heavy PRs; a red check can slip through gh ship undetected

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ship.sh fetches ALL statusCheckRollup contexts via a paginated GraphQL query (not gh pr view's un-paginated contexts(first:100))
- [ ] A failing check beyond the first 100 rollup entries blocks the merge; a >100-context regression test proves it; fetch fails closed on incomplete pagination

title: block-raw-pr-merge hook false-positives on resolveReviewThread/addPullRequestReviewThreadReply GraphQL mutations
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The hook currently refuses ANY gh api graphql mutation as a raw pr merge. Repro: gh api graphql -f query='mutation($t:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$t}){thread{isResolved}}}' -f t=<id> → blocked with the raw-pr-merge refusal. resolveReviewThread does not merge anything.

## User impact
gh ship refuses to merge while a PR has unresolved review threads and tells you to resolve them and re-run. An AGENT cannot satisfy that autonomously: the only API to resolve a thread is the resolveReviewThread mutation, which this hook blocks. So an agent that fixes a bot's review nit can push the fix but cannot resolve the thread, wedging the merge on a human click every time.

## Cost of inaction
Every ship that has a bot review thread (codex-connector P1/P2 nits are common) becomes a manual human step; agents cannot close out their own PRs even after addressing the feedback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The block-raw-pr-merge pre-bash hook only matches ACTUAL merge operations: gh pr merge (any flags incl --admin) and the mergePullRequest GraphQL mutation
- [ ] A gh api graphql call whose mutation is resolveReviewThread or addPullRequestReviewThreadReply (or any non-merge mutation) is NOT blocked; a regression test covers a resolveReviewThread call passing and a mergePullRequest call blocking

title: ship: empty statusCheckRollup on billing-blocked CI must run local gate, not fall through to ungated --admin merge
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Alex (~12x): billing-blocked CI often never enqueues workflows so statusCheckRollup is empty; ship then hard-refused and the only escape was --skip-ci (an --admin merge verifying nothing locally). The local-gate machinery existed but was unreachable for the most common outage shape.

## User impact
When CI is down for billing, whoever ships a PR can today only either not ship at all, or ship with every safety check skipped — no tests, no leftover scan, no review gate — and unreviewed code lands on main. Anyone relying on main being gated loses that guarantee exactly when CI is flaky, which Alex says will be often.

## Cost of inaction
Agents reach for --skip-ci every time CI is down (frequent), shipping becomes routinely ungated, unverified code lands on main, and the 'CI down is not a free pass' invariant stays broken.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Empty statusCheckRollup + repo HAS .github/workflows/*.yml on disk (CI configured but did not run = outage) => gh ship runs the local CI gate (tests + leftover scan + PR checklist + review threads) and merges only if ALL green
- [ ] Empty rollup + NO workflow files on disk => hard-refuse stands; foreign --repo still refuses (local gate is CWD-bound)
- [ ] Tests green: test_empty_rollup_ci_outage_local_gate_passes_merges / _fails_refuses / test_empty_rollup_no_workflows_still_refuses; suite 268 passed

title: pm-cli: autonomous PM-agent — Milestone 1 (event-sourced core + FSM)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Design in [research #255](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/docs/research/255-pm-agent-research.md) defines an autonomous PM coordinator over the task, tg and rig ecosystem; it needs a durable, replayable spine before any adapter or dispatch is built on top

## User impact
Alex gets a single durable queue that never loses an inbound request across crashes or restarts, and can see why any work item sits where it does — the foundation the intake-to-deploy tracking is built on

## Cost of inaction
Requests keep getting lost across sessions (the stale-session gap noted in [task-cli #50](https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/50)), and PM state has no crash-safe source of truth to reconcile against

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An append-only JSONL event log projects deterministically into a WorkItem queue: a crash or restart replays the log to the exact same projection (proven by test_replay_is_deterministic_across_reload)
- [ ] A configurable work-state FSM validates transitions and evidence gates before an event is written, so the log never holds an illegal move; illegal moves are rejected with a structured non-zero exit (proven by test_illegal_transition_is_rejected_at_write_time and test_evidence_gate_enforced_at_write_time)
- [ ] The pm commands run stdlib-only and pass ruff plus 27 pytest tests

title: pm-cli: Milestone 2 — task-cli adapter (intake to WorkItem projection)

## What

Alex gets his actual open tickets projected into the pm queue automatically, deduped, each tagged with a coarse pm stage and health, so nothing tracked in task-cli is invisible to the coordinator

- [ ] Each ingested ticket's task state maps to a pm state, its id is recorded as a task ref, and its url is captured as task-record evidence (proven by the adapter unit tests)

title: pm-cli: manual record intake task-ref does not dedupe against ingest qualified refs
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The M2 task adapter in [agent-tools 271](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/271) dedupes by a project-qualified ref (project plus ticket id), but manual record intake stores whatever task ref string the caller passed, so a bare ref and the qualified ref do not match

## User impact
When Alex hand-records a ticket and then runs pm ingest, the same piece of work appears twice in his queue, so his backlog counts and next-action view are wrong and he wastes time reconciling phantom duplicates

## Cost of inaction
The queue silently accumulates duplicate items whenever manual intake and adapter ingest touch the same ticket, eroding trust in every number pm reports

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A work item created by pm record intake with a bare ticket ref plus a project is matched by a later pm ingest of that same task-cli ticket, producing zero duplicate items

title: pm-cli: Milestone 3 — Telegram intake with a dead-letter queue
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The M2 task adapter (see [agent-tools 271](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/271)) reconciles durable tickets, but inbound Telegram requests have no durable capture and are the class of request that gets lost across sessions (the stale-session gap in [task-cli 50](https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/50)); the design in [research 255](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/docs/research/255-pm-agent-research.md) requires a dead-letter queue so no inbound request is silently dropped

## User impact
Every message Alex sends by Telegram is captured the instant pm sees it and can never vanish even if turning it into a work item fails; anything that repeatedly fails to process surfaces in one durable report instead of disappearing, so nothing he asked for is lost

## Cost of inaction
Inbound Telegram requests remain invisible to the coordinator and are lost whenever a session ends or processing hiccups, which is the exact failure the PM agent exists to prevent

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] pm ingest --source telegram reads tg replies user --json and records every inbound message as an intake:unprocessed ledger entry immediately, deduped by Telegram message id, before any processing
- [ ] Processing an unprocessed intake into a WorkItem is retried a bounded number of times; on exhaustion the intake moves to intake:deadletter with the failure reason, durably recorded in the event log and surfaced by pm dlq
- [ ] pm dlq lists the intake ledger (unprocessed / processed / deadletter) with a JSON mode, and the whole flow is replay-deterministic and passes ruff plus the pytest suite

title: pm-cli: Milestone 4 — dependency edges and reminders
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The M1 to M3 milestones (see [research 255](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/docs/research/255-pm-agent-research.md)) ingest and track work items independently, but the coordinator cannot flag stuck or unblocked work without modelling the relationships between items and the reminders they imply

Alex gets told when a blocked task is now free to proceed, when something has been sitting untouched too long, when two tickets duplicate each other, and when work is tangled in a dependency cycle, so nothing stalls silently or gets worked on twice

## Cost of inaction
Work items stay isolated dots with no notion of what blocks what, so the PM agent cannot nudge stuck or unblocked work and the queue cannot surface the dependency problems the design exists to catch

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] pm reminders computes reminder triggers purely from the projection plus a clock: a blocker or waited-for item reaching a terminal state, an expired timer, an active item with no progress past its SLA, a redundant duplicate or superseded item still open, and a dependency cycle

title: pm-cli: Milestone 5 — evidence reconcilers for PR and CI plus rig health, stopping before the deploy and ship-audit forks
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The M1 to M4 milestones (see [research 255](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/docs/research/255-pm-agent-research.md)) capture and relate work but only advance state on manual input; the design requires terminal-facing states to move only on evidence the PM agent cannot forge, and flags that rig status config skew must be a first-class health state

Alex sees a work item move forward automatically when its PR CI actually goes green, and never sees the PM agent claim progress it cannot prove; a broken rig config surfaces as a named drift status instead of a silent reconcile failure

## Cost of inaction
State only advances by hand, so the queue drifts from reality, and the PM agent could mark work delivered without unforgeable proof, defeating the whole point of evidence-gated states

body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The M1 to M5 milestones (see [research 255](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/docs/research/255-pm-agent-research.md)) track work and evidence but have no notion of which executor should run what; the design requires an executor ledger and risk and privacy aware routing, while being explicit that the ecosystem has invocation stats not spend data, so v1 guards quota and limits rather than pretending to account cost

Work has no routing guidance, so long tasks get started on near-limit harnesses and stall, and sensitive local-only work risks being pointed at remote models with no warning

- [ ] pm executors shows an executor ledger (harness, model, pane, repo, reliability, limit headroom, context pressure, active tasks) parsed from a telemetry snapshot, with a JSON mode
- [ ] pm route recommends an executor for a work item purely from the ledger and the item risk and privacy: it routes to a capability-appropriate executor, says wait when all executors lack quota headroom, and says blocked when local-only work has no local executor; it writes NO events and dispatches nothing

title: ship: gate --skip-ci behind a one-time Telegram HATCH approval (deny-by-default)
body:
## Problem
`gh ship --skip-ci` is a free self-service admin bypass: it skips the entire green-CI gate AND branch protection (admin merge), verifying nothing. An agent can set it itself. The legitimate "CI billing-blocked / infra down" case is ALREADY handled automatically on the normal (SKIP_CI=0) path (auto-detects the outage, runs the local fallback gate, does a NORMAL non-admin merge) — so `--skip-ci` is purely a blind self-authorized bypass.

## Change
Gate `--skip-ci` behind the existing shared hatch mechanism (`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_<HOOK_ID>` -> `agenttools_hatch_escalation` lib -> `tg-ctl ask`), mirroring the review-quorum gate (Guard-B):
- New env `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_SKIP_CI="<justification>"`, deny-by-default, bare `1` rejected, authority resolved from `resolve_home()` (never repo/cwd).
- New helper `ci/ship/skip_ci_hatch.py` (mirrors `review_quorum_hatch.py`: `python3 -I`, fixed-path lib import, APPROVED sentinel fail-closed). Dry-run previews send no Telegram round-trip but still enforce deny-by-default.
- The SKIP_CI=0 billing-outage auto-fallback is untouched.

## Acceptance
- `--skip-ci` without an approved hatch is DENIED before any merge.
- Blank / bare `1` justification is rejected without contacting tg-ctl.
- A live-approved hatch proceeds and audits `skipci:bypass:approved`.
- Billing-outage auto-fallback (SKIP_CI=0) still merges non-admin.

## Remaining
~42 existing `tests/test_ship.py` cases use `--skip-ci` as a shortcut to skip CI mocking; they must migrate to a green-CI mock (they cannot inject a fake tg-ctl in a subprocess by design). New hatch behavior is covered by 7 new tests (all green).
