comments.body: Also in this expansion-bypass class (codex quorum review): **unquoted brace/glob expansion** in a graphql query value. `gh api graphql -f query=mutation\{{noop,merge}PullRequest...\}` (zsh brace-expands `{noop,merge}` → `mergePullRequest`) and `query=*` (glob → a PR-controlled filename) are not caught by the literal `_MERGE_MUTATION` scan. title: opencode hook bridge skipped: plugin.js source became a self-referential symlink (agent-tools ships it fine)
body:
## Symptom

`rig apply` prints:

```
hook_bridge: skipped — /Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools/lib/opencode_hook_bridge is incomplete
in this agent-tools checkout (missing plugin.js; update agent-tools to a version that ships
the runnable dispatcher)
```

so the opencode hook bridge is never provisioned.

## What the investigation actually found (the "missing plugin.js" framing is misleading)

agent-tools **does** ship the runnable dispatcher. On `main`:

```
$ git ls-tree HEAD lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js
100644 blob 0679da4c...  lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js      # tracked regular file, 104 lines
$ git log --oneline -1 -- lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js
ff541e5 feat(hooks): add opencode hook bridge (#230)
```

The file is present, tracked, and complete in the repo. The problem is **on-disk
corruption of the source checkout**: on the reporting machine
`lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js` is now a **self-referential symlink** pointing to
itself:

```
$ readlink plugin.js
/Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools/lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js   # -> itself
$ test -e plugin.js && echo ok || echo BROKEN
BROKEN            # stat: "Too many levels of symbolic links"
$ git status --short lib/opencode_hook_bridge/
 T lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js                            # typechange: regfile -> symlink
```

There is a `plugin.js.rig-bak-20260715-102434` right next to it (104 lines, the real
dispatcher content) — i.e. **`rig apply` itself backed up the real file on 2026-07-15 and
replaced it with a circular symlink**, most likely a link/provision action whose source and
target resolved to the same path (`ln -s plugin.js plugin.js` in place). rig's scanner then
does a `test -e plugin.js`, which fails on the broken link, and reports the source as
"incomplete / missing plugin.js" — so it self-skips every subsequent apply.

So this is really two bugs; the agent-tools-side ask is the smaller one:

- **rig-cli (root cause, tracked separately):** a provisioning/link action created a
  `source == target` self-referential symlink in the agent-tools *source* checkout, then the
  scanner treats the broken link as a missing file. rig should never write into / symlink
  the source checkout onto itself, and the "incomplete" detection should distinguish a
  *broken symlink* from a *missing file*.

- **agent-tools (this issue):** make `lib/opencode_hook_bridge/` robust to this class —
  e.g. a `check`/self-test that verifies `plugin.js` resolves to real content, and/or docs
  noting the dispatcher must be a regular file. Confirmed present: the path exists and the
  dispatcher IS shipped (commit #230); nothing is missing from the repo itself.

## Immediate remediation on the affected machine (not done — investigation was read-only)

Restore the file from the backup / git:

```
cd /Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools
git checkout -- lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js   # or: cp plugin.js.rig-bak-20260715-102434 plugin.js
rm lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js.rig-bak-20260715-102434
```

## Acceptance

- Root cause of the self-referential symlink identified and prevented (rig side).
- `lib/opencode_hook_bridge/` grows a self-test that fails loudly if `plugin.js` does not
  resolve to the runnable dispatcher (so a corrupted source is caught, not silently skipped).

Surfaced again while working on agent-tools issues #284/#285/#289 on 2026-07-17, on

— a later timestamp (2026-07-16 19:38) than the `plugin.js.rig-bak-20260715-102434` cited

title: dep-audit.sh: script-level untrusted guard so code-executing auditors never run on PR data (defense-in-depth)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Orphaned Jul-3 wip commit db80ad2 on branch fix/129-ci-gate-bugs already implemented this (a DEP_AUDIT_UNTRUSTED=1 flag plus 494 lines of tests) but never landed: PR 131 merged an EARLIER snapshot, and main then evolved dep-audit.sh along a different path (req_file_classify) that guards ONLY python. cargo/go/pnpm/yarn have NO script-level untrusted guard in main today. Ref: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/131 and local commit db80ad2.

## User impact
Today main's shipped dependency-review workflow installs only the bun toolchain, so the source-building auditors hit command-v=false and fail-closed — no active RCE. The gap is defense-in-depth: the workflow comments invite consumers to add setup-go / rustup / setup-python. The moment a consumer adds such a toolchain to audit their ecosystem, main would run it on the PR-head worktree under pull_request_target = arbitrary PR-code execution. A script-level guard makes that impossible regardless of workflow toolchain drift.

## Cost of inaction
A future consumer adds a toolchain setup step to get their ecosystem audited, silently reopening pwn-request RCE under the privileged trigger, with no test catching it. The already-written guard and tests rot on an orphaned branch.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Under pull_request_target (untrusted PR head), dep-audit.sh must NEVER invoke an auditor that can execute repo-controlled code (govulncheck, resolving pip-audit, cargo audit alias, pnpm .pnpmfile.cjs, yarn yarn-path) even if the toolchain is present.
- [ ] A detected-but-unauditable ecosystem fails CLOSED (non-zero exit, not a silent green); only verified data-safe auditors (npm, bun) run on untrusted data.
- [ ] A behavioral test proves each code-exec auditor is NOT invoked under the untrusted signal (planted shim marker-file must not be created), mirroring the already-written tests in the orphaned commit.

title: block-raw-pr-merge false-positives on non-gh commands containing merge-like substrings
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
The block-raw-pr-merge agent-hook scans command arguments for merge-like tokens (gh ship, block-raw-pr-merge, PR-merge phrasing) even when argv[0] is NOT gh (nor git nor any merge-capable tool). This session a plain tg "<report body>" invocation (the Telegram CLI, unrelated to git or gh) was BLOCKED purely because the report text quoted the literal strings gh ship, block-raw-pr-merge and commit hashes. Root cause direction: the guard engages on argument content of arbitrary binaries instead of gating on argv[0] being an actual merge-capable invocation. Related class to [#284](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/284) - same hook accuracy family: 284 is a fail-open bypass, this is a fail-closed false-positive.

## User impact
Any agent sending a status report, a chat message, or a commit message that references gh ship, block-raw-pr-merge, or PR merges via an unrelated binary (tg, echo, git commit dash-m) gets spuriously blocked. Reporting that mentions these tools is exactly what agents do constantly, so this recurs. Workaround used this session was to move the body into a file and pass it via cat - a papercut, not a fix.

## Cost of inaction
Agents keep hitting spurious blocks on routine status reporting whenever the text references merge or ship tooling, eroding trust in the guard and wasting turns on the cat-file workaround. Suggested fix direction (do NOT implement now): the hook should only engage when argv[0] is gh or an actual git merge / merge-capable invocation, not scan arbitrary arguments of unrelated binaries; at minimum it must never match merge-like strings that appear inside a quoted message argument of a non-gh command.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A non-gh command whose argument merely mentions merge tooling is ALLOWED, e.g. tg "text mentioning gh ship and block-raw-pr-merge and a commit hash" runs without the hook blocking it
- [ ] A real merge invocation is STILL blocked (fail closed): both gh pr merge ... and gh api graphql ... mergePullRequest(...) are rejected by the hook
- [ ] A regression test pins BOTH behaviors: the non-gh message case passes through, and the two real gh merge shapes are blocked

title: Stock CI catalog templates: secret-scan.yml missing concurrency guard, baseline wiring gap, arch-blind fallback
body:
Found 2026-07-18 while provisioning CI for an unrelated repo (pm-cli) using rig-cli's stock `ci.items` catalog templates (the same templates hyperide itself uses). Three minor, cosmetic-to-low-severity issues in the vendored `secret-scan` CI item:

1. `secret-scan.yml` triggers on both `push:["**"]` and `pull_request` with no `concurrency:` guard — causes duplicate runs on the same-repo PRs (observed empirically: 2 secret-scan runs per push, both passed — cosmetic, not a functional failure, just wasted CI minutes).
2. The vendored `ci/secret-scan/secret-scan.sh` script defaults to a full-history `gitleaks git` scan with no baseline wiring — not a problem in the current push/pull_request-only workflow usage, but would be a real gap if someone later wires this script into a different CI trigger shape (e.g. a scheduled full-repo scan).
3. Same script's binary-install fallback hardcodes `linux_x64` — arch-blind, would silently fail or install the wrong binary on non-x64 Linux runners (e.g. arm64).

**Ask:** add a `concurrency: { group: secret-scan-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` block to the template; either wire a baseline file/document the full-history-scan tradeoff explicitly; and detect runner arch for the binary-install fallback (or add an explicit unsupported-arch failure message rather than silently installing the wrong binary).

**Priority:** low/cosmetic — none of these caused an actual CI failure, just flagged so they don't quietly persist across every repo that adopts this template. If the repo requires a ticket gate for issues, satisfy it minimally.

title: orchestrator-stays-thin: false-positive block on tg heredoc-argument report idiom

title: decision-request-format hook can't see content injected via command substitution ($(cat file)/heredoc)
body:
## What
The decision-request-format pre-bash hook ([agent-hooks/decision-request-format/decision_request_format.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/decision-request-format/decision_request_format.py)) inspects only the literal shell command string (args.command) — the raw text the agent asked Bash to run — BEFORE the shell expands any command substitution. So 'tg --format html --tag decision "$(cat message.html)"' gets checked against the literal text '$(cat message.html)', never the actual expanded file content, even when that file contains a fully compliant escalation body (context, a pros/cons options table, and a recommendation) per the decision-request-discipline skill. The hook then (correctly, given what it can see) rejects it as a bare question with none of the required escalation structure. This affects ANY caller who assembles a decision-request body in a file or variable and injects it via command substitution, backticks, or a heredoc, rather than pasting the entire body literally into the Bash command argument. Root cause confirmed by reading the hook source on 2026-07-19 and worked around that day by re-sending with the body pasted literally into tg's argv instead of via the file-substitution form. Full root-cause writeup already recorded in memory at /Users/ultra/.claude/projects/-Users-ultra/memory/tg-decision-gate-command-substitution-blindspot.md. This finding may also explain (not necessarily fully resolve) an earlier, separate open question logged in /Users/ultra/.claude/projects/-Users-ultra-work-hyperide/memory/reference-decision-tag-gate-misfires-use-answer-tag-fallback.md, which speculated the gate's parser might be too strict or buggy without identifying a root cause — whoever picks up this ticket should check that memory file too and update or remove it once this is genuinely fixed. NOTE: this is a separate, distinct bug from the sibling ticket at https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/307 (orchestrator-stays-thin false-positive block on the tg heredoc-argument report idiom, still open) — that ticket is about a different hook, orchestrator-stays-thin, which blanket-blocks any heredoc regardless of content; this ticket is about decision-request-format being structurally unable to see into a substitution at all. Do not conflate the two, though a reviewer fixing one will likely want context on the other.

## Why (motivation)
The hook exists to enforce the decision-request-discipline escalation format on every gated tg send, but it only ever inspects the pre-expansion shell text (args.command), so it structurally cannot validate — and will always wrongly reject — a compliant message assembled via command substitution, backticks, or a heredoc rather than pasted literally into argv. This is a structural blind spot in the hook's design, not a one-off parser glitch, and it was confirmed by reading the hook source end to end.

## User impact
Every future decision-request sent via the natural file-substitution or heredoc idiom for building a long multi-line HTML report will falsely trip this gate as a bare question with none of the required escalation structure, even though the real content is fully compliant. This forces the caller to either rediscover this same root cause each time (as happened on 2026-07-19) or reach for the RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_DECISION_REQUEST_FORMAT bypass — which the existing memory record explicitly flags as the WRONG workaround for this specific failure mode, since that hatch is meant for genuine judgement-call overrides of a correctly-functioning gate, not for routing around a caller-visible parser blind spot.

## Cost of inaction
The gate keeps silently misfiring on well-formed decision-requests sent through the file-substitution or heredoc idiom, wasting agent time re-deriving the same root cause repeatedly, and pushes agents toward either degrading message content, switching to a non-gated tag as a workaround, or invoking the RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_DECISION_REQUEST_FORMAT escape hatch inappropriately — eroding trust in the gate and the discipline it's meant to enforce.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A tg call tagged decision whose message body is passed via a file-substitution idiom (equivalent to "$(cat file.html)"), where the file contains a fully compliant escalation body (context, a pros/cons options table, and a recommendation), is ALLOWED by the hook (silent exit 0), not blocked as a bare question — demonstrated by an automated test that constructs this exact command shape and asserts the hook's decision is allow.
- [ ] A genuinely non-compliant message (no table, no real context, options, or recommendation content) is STILL blocked as bare, regardless of whether it is passed literally in argv or via the file-substitution idiom or a heredoc — demonstrated by a test covering both delivery forms of the same non-compliant body.
- [ ] If making the hook see real shell-expanded content is genuinely infeasible from a pre-exec hook (it only ever receives args.command pre-expansion), then instead of silently mis-rejecting, the hook's own block message and its README document this as a hard limitation and explicitly instruct callers to paste the body literally into argv rather than via command substitution — so the failure mode is self-explanatory instead of requiring root-cause rediscovery.

title: ship.sh: local test-runner auto-detection only checks repo root, fails for monorepo/subdirectory test layouts
body:
## What
[_local_test_runner() in ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh#L486-L527) is the CI-outage fallback gate for 'gh ship'. It only checks the git repo root for test-runner marker files (rig.yaml+dev CLI, pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml). Confirmed for [hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e) (ext-test-projects): its real tests live under `e2e/package.json`, not the repo root, so the detector always returns 'no recognized test runner found' and blocks a legitimate CI-outage merge even when local tests genuinely pass. This creates real pressure to use SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD -- an eval'd, documented test-only override explicitly commented 'never set in production' -- as if it were a legitimate per-repo 'where my tests live' config knob, which defeats the gate's own audit/safety design. This happened at least once tonight ([PR #56](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e/pull/56), suspected) and was correctly refused once ([PR #86](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e/pull/86)) after being mistakenly suggested.

## Why (motivation)
SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD's test-only boundary keeps getting pressured/violated because the legitimate detection path doesn't work for monorepo-style repos where tests live in a subdirectory rather than the root; this is a real tooling gap, not agent misuse in isolation.

## User impact
Every ext-test-projects pull request that hits a CI outage (billing block or genuine outage) currently either gets stuck waiting for CI to recover, or tempts an agent into an unaudited eval-based bypass to get a real merge through.

## Cost of inaction
Agents keep being pressured toward -- or actually using -- an unaudited eval-based override to merge PRs during CI outages, undermining the entire safety purpose of the local-fallback gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The auto-detector also checks known subdirectory conventions (e.g. an `e2e/`, `test/`, or `tests/` directory with its own package.json/pyproject.toml/Cargo.toml), OR supports a legitimate AUDITED per-repo config (not an eval'd env var) declaring where tests live
- [ ] Repos like ext-test-projects get real auto-detection (or a recorded, auditable per-repo declaration) without ever needing SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD
- [ ] SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD's documented boundary ('test-only, never set in production') is preserved -- no new eval-based escape hatch is introduced as the fix
- [ ] The leftover-marker grep in the local-fallback gate allowlists TODO/FIXME/XXX comments that cite a real ticket reference in parentheses (e.g. TODO(HYP-1003):, FIXME(JIRA-123):) -- these are legitimate forward-looking notes tracked elsewhere, not debug litter, and must not block a merge (discovered via ext-test-projects PR #124)

title: orchestrator-stays-thin heredoc carve-out: cross-file/interop follow-ups (deferred from issue 307)
body: ## What During the security-hardening review of the heredoc carve-out in agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py (tracked in issue 307), multiple review rounds surfaced cross-file and interop concerns that are out of scope for issue 307 itself (which only touches that one file's own classification logic) but should not be silently dropped: (1) the sibling agent-hook no-shell-file-edit (file agent-hooks/no-shell-file-edit/no_shell_file_edit.py) has its own, separate heredoc-detection logic that may misjudge a heredoc body the same as a live command-substitution heredoc even when it is really just literal report text wrapped by the new carve-out -- the two hooks' parsers should be cross-checked for consistency so a command allowed by one is not wrongly blocked by the other. (2) the file lib/opencode_hook_bridge/dispatch.py applies shlex.join() to the argv list [zsh, -lc, payload], which can hide heredoc syntax inside quoting before it ever reaches the classifier, unlike the file lib/codex_hook_bridge/dispatch.py which already extracts shell -c payloads correctly -- the OpenCode bridge should reuse that normalization. (3) the accepted same-line 'EOF)' heredoc-terminator form (implemented in orchestrator_stays_thin.py's _find_heredoc_terminator_end function) was verified against real bash but zsh -n rejects it as invalid syntax -- since the Codex bridge documents zsh support, the carve-out's accepted forms should be verified against zsh too, or explicitly scoped to bash-only with that documented. ## Why (motivation) These were found via multi-round adversarial AI review (Opus and Codex) while implementing the issue-307 heredoc carve-out. They are real, but each touches a different file or hook with its own parsing logic and test surface, so fixing them inside the already-large issue-307 diff would blur that ticket's scope and make the diff harder to review. Per this repo's own dead-code/deferred-findings discipline, a real finding must be tracked, not silently dropped. ## User impact Without these follow-ups: (1) an orchestrator report using the new heredoc idiom could still get wrongly blocked by the sibling no-shell-file-edit hook even though orchestrator-stays-thin now allows it, confusing whoever hits the false block; (2) an agent running under the OpenCode harness could have a genuinely dangerous heredoc-to-file command slip past classification because the bridge's shlex.join() hid it, a real security gap in a different code path than issue 307 patched; (3) a report crafted with the same-line 'EOF)' terminator could work under bash but silently fail or misbehave under zsh, a portability surprise for whichever shell an agent's harness actually invokes. ## Cost of inaction The three gaps stay live: false blocks from the sibling hook keep confusing agents, the OpenCode bridge's heredoc-hiding bypass remains an unpatched security gap in a separate code path, and the zsh-compatibility question for the new carve-out stays unverified indefinitely. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] no-shell-file-edit and orchestrator-stays-thin are run against the same corpus of report-body-shaped commands (quotes, parens, backticks, sed-i-lookalike text) and neither wrongly blocks what the other allows - [ ] lib/opencode_hook_bridge/dispatch.py extracts the real shell -c payload before classification, matching lib/codex_hook_bridge/dispatch.py's approach, with a regression test covering a heredoc-shaped OpenCode argv event - [ ] the orchestrator-stays-thin heredoc carve-out's accepted syntax forms (including the same-line 'EOF)' terminator) are verified against zsh -n, and either zsh support is confirmed or the carve-out's docs and descriptor explicitly scope it to bash - [ ] enforce-timeout-on-bash's needs_timeout() raw-scans the full command text with no quote/heredoc awareness, so a literal tg report body merely containing words like npm/test/build/pytest (e.g. "npm test passed") can trip its HANGABLE/HANGABLE_SUB regexes and produce an unwanted timeout warning (or a hard block under ENFORCE_TIMEOUT_STRICT=1) even though the report is inert text, not a real invocation of those tools -- add heredoc/quote-aware scanning (or reuse orchestrator-stays-thin's masking) so literal report content in a tg heredoc body never triggers this warning - [ ] tg-cli's own CLI argument parser (the tg binary in the tg-cli repo) separates option/feature-flag parsing from message-text positional arguments via an explicit end-of-options contract (e.g. a literal '--' separator, or only scanning argv positions before the message argument) so a single quoted message argument whose CONTENT happens to look like a flag (--help, --no-feature X, --file path) is never reinterpreted as an option -- orchestrator-stays-thin's heredoc carve-out (agent-tools#307) added a narrow, cheap mitigation (reject collapsing when a heredoc body contains a dash-prefixed line) but that only covers commands going through this one hook's heredoc carve-out, not tg-cli's own argv handling in general or any other caller - [ ] orchestrator-stays-thin's heredoc quote/depth mask (_mask_at_top_level / _mask_step) becomes heredoc-body-aware -- treating a <<'DELIM'...DELIM span as a fully opaque, un-tracked block of text before quote/comment/depth tracking runs on it -- to close the known, tested, safe-direction-only residual where a stray unmatched quote character inside an earlier heredoc's own body can over-block a later, otherwise legitimate sibling heredoc in the same command (see test_stray_quote_in_earlier_heredoc_body_can_over_block_later_sibling_documented_bias in tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py); this is purely a false-block quality issue, never a security laundering bug, but was deferred from agent-tools#307 as a larger structural change - [ ] orchestrator-stays-thin's heredoc carve-out (agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py) currently re-implements shell nesting/segment-boundary logic in three places with different fidelity: _mask_at_top_level/_mask_step (a correct per-level stack), _scan_segment_signals (its own simpler, non-stacked depth recount plus a hand-duplicated copy of _split_chain's operator set), and _split_chain itself (the real splitter used downstream) -- consolidate _scan_segment_signals to consume the stack state _mask_at_top_level already computes, and derive its segment-boundary operator set from _split_chain's rather than hand-maintaining a second copy, so there is one source of truth for depth/boundaries instead of three that must be kept in sync by convention (flagged across agent-tools#307 review rounds 9-11 by the architect reviewer; each individual finding was fixed, but the underlying three-parsers-must-agree structure was deliberately left as a larger, separate refactor rather than folded into an already-large security-fix diff) - [ ] the pin-primary-worktree agent-hook (agent-hooks/pin-primary-worktree/pin_primary_worktree.py) explicitly documents its own chain-splitter as mirroring orchestrator-stays-thin's _split_chain, but it was NOT updated alongside the double-quote/unquoted/ANSI-C escape-awareness and backslash-parity fixes made to _split_chain in issue 307 -- commands like echo "a\""; git checkout feat/x or echo $'a\''; git checkout feat/x still read as one apparent echo segment in pin-primary-worktree, so its own guard misses the real trailing git checkout; port the corrected, parity-aware splitter (or centralize it into a shared helper both hooks import) and add matching regression tests in tests/test_pin_primary_worktree.py - [ ] the no-long-inline-process and subagent-no-bg-longproc agent-hooks (agent-hooks/no-long-inline-process/no_long_inline_process.py and agent-hooks/subagent-no-bg-longproc/subagent_no_bg_longproc.py) each maintain their own wrapper-stripping table that, like orchestrator-stays-thin's did before issue 307's fix, has no operand-taking flags registered for GNU time's -f/--format and -o/--output -- so /usr/bin/time -f review diff bypasses the inline-review guard in the first hook, and the same command with a trailing & bypasses the background-process guard in the second, by the wrapper stripper reading the wrong token as the wrapped command; add the same per-wrapper operand table fix to both, ideally sharing one table across all three hooks rather than three independently-maintained copies, plus regression tests for -f/--format and -o/--output in each - [ ] _split_chain and _blank_single_quoted in agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py each maintain their OWN, separately-copy-pasted implementation of the identical quote/backslash-escape-parity/ANSI-C-detection/dollar-dollar-pairing/line-continuation-removal state machine (introduced across issue 307 review rounds 12-16) -- kept in sync by hand, not by structural sharing, and the repeated rounds 13-16 bug history (a fix landing in one copy but not the other, or landing asymmetrically, most recently the length-preservation-vs-adjacency-regex conflict in the continuation-removal branch) is the demonstrated cost of that duplication; unify the two into one shared low-level scanner (e.g. a generator yielding position/quote-state/event-kind tuples) with _split_chain and _blank_single_quoted as thin consumers doing splitting and blanking respectively, so there is one source of truth instead of two independently-fallible copies ## Screenshots (none) ## Links - (none) ## Skipped gates - links: these are repo-relative file paths and an in-repo issue number (#307), not external references needing hyperlinks

title: Adversarial review loops need an explicit scope boundary — new out-of-scope findings should become separate tickets, not more rounds on the same PR
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
A subagent fixing issue [#307](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/307) (a narrow heredoc-whitelist bug in orchestrator-stays-thin — tg was already whitelisted, but a blanket 'any heredoc anywhere = block' check fired before the whitelist check mattered) went through 17 rounds of review diff adversarial review and produced a ~2800-line diff on PR [#311](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/311), when the actual necessary fix was ~50-60 lines (a regex recognizing one narrow, provably-safe heredoc shape, stripped before the blanket check runs). Each round's finding was real (independently verified against actual repro strings), but the subagent kept fixing every newly-discovered, unrelated adversarial finding in the SAME PR instead of filing a separate ticket once the original ticket's own acceptance criteria were met. This is a process gap, not a one-off mistake — any future narrow fix in a repo that mandates adversarial review before commit is at risk of the same unbounded scope growth. Follow-up issue [#310](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/310) already captured the leftover out-of-scope items, but only after 17 rounds — this ticket is about the process rule that should have stopped it much earlier.

## User impact
When someone asks an agent for a small, narrow code fix, they currently risk getting back a sprawling, thousand-plus-line diff instead of the small fix they asked for, because the review process has no rule telling the agent to stop expanding scope once the original ask is satisfied. That means a longer wait, a much harder pull request for the person to read and approve, and wasted effort on changes nobody requested in that ticket.

## Cost of inaction
The same unbounded scope growth will recur on the next narrow fix in any repo that mandates adversarial review before commit, wasting tokens/time and producing oversized, hard-to-review diffs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The ai-review-before-commit and/or adversarial-verification skill docs (or this repo's AGENTS.md) gain an explicit rule: once a PR's own ticket's acceptance criteria are met, a review round that surfaces a NEW, unrelated finding should result in a separate ticket, not another round on the same PR — unless the finding is a direct regression risk introduced by the PR's own change.
- [ ] The docs give concrete guidance/heuristic for 'when to stop' (e.g. a round-count or diff-size threshold, or 'if the new finding requires touching a different code path/behavior than the original ticket's own diff, ticket it separately') so a future agent has an actual rule to apply rather than reasoning it out fresh each time.

title: Live-checkout personal CLIs (tg-cli, task-cli, pm-cli, etc.) go stale between sessions, causing phantom 'uncommitted work' false alarms
body:
Observed 2026-07-20: an agent investigating uncommitted changes on tg-cli's live `main` checkout (the checkout IS the running binary, per the single-file-live-symlink-cli pattern) found the diff was byte-identical to an already-merged PR (#195) — local main was simply 11 commits behind origin/main, never pulled since an earlier session. No actual work was at risk, but it cost a full investigation cycle to confirm that.

Ask: for repos following the live-checkout personal-CLI pattern, consider a lightweight session-start habit or hook that runs `git pull --ff-only` on `main` before any work begins (safe — fast-forward only, refuses if local has diverged/has uncommitted changes, so it can't clobber real in-progress work). This would prevent this class of "phantom uncommitted work" investigation from recurring across tg-cli/task-cli/pm-cli/rig-cli and similar tools.

Priority: low, quality-of-life. If the repo requires a ticket gate, satisfy it minimally.

title: ship.sh leftover-marker gate false-positives on mktemp XXXXXX templates
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
gh ship <PR> (no --skip-ci) runs the local-fallback gate when CI is billing-blocked. The leftover-marker scan uses a grep pattern with no word boundary, so it matches a 3-letter leftover-marker substring inside the standard bash mktemp template suffix used throughout the codebase for safe temp file/dir naming. Confirmed false positive on [hyper-ext-e2e#137](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e/pull/137), lines like mktemp -d with a dotted-X-run template suffix.

## User impact
Blocks a fully-reviewed, fully green-tested PR ([hyper-ext-e2e#137](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e/pull/137)) from shipping via the documented no-skip-ci fallback path when GitHub Actions is billing-blocked. Forces a choice between a live one-time --skip-ci Telegram approval (a much bigger ask than warranted) or leaving a ready PR stuck.

## Cost of inaction
Every future PR that legitimately uses this mktemp template pattern will hit the same false-positive block whenever CI is down, repeatedly forcing needless --skip-ci escalations.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] grep pattern in _local_leftover_check (ci/ship/ship.sh, around line 539) no longer flags mktemp template strings as leftover markers
- [ ] a PR containing only mktemp template lines (e.g. [hyper-ext-e2e#137](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e/pull/137)) passes the local ship gate cleanly without needing --skip-ci

title: ship.sh leftover-check diff-header filter can false-negative on lines starting with ++
body:
## Summary

`_local_leftover_check` in `ci/ship/ship.sh` (found while fixing #316 / PR #317) uses a
diff-header filter that is too loose. It can produce a **false negative** — silently
missing a real leftover marker (TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX) in an added line — when that added
source line itself starts with `++`.

## Where

`ci/ship/ship.sh`, function `_local_leftover_check` (around line 531-547):

```sh
hits=$(printf '%s\n' "$diff_out" \
  | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+\+\+' \
  | grep -E '(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)' || true)
```

The `grep -vE '^\+\+\+'` step is meant to drop unified-diff file-header lines
(`+++ b/path/to/file`). But it matches ANY line starting with three literal `+`
characters — not just the file header. An added source line whose own content starts
with `++` (e.g. a pre-increment `++counter;`) becomes, after the diff's own single `+`
add-marker is prepended, a line starting with `+++`:

```
+++counter; // TODO fix this leftover
```

That line is indistinguishable from a `+++ b/file` header by the current filter, so it
gets stripped before the TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX scan ever sees it — the leftover-marker
gate passes when it should fail.

## Repro (verified locally, not against a real PR)

Hand-built unified diff, `repro2.diff`:

```
diff --git a/file.c b/file.c
index e69de29..1234567 100644
--- a/file.c
+++ b/file.c
@@ -1 +1,2 @@
 int counter = 0;
+++counter; // TODO fix this leftover
```

Running the exact pipeline from `_local_leftover_check`:

```
$ grep -E '^\+' repro2.diff
+++ b/file.c
+++counter; // TODO fix this leftover

$ grep -E '^\+' repro2.diff | grep -vE '^\+\+\+'
(empty -- both lines dropped, including the genuine TODO line)

$ grep -E '^\+' repro2.diff | grep -vE '^\+\+\+' | grep -E '(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)'
(no output -- marker MISSED)
```

Confirmed: the added line carrying `TODO` is silently dropped, so the leftover-marker
gate reports OK even though a real leftover marker was added.

## Impact

`_local_leftover_check` is one of the three local-fallback gates run by `gh ship
--skip-ci` when CI is unavailable (see `_local_ci_fallback` further down the same
file). A PR that adds a leftover marker on a line that happens to start with `++` (any
pre-increment/pre-decrement statement, or any other source construct that starts with
two `+` characters) can pass the local leftover scan undetected, right when the normal
CI-based checks are also bypassed.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the header filter on the actual unified-diff file-header shape instead of a bare
three-character prefix, e.g.:

```sh
grep -vE '^\+\+\+ (a/|b/|/dev/null)'
```

or equivalently exclude only lines matching `^\+\+\+ ` (note the required space after
the three pluses, which a source line's own `+` characters won't produce unless the
line itself begins with `++ ` with a following space — a much narrower, and accurate,
collision surface).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Construct a repro diff with an added line starting with `++` that also contains a
      real leftover marker (as above) and confirm the CURRENT filter misses it.
- [ ] Fix `_local_leftover_check`'s header filter to anchor on the full `^+++ (a|b)/`
      (or `/dev/null`) diff-header pattern instead of the bare `^\+\+\+`.
- [ ] Add a regression test/fixture diff (added line starting with `++` containing a
      marker) to whatever test harness covers `ship.sh`'s local gates, asserting the
      gate now correctly fails.
- [ ] Existing legitimate use of the filter (dropping the real `+++ b/file` header line)
      keeps working.

## Context

Found during investigation for #316 while fixing PR #317. Deliberately NOT fixed there
— scoped out as unrelated to that PR's fix. Filing as its own tracked issue per this
repo's dead-code/deferred-finding discipline.

title: ci/ship: ROOT in the CI-down local-fallback gate may point at the launcher's checkout, not the PR's head commit
body:
## What
In [ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh), ROOT is set once near the top via `ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); cd "$ROOT"` and is then used as the working directory for the entire CI-down local-fallback gate (run_local_ci_gate -> _local_test_runner "$ROOT", plus the .ship-config load via 'git show HEAD:.ship-config' and the e2e/ subdirectory auto-detect added in [PR #314](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/314)). This ROOT is the toplevel of whatever checkout ship.sh happens to be invoked from (the launcher's ambient working tree), not necessarily a checkout of the PR's actual head commit/branch. If ship.sh is invoked from a stale, unrelated, or differently-checked-out working tree while operating on a PR by number, the local fallback gate could run tests/config detection against the wrong commit's tree entirely, and the gate's PASS/FAIL result would not reflect the PR being merged.

## Why (motivation)
Raised independently by the Codex reviewer at P1 across three separate review rounds (rounds 4, 5, 6) and by Fable in rounds 5 and 6 during [PR #314](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/314) (fix(ship): local-test-runner subdir + audited config fallback). It is a pre-existing property of the entire CI-down local-fallback gate architecture (not introduced by PR #314's subdirectory/.ship-config changes), so it was explicitly flagged as out of scope for that PR and deferred to a follow-up ticket per the PR body and final commit message [b1a625bc](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/commit/b1a625bc28bfe392489dab5da232da91dacb6618).

## User impact
gh ship's CI-down local fallback is the safety net that lets a PR merge when GitHub Actions itself is unavailable, without an admin bypass. If the local gate can silently validate the wrong commit's code instead of the PR's actual head, a broken PR could pass the fallback gate and get merged as if it were verified, defeating the purpose of the CI-down safety net across every repo using ship.sh.

## Cost of inaction
The ambiguity persists as an unverified assumption baked into a correctness-critical merge gate used by every repo on ship.sh. A future invocation from a stale worktree could get a false-positive local-gate pass that ships broken code with no CI ever having run against it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Document (or fix) whether ROOT is guaranteed to be checked out to the PR's head commit at every call site of run_local_ci_gate / _local_test_runner.
- [ ] If not guaranteed: add a check that fails closed (refuses the local-gate fallback) when the working tree at ROOT is not on the PR's head commit/branch, or make the gate explicitly verify/checkout the PR head before running local tests.
- [ ] If already guaranteed by an earlier preflight check: add an inline comment at the ROOT assignment and at run_local_ci_gate's call sites recording the invariant and which earlier check enforces it.
- [ ] Add a regression test exercising the CI-down local-fallback path from a checkout not on the PR's head commit and asserting the documented behavior.

title: ci/ship: failed-rollup CI-down path is missing the foreign-repo-target guard the empty-rollup path already has
body:
## What
In [ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh), there are two CI-down code paths that both call run_local_ci_gate as a fallback when GitHub Actions appears unavailable: (1) the empty-rollup path (PR registers zero checks after the grace window), and (2) the failed-rollup path (checks registered but most/all failed, ci_appears_structurally_down). The empty-rollup path explicitly guards against a foreign --repo/GH_SHIP_REPO invocation before running the local gate: `if [ "${_FOREIGN_REPO_INVOKE:-0}" != "1" ] && _empty_rollup_is_ci_outage; then ...` — with an inline comment explaining that a foreign target must keep the hard refuse because the local gate runs against THIS checkout, not the target (referencing issue #166). The failed-rollup path's equivalent block (`if ci_appears_structurally_down "$TOTAL_CHECKS" "$FAILED"; then ... run_local_ci_gate ...`) has no such ${_FOREIGN_REPO_INVOKE} check at all — it runs the local gate unconditionally once ci_appears_structurally_down returns true, regardless of whether the invocation targets a foreign repo.

## Why (motivation)
Raised by the Codex reviewer in round 6 of [PR #314](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/314) (fix(ship): local-test-runner subdir + audited config fallback). Unrelated to that PR's subdirectory/.ship-config diff, so it was explicitly deferred to a follow-up ticket per the PR body and final commit message [b1a625bc](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/commit/b1a625bc28bfe392489dab5da232da91dacb6618).

## User impact
If the guard gap is real, invoking gh ship against a foreign repo whose CI has genuinely failed checks could run the local fallback gate against the wrong (ambient/launcher) checkout instead of refusing, producing a false PASS and merging code that was never actually validated against the target repo's real state.

## Cost of inaction
The two CI-down branches remain structurally asymmetric with no recorded justification, leaving an unverified correctness gap in a merge-safety gate used by every repo on ship.sh.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Confirm (with a repro test) whether a foreign --repo/GH_SHIP_REPO invocation can reach the failed-rollup run_local_ci_gate call without the guard the empty-rollup path enforces.
- [ ] If the guard is needed for correctness (matching the rationale documented at the empty-rollup path referencing issue #166 — the local gate validates THIS checkout, not the foreign target's actual commit), add the same _FOREIGN_REPO_INVOKE check to the failed-rollup path so both CI-down branches are symmetric.
- [ ] If investigation shows the failed-rollup path is safe without the guard for a documented reason, add an inline comment at that call site explaining why the asymmetry is intentional, so it is not re-flagged as a gap in a future review.
- [ ] Add a regression test in tests/test_ship.py covering the failed-rollup CI-down path invoked with a foreign --repo/GH_SHIP_REPO target.

title: ci/ship: local-fallback gate's test-runner detection executes before the pre-existing dirty-worktree check
body:
## What
In ci/ship/ship.sh (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh) the CI-down local-fallback gate (run_local_ci_gate calling _local_test_runner, invoked from within the CI-check block around the empty-rollup and failed-rollup branches) runs early in the script, reading committed content at HEAD (.ship-config, subdirectory auto-detect) and then executing local test commands against the actual working tree at ROOT. The pre-existing dirty-worktree check (which refuses with 'worktree has uncommitted changes' when 'git status --short' on a linked worktree is non-empty) runs much later in the script, inside the post-merge worktree cleanup loop that walks every linked worktree for the branch. Because ROOT itself can be one of those worktrees, the local-fallback gate's test execution can run against a working tree containing uncommitted local modifications that diverge from the committed HEAD content the .ship-config/detection logic reasoned about, before the script ever verifies that the tree is clean.

## Why (motivation)
Raised by the Codex reviewer in round 6 of PR #314 (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/314) (fix(ship): local-test-runner subdir + audited config fallback), described as a property of the local fallback gate's overall check ordering rather than something specific to the subdirectory/.ship-config additions in that PR. Deferred to a follow-up ticket per the PR body and final commit message b1a625bc (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/commit/b1a625bc28bfe392489dab5da232da91dacb6618).

## User impact
A developer running gh ship on a repo with local, uncommitted edits sitting on top of a genuinely CI-down PR could get an auto-merge that was actually tested against their locally-modified files, not the code that is actually committed and about to land on the main branch — the merge could pass 'clean' review even though what got shipped differs from what was reviewed.

## Cost of inaction
The ordering gap remains latent in the merge-safety gate; a future change to either the dirty check or the local-fallback gate could silently make this exploitable (or already is) without a test catching it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Trace and document the actual order of operations between the CI-down local-fallback gate's test execution and every dirty-worktree check in the script, confirming (with a test or a script trace) whether the gate can execute local test commands against a working tree with uncommitted changes.
- [ ] If it can: either move a dirty-worktree check earlier so it runs before run_local_ci_gate is invoked, or make _local_test_runner itself refuse when the working tree at ROOT is dirty, so the local test execution never diverges from what .ship-config/HEAD said it would run.
- [ ] If investigation shows this is inconsequential (e.g. an earlier check already guarantees a clean tree by this point), add an inline comment recording that invariant at the run_local_ci_gate call sites so the ordering question is not re-raised.
- [ ] Add a regression test in tests/test_ship.py that runs the CI-down local-fallback gate against a working tree with uncommitted changes and asserts the documented behavior.

title: ci/ship: invalid committed .ship-config fails OPEN instead of fails CLOSED
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
review-cli round 1 for [HYP-1100](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-1100) (Fable, architect seat) flagged that _ship_config_load's own header doc argues a rejected SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR must not silently relocate to a different suite than intended -- but invalidating the whole file and falling through to root auto-detect does exactly that, just via a different mechanism. A nonexistent dir already fails closed (return 1); an equally plausible author typo (unsafe path, corrupt bytes) fails open.

## User impact
A developer who commits a broken .ship-config by mistake (a typo'd path, or a corrupted file from a bad merge) will see their PR merge on whatever tests ship happens to auto-detect at the repo root, not the specific suite they configured -- so a merge can look verified when the test suite they actually meant to require never ran.

## Cost of inaction
The fail-open behavior stays as tested/intentional and this design question never gets a deliberate owner decision; the next incident has to be traced back to this same review finding again.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide and document whether ship should block the merge outright (fail closed) when a committed .ship-config expresses override intent but fails validation (unsafe SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR, embedded NUL byte), instead of the current fall-through to the root auto-detect heuristic.
- [ ] If fail-closed is chosen: flip the 3 currently-pinned tests in [tests/test_ship.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/tests/test_ship.py) (rejects_unsafe_dir_absolute, unsafe_dir_invalidates_whole_file, nul_byte_is_rejected) and update the precedence docs in [ci/ship/README.md](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/README.md).

title: leftover-marker scanners misparse a diff line starting with ++ as a fake +++ header
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Found while fixing [agent-tools#318](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/318) (self-referential false positive in ship.sh's CI-outage leftover-marker fallback). A hunk-aware header-parsing design was built and discarded there in favor of a simpler fix, which reverted the diff-scanning pipeline in [ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh) back to its original, pre-existing plain grep pipeline -- which still has this separate, pre-existing false-negative bug, unrelated to the self-reference fix. [ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh)'s emit_lines() has the identical header-detection pattern and is equally exposed.

## User impact
If you add code where an added line happens to start with two plus signs (common in C/C++/Rust pre-increment expressions, e.g. a line beginning with two plus signs then a variable name), and that same line also contains a leftover debugging marker you forgot to remove, both the normal pull-request check and the backup check used when CI is down will silently wave it through instead of blocking your merge -- the exact leftover marker these checks exist to catch reaches the main branch undetected.

## Cost of inaction
The false negative persists indefinitely and undetected, since nothing currently tests this diff-parsing edge case in either scanner; it will only surface if someone later notices a leftover marker that should have been caught but wasn't, at which point the root cause (a diff-format ambiguity, not obviously related to the marker's content) will take real debugging time to trace.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The [_local_leftover_check function](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh) and the [leftover-grep.sh emit_lines function](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh) both track hunk boundaries (a real diff --git line and each file's first @@ marker) so a plus-plus-plus line is only trusted as a genuine diff header there, never for a look-alike added content line inside real hunk data.
- [ ] A regression test in [tests/test_ship.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/tests/test_ship.py) builds a realistic full unified diff (diff --git/index/---/+++/@@) where an added source line itself starts with two plus signs and contains a real leftover marker, and asserts the marker is still caught (not silently dropped as if it were a header).
- [ ] The equivalent case is covered for leftover-grep.sh's own test suite, or a ticket note explains why it is exempt.

A developer opening a pull request that edits leftover-grep.sh's own detector logic or its documentation comments (which legitimately need to show example marker text) gets their unrelated, otherwise-clean pull request blocked by the untracked-marker check flagging the tool's own source code, forcing them to work around or silence the check instead of just merging their change.

The self-trigger bug remains latent in the CI-based gate and will resurface the next time someone edits leftover-grep.sh, costing that person time re-discovering and re-diagnosing a problem that has already been solved once (for ship.sh) in this same codebase.

- [ ] The [leftover-grep.sh detector](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh) applies the same bracket-expression de-literalization idiom used to fix [agent-tools#318](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/318) in [ci/ship/ship.sh](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ci/ship/ship.sh), so its own detector line and any doc comments no longer spell out any of the four leftover-marker keywords as one contiguous literal token.

title: ship.sh local-fallback gate should warn when running from a worktree for repos with known sibling-path test dependencies
body:
## What
ship.sh's local-fallback CI gate (used when GitHub Actions billing is blocked) has no awareness of whether it is running from a git worktree vs a repo's main checkout. When a repo's own test suite depends on sibling-repo relative paths (as the [hyper-ext-e2e harness](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e) does, resolving a sibling hyperide checkout), and the gate runs from a worktree, it silently reports a wall of failures (e.g. '3025 tests failed') as if it were a real regression, with no signal that the failure might be an artifact of the checkout location rather than a real code problem.

## Why (motivation)
Discovered during investigation of a gh ship 137 false-alarm e2e failure in the [hyper-ext-e2e harness](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e): its extension-installer.ts hardcodes a sibling-repo relative path that does not resolve from a worktree checkout, causing thousands of tests to fail near-instantly. ship.sh's local-fallback gate reported this as a plain wall of failures with no hint that the checkout location was the cause, wasting investigation time before the real root cause was found and tracked as [HYP-1122](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-1122/extension-installerts-sibling-path-resolution-breaks-when-e2e-harness).

## User impact
Anyone using gh ship --skip-ci from a worktree, on a repo whose tests have sibling-path dependencies, gets a scary false-alarm wall of failures indistinguishable from a real regression, and has to manually re-investigate from scratch each time instead of getting a hint toward the likely cause.

## Cost of inaction
This diagnostics gap will keep costing investigation time on every future false-alarm case of this shape, across any repo with sibling-path test dependencies run through gh ship's local fallback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The local-fallback gate detects, at minimum via a heuristic, when a large fraction of tests fail near-instantly with a consistent build/setup error, and surfaces a warning in its output suggesting the failure may be checkout-location-related rather than a real regression.
- [ ] The gate detects worktree-vs-main-checkout status (e.g. via git rev-parse --git-common-dir vs --git-dir) and includes that status in its diagnostic output when a failure wall like this occurs.

title: Auto-mode classifier blocks invocation of RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* sanctioned escalation hatches
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
During a real shipping session (2026-07-23), an agent hit a genuine external blocker: the codex:gpt-5.6-sol review model was quota-exhausted (backend returned a real usage-limit error, retry after Jul 28 2026), so a security-fix PR's review-quorum gate (3 distinct clean-pass models required) could not be satisfied -- 2 of 3 seats (opus, fable) converged clean, codex failed all 6 attempts. The repo has a sanctioned escalation path for exactly this: RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM="<justification>", documented as escalating live to the human via Telegram for approval (deny-by-default, no bare "1" accepted) -- see [ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/8291167/ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py) and [ci/ship/README.md](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/8291167/ci/ship/README.md). The agent correctly tried to invoke this sanctioned path with a real, detailed justification instead of self-authorizing a workaround. But the Claude Code auto-mode classifier blocked the hatch invocation itself, requiring a separate manual permission grant on top of the already-sanctioned escalation mechanism. This defeats the purpose of a hatch specifically designed to escalate to the human for approval -- it should not itself require a second, different approval step with no documented resolution path.

## User impact
Agents doing security-sensitive or otherwise gated work hit a dead end when they need the sanctioned escalation path, and either give up, work around it improperly, or (as happened here) require an entirely separate manual decision-request message sent outside the tool's own designed mechanism -- inconsistent and easy to get wrong under time pressure. This is not limited to the ship-review-quorum hatch: every RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* mechanism in the ecosystem (worktree-only-writes, pin-primary-worktree, orchestrator-stays-thin, decision-request-format, skills-read-gate, background-subagent-gate) likely has the same gap, silently forcing every legitimate escalation into an ad-hoc manual workaround instead of the designed flow.

## Cost of inaction
This specific incident required a full manual decision-request drafted and sent via tg instead of the lightweight hatch flow -- a working but heavier, more error-prone path than the tool intended. Future agents hitting any of the other hatch gates will likely hit the same wall, and the sanctioned-escalation design pattern effectively does not work as designed across the ecosystem.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Either (a) the Claude Code auto-mode classifier treats setting or reading a RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* env var (SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM, WORKTREE_ONLY_WRITES, PIN_PRIMARY_WORKTREE, ORCHESTRATOR_STAYS_THIN, DECISION_REQUEST_FORMAT, SKILLS_READ_GATE, BACKGROUND_SUBAGENT_GATE, and any others found via a repo grep) as inherently safe and auto approved, since invoking a hatch only sends a request for human approval via tg and cannot itself bypass anything -- the real bypass only happens if and when the human approves it
- [ ] Or (b), if there is a legitimate reason the classifier must still gate the hatch-invocation step itself, that reasoning AND a documented resolution path (what an agent should concretely do when even the hatch-request attempt is blocked) is written down somewhere findable, such as [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/8291167/AGENTS.md) or the relevant hook or ci README
- [ ] A regression test or documented manual-verification note proves the chosen resolution actually works end to end -- a hatch invocation reaches tg approval without a second manual permission grant, or the documented fallback is exercised and works

title: block-raw-pr-merge: consolidate clustered short-flag classification into one shared state machine
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
[PR #335](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/335) (ticket [#333](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/333)) fixed a real fail-open bypass where an unrecognized clustered short-flag char (e.g. a hypothetical future gh boolean flag) was left unexpanded and invisible to every downstream merge detector in block_raw_pr_merge.py. The fix works and is fully tested, but a review (Fable, repeated across 2 rounds) flagged that it adds a SECOND parallel parser that must stay in lockstep with the expander's own state machine -- two independently-maintained walks over the same token grammar is exactly the kind of structural risk that caused the original bug (two things disagreeing about the same token).

## User impact
If the two mirrored walks (expander vs unprovable-cluster detector) are ever edited independently and drift apart, the safe direction is an over-block (a legitimate gh api call refused) -- annoying but not a security bypass, since a mismatch strictly enlarges the block set rather than shrinking it, given _gh_api_is_merge ORs the two checks. But it is real friction: a future contributor touching one of the two mirrors without touching the other could break a working command silently, and the current design requires reading both implementations plus their docstrings to know they must move together.

## Cost of inaction
No user-visible bug ships if this is deferred (the current code is a completely correct fail-closed fix, and this is a maintainability/robustness suggestion, not a demonstrated correctness gap). But the module keeps accreting review-finding docstrings explaining an asymmetry that would not need explaining if unprovability were structural to the expander instead of inferred from the outside at one call site (_gh_api_is_merge).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A single walk both expands a gh-api clustered short-flag token AND reports unprovability, replacing the current two independently-maintained mirrors: [_expand_clustered_short_flag/_expand_clustered_gh_api_flags](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/block-raw-pr-merge/block_raw_pr_merge.py) vs [_short_flag_cluster_is_unprovable/_gh_api_flags_contain_unprovable_cluster](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/block-raw-pr-merge/block_raw_pr_merge.py)
- [ ] Existing test coverage for both the expansion behavior and the unprovable-cluster fail-closed behavior (added in [PR #335](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/335)) continues to pass unmodified in intent (same observable allow/block outcomes)

title: ship.sh checklist gate has no override for a billing-block-unsatisfiable CI-passes checkbox
body:
## What
ship.sh's local PR-checklist gate (function _local_pr_checklist_check, ship.sh lines around 930-947) hard-blocks gh ship whenever the PR body has ANY unchecked dash-bracket-space line, with no override flag -- unlike the no-screenshot-ok, no-version-bump-ok, and no-review-dwell-ok escape hatches that exist for other gates. This collides with ship.sh's own billing-block auto-fallback: when GitHub CI is billing-blocked, a bare gh ship call auto-detects the outage and runs local checks (typecheck, lint, tests, build) as a substitute, merging normally if they pass -- verified working end-to-end today for [PR #688](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas/pull/688) ([HYP-1140](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-1140)) in [hyperide/hyper-saas](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas). But if that PR's body contains a checklist item worded like 'CI passes.' (a real, common item under this repo's ticket-documentation-standard convention), that box is honestly never checkable while CI is billing-blocked: it is not a lie to leave it unchecked, CI genuinely is not passing, it is blocked. There is no way to satisfy that specific checkbox without either waiting for real CI (defeating the point of the local-checks fallback) or someone manually rewording or removing that one checklist line from the PR body each time (fragile, easy to forget, and itself a workaround). Net effect: every billing-blocked PR whose body includes a literal CI-passes-style checkbox hits this same permanent block regardless of how clean the local-checks fallback result is, defeating the autonomous-merge promise for exactly the scenario it is designed to handle.

## Why (motivation)
Found today while shipping [PR #688](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas/pull/688) ([HYP-1140](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-1140)) in [hyperide/hyper-saas](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas). ship.sh correctly auto-detected the GitHub Actions billing block and ran the local-checks fallback, which passed. But gh ship still refused to merge with: local gate: FAILED -- PR has 2 unchecked checklist item(s). One of those two items was a standard 'CI passes.' acceptance criterion from this repo's ticket-documentation-standard template -- a box that cannot be honestly checked while CI is billing-blocked, since CI is in fact not passing (it is blocked), yet the local-checks substitute already proved the change is safe to merge.

## User impact
Anyone shipping a PR during a GitHub Actions billing block, using this repo's standard PR or ticket template (which includes a CI-passes style checkbox), hits a merge that never actually completes autonomously -- they must either wait for real CI to come back (which may be hours or days, and defeats the purpose of the local-checks fallback entirely) or manually edit the already-drafted PR body to remove or reword that one line before retrying gh ship. This silently reintroduces a manual step in exactly the scenario the local-checks fallback exists to make hands-off, and is easy to forget, producing repeated confusion about why a demonstrably clean, locally-verified PR still will not ship.

## Cost of inaction
Every future billing-blocked PR that uses the standard ticket-documentation-standard checklist template will hit this identical permanent block, regardless of how clean its local-checks fallback result is. Each occurrence costs the time to notice the block, look up ship.sh's checklist logic, and manually edit the PR body -- work that has to be redone by whoever ships the next affected PR, because there is no override flag and no gate-side exception recorded anywhere. The billing-block never-manually-intervene guarantee documented for this exact scenario silently does not hold for any PR using the standard template.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A decision is made and documented on where the fix belongs: (a) ship.sh's checklist gate special-cases a CI-passing-worded item so it is treated as satisfied automatically when the local-checks fallback already ran and passed, OR (b) the repo's standard ticket-documentation-standard acceptance-criterion wording for CI passes is changed to something that stays truthfully checkable during a confirmed billing-block (for example: CI passes, or ship's local-checks fallback ran clean during a confirmed billing-block), OR (c) the current manual-reword behavior is explicitly kept as the accepted process, with the billing-block fully-autonomous-never-manual claim corrected to note this exception.
- [ ] Whichever direction is chosen is implemented (gate change, template wording change, or explicit documented exception) and demonstrated: a billing-blocked PR using the repo's standard checklist template completes gh ship end to end (local-checks fallback plus merge) without a human or agent manually editing the PR body's checklist wording first, while a genuinely unrelated unchecked checklist item still blocks the merge as before.

title: model-freshness: bump proposal rewrites only id:, leaves :latest alias + fallback_chain dangling
body:
Found during review of #342 (pre-existing since the checker landed in #10, affects every provider with a `:latest` alias — filing instead of scope-creeping that PR).

## Problem
`rewrite_manifest_text` (lib/checker/model_freshness.py) swaps only the first `id: <current_id>` line when building a bump-proposal PR. Dependent references are not updated:

- the provider's `<provider>:latest` alias keeps pointing at the removed id (e.g. a glm-5.2 → glm-5.3 proposal leaves `zai:latest: glm-5.2` dangling);
- `fallback_chain:` entries naming the old id (e.g. `oc:GLM-5.2`) go stale.

The resulting manifest fails `--validate` (alias target missing), so the first auto-proposal for any aliased provider produces a broken PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Proposal rewrite atomically repoints the provider's `:latest` alias and any `fallback_chain` entries that reference the old id
- [ ] Rewritten manifest is validated before the proposal PR is committed/pushed
- [ ] Regression test: a bump proposal on the real manifest (e.g. k3 → hypothetical k4) yields a manifest that passes `--validate`

## Impact
The daily freshness cron's output is propose-never-merge, so nothing breaks silently — but every proposal PR for an aliased provider needs manual repair today.

title: ci templates: CodeQL suppression markers emitted in a form the self-gate cannot recognize
body:
## What

`ci/dependency-review/workflow.yml` (line 77, 100) and `ci/leftover-grep/workflow.yml` (line 48, 82) emit the CodeQL suppression marker as a bare `# codeql[<rule-id>]` at the TOP of the justification comment block, several lines above the flagged step.

## Why it breaks

Consumer repos' CodeQL self-gate (`codeql.yml` `is_source_suppressed()`) greps for the literal `// codeql[<rule-id>]` on the flagged line OR the line directly above it. The template output satisfies neither:

1. bare `# codeql[...]` lacks the `// ` substring the gate greps for (`grep -qF '// codeql[<id>]'`);
2. the marker sits at the top of a 5-6 line justification block, not directly above the flagged `- name:` step.

Observed downstream (hyperide/hyper-saas PR #701, after `rig apply commit --only ci`): CodeQL Self-Gate (actions) FAILED with 4 gated findings — `actions/untrusted-checkout/medium` x2 + `actions/cache-poisoning/poisonable-step` x2 — on exactly the four steps the markers were meant to suppress.

## Fix

Emit the marker as the LAST comment line directly above the flagged step, in the gate-recognized form:

```yaml
      # Justified: ...
      # // codeql[actions/untrusted-checkout/medium]
      - name: Fetch the PR head commit as DATA (not checked out / not executed)
```

This is the layout hyper-saas's HEAD used before the template drifted (proven: gate suppressed those findings there). Downstream workaround applied in hyperide/hyper-saas#701; until the template is fixed, every `rig apply` re-introduces the failure.

title: orchestrator-stays-thin falsely blocks read-only find+git-grep Bash chains

## What

The hook's documented contract explicitly exempts read-only inspection commands from gating; this is a false positive against that documented contract, not a new restriction being requested.

The orchestrator cannot run ordinary read-only research (locating files, searching repo content) without being wrongly blocked, forcing extra delegation hops or hatch-escalation for work that should be free.

False blocks on legitimate read-only commands keep recurring, wasting turns and eroding trust in the hook, which in turn encourages agents to route around guardrails instead of respecting them.

title: test_rig_cli_generates_if_importable crashes on SyntaxError instead of skipping
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Discovered 2026-08-06: gh ship's local-fallback path runs this best-effort cross-repo test, which imports the sibling rig-cli checkout. That checkout was mid-merge with an unresolved conflict marker left in one of its source files, producing a real Python SyntaxError on import - not an ImportError, so the except clause did not catch it.

## User impact
gh ship's local-fallback CI substitute hard-crashes instead of skipping when an unrelated sibling checkout happens to be in a broken or mid-merge state, blocking merges in agent-tools for a reason entirely outside that PR's own changes. This test is best-effort and gated by design per its own docstring - a SyntaxError should skip exactly like an ImportError does, not propagate.

## Cost of inaction
Any future sibling checkout left in a broken or conflicted state will continue to silently block unrelated agent-tools PRs via gh ship's fallback path, with a confusing crash instead of a clear skip reason.

title: Deny-by-default PreToolUse guard for git worktree remove --force / git branch -D
body:
## What
Add a new pre-bash agent-hook (sibling to block-reset-hard, same argv-parsed detection discipline and same deny-by-default + approval_cmd + RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* Telegram-hatch escalation pattern) that blocks 'git worktree remove --force'/'-f' and 'git branch -D'/'--delete --force' unless explicitly approved. Neither of the two existing worktree/branch guards (pin-primary-worktree: only gates checkout/switch on the PRIMARY worktree; worktree-only-writes: only gates Edit/Write on the default branch) intercepts a destructive worktree-remove or branch-delete, and block-reset-hard itself only covers the destructive reset and clean forms. orchestrator-stays-thin treats a 'git branch <arg>' as forfeiting its allow-list, but that is a delegation-discipline gate scoped to the ORCHESTRATOR only (agent_id-present subagents are explicitly exempt) — it does not stop a dispatched subagent, which is exactly who ran the destructive command in the incident this ticket documents.

## Why (motivation)
A subagent dispatched inside a hyperide-repo session force-removed a worktree and force-deleted its branch — a dead worktree from a PRIOR, unrelated session — deleting real uncommitted work, with no reflog safety net for uncommitted content, and with no user authorization. Its dispatch prompt said to salvage any diff first and never authorized deletion; the agent made the deletion call on its own after concluding (correctly, in outcome) the work was superseded. A safety classifier caught this, but only POST-HOC, after the deletion had already run — that classifier layer is Anthropic-side and outside agent-tools'/hyperide's control to change. What IS actionable and already owned by agent-tools is a PRE-execution PreToolUse hook, exactly the mechanism block-reset-hard already proves out for the destructive reset/clean forms — the identical failure class, just two different git subcommands that currently have zero coverage. A memory-only fix (tell every future dispatch prompt not to delete) is necessarily incomplete: it depends on every prompt author remembering to say so, and this specific prompt already DID say salvage first and STILL didn't stop the agent, because there was no technical backstop enforcing it.

## User impact
Every hyperide (and any other agent-tools-enrolled repo's) developer whose uncommitted work sits in a worktree is one confused subagent away from silent, irreversible data loss — uncommitted content has no git reflog, so a wrongly-judged this-is-dead call is unrecoverable by git alone (this specific incident was recoverable only by chance, via a session transcript containing full diffs — not a general guarantee).

## Cost of inaction
The next agent that decides a worktree looks dead and force-removes it (or force-deletes its branch) — including one working an entirely unrelated task in a shared checkout, exactly like this incident — has zero technical resistance, only whatever that agent's own dispatch prompt happened to say. Given the fleet already runs many concurrent/background subagents across shared checkouts, recurrence is a when, not an if, and the next occurrence may not have this incident's lucky transcript-based recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new pre-bash hook, sibling to [block-reset-hard](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/block-reset-hard/block_reset_hard.py), BLOCKS an unapproved worktree-remove-with-force and an unapproved branch-delete-with-force (also the long-flag spelling, wrapped forms via the same wrapper-stripping table block-reset-hard already uses for its sudo, timeout, and env wrappers, chained via shell operators or newline) — verified by a passing pytest suite mirroring [tests/test_block_reset_hard.py](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/tests/test_block_reset_hard.py), run via: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest -q on the new hook's own test file
- [ ] The safe/reversible forms are unaffected: worktree-remove WITHOUT force (git itself refuses on a dirty tree), branch-delete WITHOUT force (git itself refuses on unmerged commits), and worktree-list all pass through — verified by the same test suite plus a manual smoke test in agent-tools itself piping a JSON event for each command through the new hook script and checking its exit code is 10 for the force forms and 0 for the safe forms.
- [ ] The new hook's own README documents it exactly like [block-reset-hard's README](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/agent-hooks/block-reset-hard/README.md) (why an agent-hook, parsed-not-raw-matched, no self-service bypass, approval_cmd + RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* Telegram hatch, fail-closed on_error, known limitations) and EXPLICITLY records the decision NOT to gate on a was-this-created-by-the-current-agent-invocation mtime/naming heuristic — that approach was considered and rejected per the agent-tools operator's own recorded finding that mtime is not a reliable signal for agent/session identity — in favor of the same deny-by-default posture block-reset-hard already uses successfully for the identical failure class: irreversible working-tree destruction with no git-managed undo.
